motu: Mamoe bona nani hahinedia e rogorogova negana ai na na nihi, egu nihi ai na itadia, mamarauendia mai toutoudia bona mai revarevadia bona koremadia mo ema, hahine dekediai.
english: During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats which leaped on the flock were streaked, speckled, and grizzled.

motu: Bena egu nihi ai Dirava ena aneru ta ese e hereva henigu, eto “Iakob”. Lau nato “Lau o ina.”
english: The angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob,’ and I said, ‘Here I am.’

motu: Ma eto “A itadia, mamoe bona nani hahinedia e harogorogodiamu mamaruanedia iboudiai na mai toutoudia eiava mai revarevadia eiava koremadia: badina be Laban ena kara iboudiai oiemu ai e karamu vada na ita vaitani.
english: He said, ‘Now lift up your eyes, and behold, all the male goats which leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.

motu: Lau binai, Betele Diravana: unuseni ai oi ese boubou nadina dehoro o horolaia, bona o gwau henigu hamata. Benaini, a tore isi, ina tano amo ba raka lasi, o vara gabuna ba lou henia.”
english: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar, where you vowed a vow to me. Now arise, get out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.’”

motu: Bena Rahela bona Lea ese e haere henia, eto, Ai ahumai be dahaka tamamai ena ruma ai? Ai na dia ia dihina.
english: Rachel and Leah answered him, “Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?

motu: Ai na idau taudia na heheto ienai, ani? Badina be davamai vada e abi bona vada e hapetapetalai.
english: Aren’t we considered as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also used up our money.

motu: Taḡa idoinai Dirava ese tamamai ena amo vada e abihaia na ai emai bona natumai edia; taunabunai, Dirava ese vada e hamaoromu heḡereḡerena vada ba karaia.
english: For all the riches which God has taken away from our father are ours and our children’s. Now then, whatever God has said to you, do.”

motu: Bena Iakob ese adavana raruosi bona natuna iboudiai na kamelo ai e hahelaidia kau;
english: Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives on the camels,

motu: ena seri iboudiai bona ena kohu idoinai Padan-aram ai e habou danu e siaidia guna; bena e heḡaeḡae, Kanaan tanona bainela, tamana Isaak dekenai.
english: and he took away all his livestock, and all his possessions which he had gathered, including the livestock which he had gained in Paddan Aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.

motu: Una negana ai Laban na ena mamoe huidia iutudia ela. Bena Rahela ese tamana ena dirava laulaudia e henao;
english: Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole the teraphim + 31:19 teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. * that were her father’s.

motu: bona Iakob na e heau hehuni, Laban tau Suria se hadibaia guna.
english: Jacob deceived Laban the Syrian, in that he didn’t tell him that he was running away.

motu: Ia na ela, ena orea taudia bona ena kohu idoinai danu e laohai, sinavai e hanaia, Gilead ororodia dalana ai ela.
english: So he fled with all that he had. He rose up, passed over the River, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.

motu: Dina ihatoina ai Laban na Iakob ena heau harina e kamonai.
english: Laban was told on the third day that Jacob had fled.

motu: Bena ia ese varavarana e haboudia, dina hitu Iakob e ḡavaia, ela bona Gilead ororodia ai e ḡavaia tao.
english: He took his relatives with him, and pursued him seven days’ journey. He overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.

motu: A Dirava ese Laban tau Suria nihi ai e hahedinarai henia, eto, Iakob basio hereva henia, hereva namona eiava hereva dikana.
english: God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.”

motu: Bena Laban ese Iakob e lasia tao. Iakob na ororo ai vada e taruha; bena Laban mai varavarana ida danu Gilead ororodia ai e taruha.
english: Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.

motu: Bena Laban ese Iakob e gwau henia, eto, Badina be dahaka o heau hehuni, natugu hahinedia danu abimauri hahinedia na heheto o heaulaidia?
english: Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done, that you have deceived me, and carried away my daughters like captives of the sword?

motu: Dahaka dainai o heau hehuni, so hadibagu? Boma hadibagu, bena bama kahumu nege mai moale karadia bona mai moale anedia ida, oibe, mai gaba reḡedia bona mai gitara reḡedia ida.
english: Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn’t tell me, that I might have sent you away with mirth and with songs, with tambourine and with harp;

motu: A oi ese o laogu ahu, natugu asina harahudia. Vada o kara kava.
english: and didn’t allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters? Now you have done foolishly.

motu: Harihari, lau na mai siahugu bama hadikamu; ḡau tamona, tamamu ena Dirava ese boi hanuaboi e hahedinarai henigu, eto, “Iakob basio hereva henia, hereva namona eiava hereva dikana.”
english: It is in the power of my hand to hurt you, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, ‘Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.’

motu: Harihari tamamu ena ruma o ura henia lalo-dikamu dainai vada bo laomu; to dahaka dainai egu dirava laulaudia o henaodia?
english: Now, you want to be gone, because you greatly longed for your father’s house, but why have you stolen my gods?”

motu: Bena Iakob ese Laban e haere henia, eto, Na gari, nato natumu na egu amo ba dadidia oho readia.
english: Jacob answered Laban, “Because I was afraid, for I said, ‘Lest you should take your daughters from me by force.’

motu: A emu dirava laulaudia na daika dekenai ba davaridia, ia na baine mase. Ai vairamai ai emu a tahu, bavabi. Badina be Iakob na asi dibana Rahela ese e abidia.
english: Anyone you find your gods with shall not live. Before our relatives, discern what is yours with me, and take it.” For Jacob didn’t know that Rachel had stolen them.

motu: Taunabunai Laban ese Iakob ena dabua rumana ai e tahu, bona Lea ena dabua rumana ai, bona hesiai hahinedia raruosi edia dabua rumadia ai, to ḡau ta se davaria. Bena Rahela ena dabua rumana ai e raka vareai.
english: Laban went into Jacob’s tent, into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two female servants; but he didn’t find them. He went out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.

motu: Rahela ese hari dirava laulaudia vada e abi, kamelo e hua modadia ai vada e huni, bena moda latadiai e helai. Bena Laban ese dabua rumana ai e tahu malaka-malaka, a ḡau ta se davaria.
english: Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find them.

motu: Bena hahine ese tamanae hereva henia, eto, Ḡauka, basio badu; vairamu ai asina tore isi, badina be vaia hahine emai kara e goreregumu. Taunabunai e hetahu mase, to ena dirava laulaudia se davaridia.
english: She said to her father, “Don’t let my lord be angry that I can’t rise up before you; for I’m having my period.” He searched, but didn’t find the teraphim.

motu: Bena Iakob ese Laban e badu henia, e gwau henia, eto, Egu kerere be dahaka, egu dika be dahaka, bena oi ese daidiai o havagu mai badumu ida?
english: Jacob was angry, and argued with Laban. Jacob answered Laban, “What is my trespass? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?

motu: Egu kohu idoinai vada o tahu vaitani, emu o davaria be edena? Lauegu orea taudia bona oiemu orea taudia vairadiai ba vaia dae, bena ita raruosi bae hahemaoro henida.
english: Now that you have felt around in all my stuff, what have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge between us two.

motu: Laḡani ruahui dekemu ai na noho; emu mamoe bona emu nani hahinedia asie mara dika, emu nani mamaruanedia danu ta asina abia, asina ania.
english: “These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not cast their young, and I haven’t eaten the rams of your flocks.

motu: Uda boromadia ese e habero ḡaudia danu asina vasilai; sibogu ibolodia na heni. Henao taudia ese dina ai e henao eiava hanuaboi ai e henao ḡaudia danu davadia lauegu amo o gwaurai.
english: That which was torn of animals, I didn’t bring to you. I bore its loss. Of my hand you required it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

motu: Unu na noho tomava: dina ai dina ḡaraḡara ese e hadikaguva; hanuaboi ai keru ese e alaguva; matagu na asie mahutava.
english: This was my situation: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes.

motu: Laḡani ruahui emu ruma ai na nohova: laḡani gwauta-hani isiaimu na lao heni, natumu raruosi davadia, ma laḡani tauratoi emu seri davadia. Nega gwauta davagu o ha-idaua.
english: These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.

motu: Tamagu ena Dirava, Abraham ena Dirava, Isaak ese e gari heniamu Diravana, basinema bamogu, oi na harihari ima-kavakava boma lulugu. A Dirava ese egu hekwarahi vada e itaia bona imagu ḡaukaradia vada e nene, bena boi hanuaboi e gwaumu tubu.
english: Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”

motu: Bena Laban ese e haere henia, eto, Ini hahine na lau natugu; ini memero na lau tubugu; ini seri na lauegu seri; o itamu ḡaudia iboudiai na lauegu. Ma dahaka aina karaia hari dina ai, ini natugu bona tubugu ihanamodia?
english: Laban answered Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine! What can I do today to these my daughters, or to their children whom they have borne?

motu: Aoma, aita herohemaino; eda herohemaino ese baine hahemaoro henida.
english: Now come, let’s make a covenant, you and I. Let it be for a witness between me and you.”

motu: Bena Iakob ese nadi ta e abia, e haginia, pupuna ai e halaoa.
english: Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

motu: Iakob ese danu ena orea taudia e hamaorodia, eto, Nadi a gogo. Unu e kara toma, bena una nadi senuna latanai e aniani hebou.
english: Jacob said to his relatives, “Gather stones.” They took stones, and made a heap. They ate there by the heap.

motu: Bena Laban ese una gabu ladana e hatoa legara-sahaduta; + 31:47 “legara-sahaduta” anina be “Hereva-hedinarai senuna”, Aramaik gadona ai. “Galeed” anina be “Hereva- hedinarai senuna”, Heberu gadona ai. * a Iakob ese ladana e hatoa Galeed.
english: Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, + 31:47 “Jegar Sahadutha” means “Witness Heap” in Aramaic. * but Jacob called it Galeed. + 31:47 “Galeed” means “Witness Heap” in Hebrew. *

motu: Bena Laban eto, Hari dina ai ina nadi senuna ese e hahemaoro henidamu. Una dainai ladana na Galeed.
english: Laban said, “This heap is witness between me and you today.” Therefore it was named Galeed

motu: Ma ladana ta be Mispa; + 31:49 “Mispa” anina be “Hegima kohorona”. * badina be ia eto, Basita heita heheni negadia ai Iehova ese baine gimada.
english: and Mizpah, for he said, “Yahweh watch between me and you, when we are absent one from another.

motu: Natugu ba daḡedaḡe henidia, eiava hahine haida ma bavabidia, tau ta ese basine itamu, to Dirava ese baine hahemaoro henida.
english: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives in addition to my daughters, no man is with us; behold, God is witness between me and you.”

motu: Laban ese Iakob ma e hereva henia, eto, Ini nadi bona ina pupuna na ita raruosi padadai vada na hagini.
english: Laban said to Jacob, “See this heap, and see the pillar, which I have set between me and you.

motu: Ini nadi anidia binai bona ina pupuna anina binai: lau ese ini nadi basina rakadia hanai, oi ihadikamu, bona oi ese ini nadi bona ina pupuna basio rakadia hanai, lau ihadikagu.
english: May this heap be a witness, and the pillar be a witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and that you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.

motu: Abraham ena Dirava, Nahoro ena Dirava, tamadia ena Dirava danu, ia ese baine hahemaoro henida. Bena Iakob na ia tamana Isaak ese e gari henia Diravana ladana ai e gwau hamata.
english: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” Then Jacob swore by the fear of his father, Isaac.

motu: Bena Iakob ese Dirava e boua + 31:54 Dirava e boua: Heberu taudia edia kara ta, Dirava ihanamolaina karana, be edia mauri gauna namona ta, boromakau eiava mamoe eiava nani eiava manu, e abia, edia boubou gauna ai e halaoa. Ihaboulaina patana vairanai e alaia mase, bena ihaboulaina patana lahina latanai e atoa kau, lahi ese e golea oho. Unu amo Dirava e boua. Matamana negana ai edia ihaboulaina patadia be nadi ta e haginia eiava nadi haida e lareba. Gabeamo pata korikori edia dubu ai e karaia: Esodo Karoa 27 ba itaia. * una ororo ai, bona ena orea taudia e haduadia, bae aniani. Taunabunai, e aniani, bona ororo ai e noho rani.
english: Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his relatives to eat bread. They ate bread, and stayed all night in the mountain.

motu: Daba ai Laban e tore isi, tubuna mai sinadia ida e harahudia bona e hanamodia. Bena e rakatanidia, ena hanua e lou henia.
english: Early in the morning, Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Laban departed and returned to his place.

motu: Iakob na ena dala ai ela, bena Dirava ena aneru loḡora ida e hedavari.
english: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

motu: Iakob ese e itadia, bena eto, Ina na Dirava ena tuari oreana: taunabunai una gabu ladana e hatoa Mahanaim. + 32:2 “Mahanaim” anina be “Tuari oreadia”. *
english: When he saw them, Jacob said, “This is God’s army.” He called the name of that place Mahanaim. + 32:2 “Mahanaim” means “two camps”. *

motu: Una negana ai Iakob ese ena hesiai taudia e siaidia guna, kakana Esau dekena baela, Seiri tanona ai: Edom ena tano bunai.
english: Jacob sent messengers in front of him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.

motu: E haduadia, eto, Egu lohia Esau ini ba hamaoroa toma, baoto “Emu hesiai tauna Iakob na e tomu: lau na Laban ida vada na noho ema bona hari;
english: He commanded them, saying, “This is what you shall tell my lord, Esau: ‘This is what your servant, Jacob, says. I have lived as a foreigner with Laban, and stayed until now.

motu: lau na mai egu boromakau bona doniki bona mamoe bona nani bona hesiai taudia bona hesiai hahinedia; bena ihamaorolaimu herevana egu lohia emu ai name siaia vasi, oi vairamu ai hebogahisi baina davaria totona”.
english: I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in your sight.’”

motu: Hesiai taudia na e lou ema, eto, Ai na kakamu Esau ida a hedavari, ia na dekemu e maimu, ena orea taudia sinahu-hani ida.
english: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau. He is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”

motu: Bena Iakob na e gari dikadika, kudouna e hetaha. Bena ena orea taudia bona ena mamoe, ena nani, ena boromakau, ena kamelo danu, orea rua ai e hididia.
english: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and was distressed. He divided the people who were with him, along with the flocks, the herds, and the camels, into two companies.

motu: eto, Esau ese orea ta baine davaria bena baine habuaia tari reana, a orea ta ma baine mauri.
english: He said, “If Esau comes to the one company, and strikes it, then the company which is left will escape.”

motu: Bena Iakob e ḡuriḡuri, eto, Tubugu Abraham ena Dirava, tamagu Isaak ena Dirava, Iehova e, oi ese o haduagu, oto “Emu tano ba lou henia, varavaramu dekedia baola, bena baina hanamomu”.
english: Jacob said, “God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Yahweh, who said to me, ‘Return to your country, and to your relatives, and I will do you good,’

motu: Emu hebogahisi karadia iboudiai emu hesiai tauna egu ai o kara, bona emu gwau-hamata herevadia emu hesiai tauna egu ai o hamomokani, lau na dia heḡereḡere; badina be imagu mai itotohina mo ina Ioridane sinavaina na hanai nala, a harihari mai orea rua ida vada na lou mai.
english: I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your servant; for with just my staff I crossed over this Jordan; and now I have become two companies.

motu: Na noimumu, kakagu Esau imana amo ba hamaurigu; badina be na garimu, ia na bainema, baine tuari henigu, natugu mai sinadia ida baine aladia mase.
english: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and strike me and the mothers with the children.

motu: A oi vada oto “Momokani, lau ese baina hanamomu, bona garamu baina hahutumadia kone mirina na heto, asi iduahidia”.
english: You said, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your offspring as the sand of the sea, which can’t be counted because there are so many.’”

motu: Una hanuaboi ia na unuseni ai e taruha; bena ena kohu amo herahia gaudia e abi, kakana Esau ena.
english: He stayed there that night, and took from that which he had with him a present for Esau, his brother:

motu: Gaudia bini: nani hahinedia sinahu-ruabona nani mamaruanedia ruahui; mamoe hahinedia sinahu-rua bona mamoe mamaruanedia ruahui;
english: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

motu: kamelo toi-ahui mai natudia ida; boromakau hahinedia hari-ahui; boromakau mamaruanedia gwauta; doniki ruahui; bona doniki natudia gwauta.
english: thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.

motu: Ini iboudiai ena hesiai taudia e henidia, ta ta ena seri ena seri ai. Bena ia ese ena hesiai taudia e hamaorodia, eto, Umui ba raka guna, seri ta ta mai padadia ida ba hakaudia lao.
english: He delivered them into the hands of his servants, every herd by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put a space between herd and herd.”

motu: Bena baine raka guna tauna e haduaia, eto, Kakagu Esau ida ba hedavari negana ai, ia baine henanadai, baineto “Oi na daika ena hesiai tauna? Ede bo laomu? Ina seri be daika ena?”
english: He commanded the foremost, saying, “When Esau, my brother, meets you, and asks you, saying, ‘Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these before you?’

motu: Bena oi ese ba haere henia, baoto “Ini na emu hesiai tauna Iakob ena, ena herahia ḡaudia lohia taumu Esau emu; ia danu murimai ai e maimu”.
english: Then you shall say, ‘They are your servant, Jacob’s. It is a present sent to my lord, Esau. Behold, he also is behind us.’”

motu: Ihararuana danu unu e haduaia toma, bona ihatatoina, bona idia muridiai seri ta ta bae hakaudia taudia, hahedua tamona e henidia, eto, Esau ida ba hedavari negana ai ini ba hereva henia toma.
english: He commanded also the second, and the third, and all that followed the herds, saying, “This is how you shall speak to Esau, when you find him.

motu: Ma baoto “Emu hesiai tauna Iakob na murimai ai e maimu”. Ia na lalona ai eto: Egu herahia ḡaudia amo ena badu baina laoa ahu guna, gabeai ia vairanai baina hedinarai negana ai reana baine abigu dae.
english: You shall say, ‘Not only that, but behold, your servant, Jacob, is behind us.’” For, he said, “I will appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face. Perhaps he will accept me.”

motu: Taunabunai, unu hesiai taudia ese herahia ḡaudia e gunalai, a Iakob na una hanuaboi taruha ai e noho, ena orea taudia ida.
english: So the present passed over before him, and he himself stayed that night in the camp.

motu: Malokihi ai e tore isi, adavana raruosi bona ena hesiai hahinedia raruosi bona natuna mamaruanedia gwauta-ta-osi e abidia, sinavai maraḡina ladana Iabok bae turu hanai.
english: He rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two servants, and his eleven sons, and crossed over the ford of the Jabbok.

motu: Ia ese e abidia, e siaidia hanai, ena kohu idoinai danu e hanailai.
english: He took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that which he had.

motu: A Iakob na sibona noho, bena tau ta na ia ida e hedaverai ela bona daba e kinia.
english: Jacob was left alone, and wrestled with a man there until the breaking of the day.

motu: Hari tau na dibana ia na basine kwalimu diba, bena ia ese Iakob mamuna varovarona e daua toho; taunabunai Iakob aena e heride, ia na hari tau ida e hedaverai negana ai.
english: When he saw that he didn’t prevail against him, the man touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained as he wrestled.

motu: Bena hari tau eto, A kahugu nege, badina be daba vada e kinia. A Iakob eto, Lau na basina kahumu nege ela bona oi ese ba hanamogu.
english: The man said, “Let me go, for the day breaks.” Jacob|strong="H3290" * said, “ I|strong="H3588" * won’t let|strong="H3808" * you|strong="H3588" * go|strong="H3201" * unless|strong="H3588" * you|strong="H3588" * bless me|strong="H7200" *.”

motu: Bena hari tau eto, Oi ladamu be daika? Ia na e haere, eto, Ladagu na Iakob.
english: He said to him, “What is your name?” He|strong="H3588" * said, “ Jacob|strong="H7971" *”.

motu: Hari tau ma eto, Harihari ela oi ladamu na dia Iakob; oi ladamu na Israel, + 32:28 “Israel” anina be “Dirava ida e goada helulu”. * badina be Dirava ida vada o goada helulu bona taunimanima ida danu, bona vada o kwalimu.
english: He said, “Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed.”

motu: Bena Iakob ese e nanadaia, eto, Mani emu kara, oi ladamu ba hadibagu. Hari tau elo, Badina be dahaka lau ladagu o henanadailaiamu? Bena ia ese e hanamoa.
english: Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” He|strong="H3588" * said, “ Why|strong="H3588" * is|strong="H8034" * it|strong="H3588" * that|strong="H3588" * you|strong="H3588" * ask what|strong="H3588" * my|strong="H3290" * name|strong="H8034" * is|strong="H8034" *?” So|strong="H3808" * he|strong="H3588" * blessed him|strong="H5973" * there|strong="H8034" *.

motu: Bena Iakob ese una gabu ladana e hatoa Peniel; + 32:30 “Peniel” anina be “Dirava Vairana”. * eto, Dirava vada na itaia, raruosi vada ame hegaga heheni, to vada na maurimu.
english: Jacob called the name of the place Peniel; + 32:30 Peniel means “face of God”. * for he said, “I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”

motu: Bena Penuel e rakaia hanai ai daba e rere, ia na aena e heride.
english: The sun rose on him as he passed over Peniel, and he limped because of his thigh.

motu: Badina bunai Israel besena taudia na mamu varovarodia asie animu ema bona harihari: badina be Iakob mamuna varovarona e daua toho bena aena e heride.
english: Therefore the children of Israel don’t eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.

motu: Bena Iakob na e gaga isi, Esau e itaia, ena orea taudia sinahuhaniosi ida e maiva. Bena ia ese natuna e hididia, Lea natuna bona Rahela natuna bona hesiai hahinedia natudia;
english: Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children between Leah, Rachel, and the two servants.

motu: hesiai hahinedia mai natudia ida vairai bae raka, idia muridiai Lea mai natuna ida, ma idia muridiai Rahela mai natuna Iosef ida.
english: He put the servants and their children in front, Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.

motu: A ia na e raka guna, nega hahitu tano ai e goru diho, ela bona kakana e raka henia kahi.
english: He himself passed over in front of them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

motu: Bena Esau na e heau ela, e rosia, e harahua; bena raruosi na e taitai.
english: Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.

motu: Bena Esau na e gaga isi, hari hahine mai natudia ida e itadia, bena eto, Idia be daidia? Iakob e haere, eto, Natugu bunu, Dirava ese emu hesiai tauna vada e bogagu hisi, vada e henigu.
english: He lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, “Who are these with you?” He|strong="H4310" * said, “ The|strong="H7200" * children|strong="H3206" * whom|strong="H4310" * God|strong="H4310" * has|strong="H4310" * graciously|strong="H2603" * given|strong="H5650" * your|strong="H5375" * servant|strong="H5650" *.”

motu: Bena hari hesiai hahinedia mai natudia ida e raka kahira, tano ai e goru goru diho.
english: Then the servants came near with their children, and they bowed themselves.

motu: Lea danu natuna ida e raka kahira, bona Rahela mai natuna Iosef ida danu, bena idia danu e goru goru diho.
english: Leah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves. After them, Joseph came near with Rachel, and they bowed themselves.

motu: Esau ma e henanadai, eto, Unu seri iboudiai dala ai na itadia be edeheto? Iakob na e haere, eto, Una na herahia ḡauna, egu lohia vairamu ai baina mauri helaoreana.
english: Esau said, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?” Jacob said, “ To|strong="H5869" * find|strong="H4672" * favor|strong="H2580" * in|strong="H4672" * the|strong="H3605" * sight|strong="H5869" * of|strong="H5869" * my|strong="H3605" * lord.”

motu: A Esau eto, Tadigu e, lauegu na davana, oiemu hari ba dogo tao.
english: Esau said, “I have enough, my brother; let that which you have be yours.”

motu: Iakob eto, Lasi, bema lalomu vada eme namo egu ai, bavabi, egu lalokau toana; badina be oi vairamu vada na itaia, Dirava vairana bama itaia heḡereḡerena, bona vada o lalo namo henigu.
english: Jacob said, “Please, no, if I have now found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me.

motu: Taunabunai egu herahia ḡaudia bavabi dae, bona egu hahenamo danu; badina be Dirava ese vada e hanamogu badabada, mai dinagu vada nama. Bena e noia goada dainai vada e abi.
english: Please take the gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he took it.

motu: Bena Esau eto, Mani aita laolao hebou; lau na vairai baina raka.
english: Esau said, “Let’s take our journey, and let’s go, and I will go before you.”

motu: A Iakob eto, Egu lohia dibana natugu na mamaraḡi; egu mamoe hahinedia bona egu boromakau hahinedia haida na mai bogadia, bena dina tamona mo bae luludia haraḡa-haraḡa vada bae mase ore.
english: Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.

motu: Taunabunai, egu lohia e, oi na emu hesiai tauna ba gunalaigu; a lau na baina raka metaira-metaira, egu seri bona natugu edia goada heḡereḡerena, ela bona Seiri ai egu lohia baina vasi henimu.
english: Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir.”

motu: Bena Esau eto, Benaini, egu orea taudia haida bavabidia, bae bamomu. A Iakob eto, Una na herevana; egu lohia lalomu vada e namo egu ai vada davana.
english: Esau said, “Let me now leave with you some of the people who are with me.” He|strong="H4480" * said, “ Why|strong="H4100" *? Let|strong="H4994" * me|strong="H4994" * find|strong="H4672" * favor|strong="H2580" * in|strong="H4672" * the|strong="H4480" * sight|strong="H5869" * of|strong="H5869" * my|strong="H4480" * lord.”

motu: Taunabunai Esau na una dina ai e lou, Seiri dalana ai e lou ela.
english: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.

motu: A Iakob na Sukoto ela; unuseni ai ia ese ruma auta e hadaia iena, bona kalaga haida e hadai ena boromakau edia. Una dainai gabu ladana e hatoa Sukoto. + 33:17 “Sukoto” anirla be “Kalaga”. *
english: Jacob traveled to Succoth, built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place is called Succoth. + 33:17 succoth means shelters or booths. *

motu: Unuhetomana Iakob na mai maurina ida Padan-aram amo ema, Sekem hanuana ai e lasi, Kanaan tanona ai; bena hanua badinai e taruha.
english: Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan Aram; and encamped before the city.

motu: Bena e taruha henia tanona na Hamoro, Sekem e hadaia tauna, natuna edia amo e hoia, davana na silver * monidia sinahu-ta.
english: He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.

motu: Unuseni ai boubou patana ta e larebaia, ladana e hatoa El-Elohe-Israel. + 33:20 “El-Elohe-Israel” anina be “Dirava, Israel Diravana”. *
english: He erected an altar there, and called it El Elohe Israel. + 33:20 El Elohe Israel means “God, the God of Israel” or “The God of Israel is mighty”. *

motu: Iakob bona Lea natudia hahinena Daina na eha loaloa, una tano hahinedia i'igo-itadia ela.
english: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

motu: Bena una tano lohiana, Hamoro, tau Hivi, natuna Sekem ese e ḡahusia, bena e rosia, e ḡaḡaia.
english: Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her, lay with her, and humbled her.

motu: To ia ese Iakob natuna Daina e ura henia lalodika, mai lalona idoinai, bena ia lalona ihamarumaruna herevadia e gwaurai heniava.
english: His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.

motu: Bena Sekem ese tamana Hamoro e hamaoroa, eto, Ina hane-ulato bavabia, baina adavaia.
english: Shechem spoke to his father, Hamor, saying, “Get me this young lady as a wife.”

motu: Iakob na harina e kamonai Sekem ese natuna Daina vada e hahemaraia, a natuna mamaruanedia ese taora ai seri e reḡudiava, bena Iakob ese hereva ta se gwauraia ela bona idia ema.
english: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah, his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field. Jacob held his peace until they came.

motu: Bena Hamoro, Sekem tamana, e lasi, Iakob ida bae hereva-hereva eto.
english: Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to talk with him.

motu: A Iakob natuna mamaruanedia na harina e kamonai, bena taora amo e lasi mai lalo-hisihisidia bona mai badudia ida; badina be una tau ese Israel vada e hahemaraia, Iakob natuna Daina vada e ḡaḡaia, dainai.
english: The sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it. The men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter, a thing that ought not to be done.

motu: A Hamoro ese e hamaorodia, eto, Natugu Sekem ese oi natumu e ura henia lalodikamu; mani emu kara ba henia, baine adavaia.
english: Hamor talked with them, saying, “The soul of my son, Shechem, longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.

motu: Beseda bae hatamona: umui ese natumui ulatodia ba henimai, emai ai bae headava; ai danu natumai ulatodia baia henimui, emui ai bae headava.
english: Make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.

motu: Bogaragimai ai ba noho: ai emai tano na umui emui tano ai bainela; iniseni ai ba biru, ba hoihoi, ba hanua.
english: You shall dwell with us, and the land will be before you. Live and trade in it, and get possessions in it.”

motu: Sekem ese danu hane-ulato tamana bona taihuna e hereva henidia, eto, Egu noinoi boma abia dae, hane-ulato davana boma gwauraia, bena bama henimui.
english: Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you will tell me I will give.

motu: Ena be davana ba habadaia herea, to vada baina henimui; ḡau tamona, hane-ulato na ba henigu, baina adavaia.
english: Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I will give whatever you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”

motu: A Iakobo natuna mamaruanedia na e haere koikoi, Sekem, tamana Hamoro ida, e dibaḡanidia, taihuna Daina vada e hahemaraia dainai.
english: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit when they spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,

motu: E hamaorodia, eto, Taihumai na se peritomea tauna baia henia na taravatu, bona hemarai ihavarana karana emai ai.
english: and said to them, “We can’t do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.

motu: To ini baia kara henimui toma: bema umui ese emui maruane iboudiai ba peritomedia, ai bamomai,
english: Only on this condition will we consent to you. If you will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised,

motu: ai ese natumai ulatodia baia henimui bona natumui ulatodia baia abidia, bena bogaragimui ai baia noho, bese tamona ai baitala.
english: then will we give our daughters to you; and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.

motu: A bema emai hereva basio abia dae, basio peritome, ai na hane-ulato baia abia, baiala.
english: But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, then we will take our sister, + 34:17 Hebrew has, literally, “daughter” * and we will be gone.”

motu: Hamoro bona natuna Sekem na edia hereva e kamonai, bena raruosi e moale;
english: Their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.

motu: hari tauhau na se halahe, edia ura mo e karaia, badina be Iakob natuna ulatona e moalelaia bada; tamana ena ruma ai danu ia sibona herea.
english: The young man didn’t wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was honored above all the house of his father.

motu: Bena Hamoro, natuna Sekem ida, edia hanua ikoukouna ela, edia hanua taudia e hereva henidia, eto,
english: Hamor and Shechem, his son, came to the gate of their city, and talked with the men of their city, saying,

motu: Ini taunimanima na maino e uramu; taunabunai eda tano ai bae noho baine namo: bae hoihoi bona bae biru, badina be tano na bada. Natudia ulatodia baita adavadia, bona natuda ulatodia baita henidia.
english: “These men are peaceful with us. Therefore let them live in the land and trade in it. For behold, the land is large enough for them. Let’s take their daughters to us for wives, and let’s give them our daughters.

motu: To idia lalodia bae heḡereḡere bogaragidai bae noho bona ita ida bese tamona ai baitala dalana na tamona mo: ita bogaragidai maruane iboudiai baita peritomedia, idia e karamu heḡereḡerena.
english: Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people, if every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.

motu: Gabe amo edia seri bona edia kohu bona edia boromakau iboudiai na iseda ai baita halao, ani? Idia ida baita herohemaino, bena bogaragidai do bae noho.
english: Won’t their livestock and their possessions and all their animals be ours? Only let’s give our consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”

motu: Hanua taudia iboudiai ese Hamoro bona natuna Sekem edia hereva e abia dae; bena maruane iboudiai e peritomedia.
english: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor, and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.

motu: Dina ihatoina ai, taudia hisidia e dai lasi, bena Iakob natuna rarua, Simeon bona Levi, hari Daina taihuna, ese edia dare e abi, hanua ai e raka vareai, bena mamaruanedia ibouboudiai e aladia mase;
english: On the third day, when they were sore, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the unsuspecting city, and killed all the males.

motu: Hamoro bona natuna Sekem danu dare amo e aladia mase. Daina danu Sekem ena ruma amo e hakaua diho, bena ela.
english: They killed Hamor and Shechem, his son, with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.

motu: Bena Iakob natuna mamaruanedia na ela, Sekem taudia masedia ai e davaridia, bena hanua e habuaia tari, taihudia e hahemaraia dainai.
english: Jacob’s sons came on the dead, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.

motu: Edia mamoe bona edia boromakau bona edia doniki bona edia ruma kohudia bona adia uma anidia idoidiai e abihaidia;
english: They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, that which was in the city, that which was in the field,

motu: natudia maraḡidia danu bona adavadia e abidia mauri. Edia ruma kohudia e ha-ore, bena ruma e doudia.
english: and all their wealth. They took captive all their little ones and their wives, and took as plunder everything that was in the house.

motu: Bena Iakob ese Simeon bona Levi e gwau henidia, eto, Hekwarahi egu ai vada o havaraia, bona ladagu vada o hadikaia ina tano taudia, Kanaan taudia bona Perisi taudia, bogaragidiai. Bena ita na dia hoho dainai idia na bae hebou, bae tuari henigu; bena lau bona egu ruma taudia iboudiai baita mase ore.
english: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number. They will gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house.”

motu: A idia e haere, eto, Be, taihumai na ariara hahinena ai e halaoa namo eiava?
english: They said, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”

motu: Dirava ese Iakob e hamaoroa, eto, Betele baola, unuseni ai ba ha noho; unuseni ai danu kakamu Esau o heautania negana ai e hahedinarai henimu Diravana ena ihaboulaina patana ba larebaia.
english: God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and live there. Make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.”

motu: Taunabunai, Iakob ese ena orea taudia iboudiai e haduadia, eto, Dirava idaudia dekemui ai mimia vada a negedia, ba haheḡoeva, dabua ḡoevadia ba rio;
english: Then Jacob said to his household, and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your garments.

motu: Betele baitala, unuseni ai egu dika dinana ai e haere henigu bona egu dala iboudiai lalodiai e bamogu Diravana ena ihaboulaina patana baina larebaia.
english: Let’s arise, and go up to Bethel. I will make there an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me on the way which I went.”

motu: Bena idia ese edia dirava idaudia bona taiadia gadeidia na Iakob e henia. Iakob ese e abidia, au helaḡana Sekem ai henunai e guridia.
english: They gave to Jacob all the foreign gods which were in their hands, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.

motu: Bena edia laolao ela; bona hanua hanua taudia ese Dirava garina e gariva dainai idia ese Iakob natuna asie tuari henidia
english: They traveled, and a terror of God was on the cities that were around them, and they didn’t pursue the sons of Jacob.

motu: Bena Iakob na Lusu ai e kau (una na Betele ladana ta) Kanaan tanona ai, ia bona ena orea taudia iboudiai danu.
english: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.

motu: Unuseni ai ia ese boubou patana ta e larebaia, ladana e hatoa El-betele; + 35:7 “El-betele” anina be “Betele Diravana”. * badina be una gabu ai Dirava ese e hahedinarai henia, ia ese kakana e heautania negana ai.
english: He built an altar there, and called the place El Beth El; because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.

motu: Una negana ai, Rebeka ena hesiai hahinena, ladana Debora, Rebeka e vara negana amo isiaina e lao heniva hahinena, vada e mase. Bena Betele ai e guria, au helaḡana henunai; una gabu ladana e hatoa Alono-bakutu. + 35:8 “Alono-bakutu” anina be “Taitai auna”. *
english: Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was called Allon Bacuth.

motu: Dirava ese Iakob ma e hahedinarai henia lou, Padan-aram amo ema negana ai, e hanamoa, eto,
english: God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.

motu: Oi ladamu na Iakob, a ladamu basie hatoa lou Iakob; harihari bainela ladamu bae hatoa Israel. Taunabunai, ladana e hatoa Israel.
english: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be Jacob any more, but your name will be Israel.” He named him Israel.

motu: Bena Dirava ese e hamaoroa, eto, Lau na Siahu-idoinai Diravana: natumu ba havaradia, garamu bae hutuma; bese momo oiemu amo bae vara, bona hanua pavapavadia danu.
english: God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body.

motu: Abraham bona Isaak na henidia tanona oi baina henimu, bona oi garamu murimu ai bae vara danu baina henidia.
english: The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”

motu: Bena Dirava ese ia e rakatania, e hereva henia gabuna danu e rakatania.
english: God went up from him in the place where he spoke with him.

motu: Bena Iakob ese nadi ta e haginia, pupuna ai e halaoa, Dirava ida e hereva gabuna ai, vine ranuna na latanai e seia, ena boubou, bona dehoro danu latanai e seia.
english: Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.

motu: Bena una Dirava ese e hereva henia gabuna ladana e hatoa Betele.
english: Jacob called the name of the place where God spoke with him “Bethel”.

motu: Idia na Betele amo eha laolao, ela Efrata vada e kahirakahira, bena Rahela e hekamonai, hisina vada e bada.
english: They traveled from Bethel. There was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.

motu: Ena hekamonai hisidia vada e bada herea ai, hegwaroto hahinena ese e hamaoroa, eto, Basio gari; mero ta do bavabia.
english: When she was in hard labor, the midwife said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for now you will have another son.”

motu: Laumana ese e rakatania horana ai (badina be ia na una negana ai e mase), ia ese mero ladana e hatoa Benoni. + 35:18 “Benoni” anina be “Egu lalo-hisihisi merona”. * Bena hahine na e mase. A tamana ese mero ladana e hatoa Beniamina. + 35:18 “Beniamina” anina be “Imagu idibana merona”. *
english: As her soul was departing (for she died), she named him Benoni, + 35:18 “Benoni” means “son of my trouble”. * but his father named him Benjamin. + 35:18 “Benjamin” means “son of my right hand”. *

motu: Unuhetomana Rahela e mase, bena Efrata dalana badinai e guria. Una Efrata ladana ta be Betelehem.
english: Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath (also called Bethlehem).

motu: Bena Iakob ese nadi pupuna ta e haginia ena gara latanai; ladana na doini e hatoamu “Rahela ena gara pupuna” ema bona harihari.
english: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave. The same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.

motu: Israel ma e laolao, kohoro ladana Mamoe Kohorona unukahana ai e taruha.
english: Israel traveled, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.

motu: Una tano ai e nohova negana ai Ruben na tamana ena hesiai hahinena Bilha ida e eno bou; bena Israel ese harina e kamonai.
english: While Israel lived in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it. Now|strong="H1961" * the|strong="H8085" * sons|strong="H1121" * of|strong="H1121" * Jacob|strong="H3290" * were|strong="H3478" * twelve|strong="H8147" *.

motu: Iakob natuna mamaruanedia na gwauta-rarua. Lea natuna: Ruben, Iakob natuna roboana, bona Simeon bona Levi bona Iuda bona Isakara bona Sebulun.
english: The sons of Leah: Reuben (Jacob’s firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

motu: Rahela natuna: Iosef bona Beniamina.
english: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

motu: Rahela ena hesiai hahinena Bilha natuna: Dan bona Napatali.
english: The sons of Bilhah (Rachel’s servant): Dan and Naphtali.

motu: Lea ena hesiai hahinena Silpa natuna: Gad bona Asere. Iakob natuna mamaruanedia, Padan-aram ai e abidia, ladadia bunu.
english: The sons of Zilpah (Leah’s servant): Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan Aram.

motu: Iakob na tamana Isaak dekena ela, Mamare ai, hanua ladana Araba. Una hanua ladana ta be Heberon; Abraham bona Isaak edia noho gabuna bunai.
english: Jacob came to Isaac his father, to Mamre, to Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac lived as foreigners.

motu: Hari Isaak ena mauri laḡanidia na sinahu-ta taurahani-ahui.
english: The days of Isaac were one hundred eighty years.

motu: Bena Isaak na laumana e heni dae, vada e mase, tubu tama dekediai eha hebou. Ia na tau buruka; ena mauri vada e daudau herea. Ia natuna raruosi, Esau bona Iakob, ese e guria.
english: Isaac gave up the spirit and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.

motu: Esau garana bini. Ia ladana ta be Edom.
english: Now this is the history of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).

motu: Esau adavana na Kanaan hahinedia: Ada, Elon tau Hiti natuna; bona Oholibama, Ana natuna, Sibeon tau Hivi tubuna;
english: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon, the Hittite; and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the Hivite;

motu: bona Basemata, Ismael natuna, Nebaioto taihuna.
english: and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.

motu: Ada ese mero ta e abia, ladana Elifasa; bona Basemata ese mero ta e abia, ladana Reuele;
english: Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz. Basemath bore Reuel.

motu: bona Oholibama ese memero tatoi e abidia, ladadia na Ieusu bona Ialam bona Kora: Esau natuna bunu, Kanaan tanona ai e vara.
english: Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

motu: Esau ese adavana tatoiosi bona natuna mamaruanedia bona hahinedia, bona ena orea taudia iboudiai, bona ena boromakau bona ena seri iboudiai bona ena kohu idoidiai Kanaan ai e habou, e abidia, tadina Iakob e rakatania, Seiri tanona ela.
english: Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the members of his household, with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the land of Canaan, and went into a land away from his brother Jacob.

motu: Badina be raruosi edia taḡa na bada herea dainai tano na dia heḡereḡere idia raruosi bona edia seri idoidiai bae noholaia.
english: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their travels couldn’t bear them because of their livestock.

motu: Taunabunai, Esau na Seiri ororodia ai eha noho. Esau na Edom.
english: Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.

motu: Esau garana bini: ia na Edom besena, Seiri ororodia ai e nohomu besena, ihavarana tauna.
english: This is the history of the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir:

motu: Esau natuna mamaruanedia bini: Elifasa, Esau adavana Ada natuna; bona Reuele, Esau adavana Basemata natuna.
english: these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; and Reuel, the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

motu: Elifasa natuna na Teman bona Omara bona Sefo bona Gatam bona Kena.
english: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.

motu: Elifasa, Esau natuna, ese danu hahine ta ladana Timna e adavaia; hari Timna ese mero ta e abia, ladana Amalek: ini iboudiai na Esau adavana Ada tubuna.
english: Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son; and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek. These are the descendants of Adah, Esau’s wife.

motu: Reuele natuna bini: Nahata bona Sera bona Sama bona Misa. Idia na Esau adavana Basemata tubuna.
english: These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the descendants of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

motu: Esau adavana Oholibama, Ana natuna, Sibeon tubuna, natuna bini: Ieusu bona Ialam bona Kora.
english: These were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

motu: Hanua lohiadia Esau ena amo e vara ladadia bini: Elifasa, Esau natuna roboana, ese Teman bona Omara bona Sefo bona Kena,
english: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,

motu: bona Kora bona Gatam bona Amalek e havaradia: ini iboudiai na Edom tanona lohiadia, Elifasa, Ada natuna, ese e havaradia.
english: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs who came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Adah.

motu: Esau natuna Reuele natuna bini: Nahata bona Sera bona Sama bona Misa. Idia na hanua lohiadia Reuele ai, Edom tanona ai; idia danu Esau adavana Basemata tubuna.
english: These are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs who came of Reuel in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

motu: Esau adavana Oholibama natuna bini: Ieusu bona Ialam bona Kora. Ini na hanua lohiadia, Esau adavana Oholibama, Ana natuna, ese e abidia.
english: These are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These are the chiefs who came of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.

motu: Esau natuna bunu, bona Edom lohiadia bunu.
english: These are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these are their chiefs.

motu: Seiri tau Hori natuna una tano ai e nohova ladadia bini: Lotan bona Sobal bona Sibeon bona Ana
english: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

motu: bona Dison bona Esere bona Disan: Hori lohiadia bunu, Seiri ese e havaradia Edom tanona ai.
english: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.

motu: Lotan natuna na Hori bona Heman; Lotan taihuna na Timna.
english: The children of Lotan were Hori and Heman. Lotan’s sister was Timna.

motu: Sobal natuna na Alavan bona Manahata bona Ebal bona Sefo bona Onam.
english: These are the children of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

motu: Sibeon natuna na Aia bona Ana. Hari Ana na ranu e lohilohimu gabudia e davaridia tano ḡaḡaena ai, tamana Sibeon ena doniki e reḡudiava negana ai.
english: These are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Zibeon his father.

motu: Ana natuna bini: maruanena ta ladana na Dison, bona hahinena ta ladana na Oholibama.
english: These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.

motu: Dison natuna na Hemudan bona Eseban bona Itiran bona Keran.
english: These are the children of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.

motu: Esere natuna na Bilhan bona Saavan bona Akan.
english: These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

motu: Disan natuna na Usu bona Aran.
english: These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

motu: Hori lohiadia bini: Lotan bona Sobal bona Sibeon bona Ana
english: These are the chiefs who came of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,

motu: bona Dison bona Esere bona Disan. Hori lohiadia bunu, Seiri tanona e lohiaia taudia.
english: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.

motu: Hanua pavapavadia haida ese Edom tanona e lohiaia, Israel taudia na do asi edia pavapava negadia ai. Ladadia bini:
english: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel.

motu: Bela Beoro na Edom pavapavana, ena hanua badana ladana na Dinihaba.
english: Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.

motu: Ia e mase; bena Iobab, Sera tau Bosra natuna, ese gabuna e abia.
english: Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, reigned in his place.

motu: Iokab e mase; bena Husam na Teman tanona amo ema, gabuna e abia.
english: Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

motu: Husam e mase; bena Hadad Bedad, Moab taorana ai Midian taudia e hadareredia tauna, ese gabuna e abia; iena hanua badana ladana na Aviti.
english: Husham died, and Hadad, the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith.

motu: Hadad e mase; bena Samula tau Masareka ese gabuna e abia.
english: Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.

motu: Samula e mase: bena Saul na sinavai isena hanuana ladana Rehoboto amo ema, gabuna e abia.
english: Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his place.

motu: Saul e mase; bena Baal-hanana Akaboro ese gabuna e abia.
english: Shaul died, and Baal Hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.

motu: Baal-hanana e mase; bena Hadara ese gabuna e abia. Iena hanua badana ladana na Pau. Adavana ladana be Mehetabel; ia na Matared natuna, tubuna be Mesahab.
english: Baal Hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau. His wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

motu: Esau besena edia hanua lohiadia, ta ta mai edia iduhu bona mai edia hanua, ladadia bini: Timna; Alava; Ietete;
english: These are the names of the chiefs who came from Esau, according to their families, after their places, and by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,

motu: Oholibama; Elaha; Pinon;
english: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

motu: Kena; Teman; Mibsara;
english: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

motu: Magdiel; Iram: Edom lohiadia bunu, ta ta ese ena hanua ena hanua e halohiadia. A Edom besena ihavarana tauna be Esau.
english: chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.

motu: Iakob ese tamana e noholaia tanona ma e noholaia, Kanaan tanona.
english: Jacob lived in the land of his father’s travels, in the land of Canaan.

motu: Iakob garana herevadia bini: Iosef ena mauri laḡanidia na gwautahitu, bena nega ta seri e reḡuva, ia kakana, tamana adavana Bilha bona Silpa natudia, ida. Bena Iosef na tamana dekena ela, kakana e habadelaidia.
english: This is the history of the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers. He was a boy with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. Joseph brought an evil report of them to their father.

motu: Israel ese hari Iosef e lalokau henia bada, natuna orena e lalokau henidia maraḡi; badina be burukana ai e havaraia. Bena ia ese hahedoki namohereana ta e henia.
english: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a tunic of many colors.

motu: A kakana ese e itaia, tamadia ese Iosef e lalokau henia bada, idia e lalokau henidia maraḡi; bena idia ese e inai henia, hereva namona ta asie gwaurai henia.
english: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him, and couldn’t speak peaceably to him.

motu: Hari Iosef na e nihi, bena ena nihi na kakana e hamaorolaidia; una dainai idia ese e inai henia lalodika.
english: Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him all the more.

motu: E hamaorodia eto, Egu nihi mani aina hamaorolaimui.
english: He said to them, “Please hear this dream which I have dreamed:

motu: Egu nihi ai ita na uma ai, uit ta ḡui; bena lauegu iḡui na e gini tore, a umui emui iḡui ese e ginia heḡeḡe, lauegu iḡui e toma henia diho.
english: for behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves came around, and bowed down to my sheaf.”

motu: Bena kakana ese e gwau henia, eto, Oi na ai emai pavapava ai baola a? Oi ese ai ba halohiamai a? Bena ena nihi bona ena hereva daidiai edia badu ienai vada e bada e laova.
english: His brothers asked him, “Will you indeed reign over us? Will you indeed have dominion over us?” They hated him all the more for his dreams and for his words.

motu: Ma e nihi lou, bena ena nihi na kakana e hamaorolaidia, eto, Vada na nihi lou, bena egu nihi ai dina bona hua bona hisiu gwauta-taese e toma henigu diho.
english: He dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brothers, and said, “Behold, I have dreamed yet another dream: and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to me.”

motu: Ia ese tamana bona kakana unu e hamaorodia toma; bena tamana e gwaugwau, eto, Emu nihi anina be dahaka a? Lau bona sinamu bona kakamu ese oi baia toma henimu diho a?
english: He told it to his father and to his brothers. His father rebuked him, and said to him, “What is this dream that you have dreamed? Will I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow ourselves down to the earth before you?”

motu: Bena kakana e badu dikadika, a tamana ese ena hereva e lalo tao.
english: His brothers envied him, but his father kept this saying in mind.

motu: Nega ta kakana na Sekem ela, tamadia ena seri ireḡudia.
english: His brothers went to feed their father’s flock in Shechem.

motu: Bena Israel ese Iosef e hereva henia, eto, Kakamu na Sekem ai seri e reḡudiamu ani? Aoma, aina siaimu dekediai. Iosef e haere, eto, Lau o ina.
english: Israel said to Joseph, “Aren’t your brothers feeding the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.” He said to him, “Here I am.”

motu: Ma e hamaoroa, eto, Vada aola, ba itadia, kakamu be nanamo eiava, bona seri na edeheto; bena ma baoma, ba hadibagu. Bena e siaia; Heberon kourana amo e lasi, Sekem ai e kau.
english: He said to him, “Go now, see whether it is well with your brothers, and well with the flock; and bring me word again.” So he sent him out of the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.

motu: Bena tau ta ese e itaia, taora ai e loa eva-eva, bena e nanadaia, eto, Dahaka o tahuamu?
english: A certain man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the field. The man asked him, “What are you looking for?”

motu: Iosef na e haere, eto, Lau na kakagu na tahudiamu; mani emu kara ba hadibagu, idia na edeseni ai edia seri e reḡudiamu.
english: He said, “I am looking for my brothers. Tell me, please, where they are feeding the flock.”

motu: Hari tau eto, Ini amo vada e raka oho; badina be edia hereva na kamonai, eto, “Ita na Dotan baitala”. Taunabunai Iosef ese e ḡavadia ela, Dotan ai e ḡavadia tao.
english: The man said, “They have left here, for I heard them say, ‘Let’s go to Dothan.’” Joseph|strong="H3130" * went|strong="H3212" * after|strong="H3588" * his|strong="H8085" * brothers, and|strong="H3212" * found|strong="H4672" * them|strong="H4672" * in|strong="H8085" * Dothan|strong="H1886" *.

motu: A ia na dounu dauhai, idia ese e itaia; bena ia do se raka henidia kahi ai idia vada e henega bou, bae alaia mase eto.
english: They saw him afar off, and before he came near to them, they conspired against him to kill him.

motu: E hereva heheni, eto O itaia, hari nihi tauna vada e maimu;
english: They said to one another, “Behold, this dreamer comes.

motu: aita alaia mase, ini guri asi ranudia ta ai baita negea dobi; bena baitato “Uda boromana ta ese e alaia mase”; unu amo baita itaia, ena nihi anidia be dahaka.
english: Come now therefore, and let’s kill him, and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say, ‘An evil animal has devoured him.’ We will see what will become of his dreams.”

motu: A Ruben na unu hereva e kamonai, bena ia ese idia imadia amo e hamauria, eto, Lasi, ena mauri basita abia oho,
english: Reuben heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said, “Let’s not take his life.”

motu: basita alaia mase, a guri ta ai baita tahoa dobi. Unu e gwau toma badina ena lalo-hadai be idia imadia amo baine hamauria, tamana baine henia lou eto.
english: Reuben said to them, “Shed no blood. Throw him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but lay no hand on him”—that he might deliver him out of their hand, to restore him to his father.

motu: Taunabunai, Iosef na kakana dekediai e kau ai, idia ese e dabaia tao, ena hahedoki namo-hereana e dokia oho,
english: When Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic of many colors that was on him;

motu: e laohaia, guri ta ai etahoa dobi. Una guri na asi ranuna.
english: and they took him, and threw him into the pit. The pit was empty. There was no water in it.

motu: Bena idia na e ege diho, e aniani. Bena e gaga isi, laolao taudia haida e itadia; idia na Ismael taudia, Gilead amo e maiva, Aigupto baela eto. Edia kamelo ese aniani muramuradia bona muramura mai bonadia e hua.
english: They sat down to eat bread, and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.

motu: Bena Iuda ese tadikakana e hamaorodia, eto, Tadida baita alaia bona ena mase baita hunia anina be dahaka?
english: Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

motu: Ini Ismael taudia ediai aita hoia. Imada na ienai basita dau kau, badina be ia na tadida korikori. Bena tadikakana ese ena hereva e abia dae.
english: Come, and let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites, and not let our hand be on him; for he is our brother, our flesh.” His brothers listened to him.

motu: Hari hoihoi taudia na Midian amo e raka hanai; bena Iosef kakana ese guri amo e veria dae, Ismael taudia ediai e hoia, silver * monidia ruahui davana. Bena idia ese e hakaua lao, Aigupto e laohaia.
english: Midianites who were merchants passed by, and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. The merchants brought Joseph into Egypt.

motu: Gabeamo Ruben na guri e lou henia, a Iosef na lasihia. Bena ena dabua e darea,
english: Reuben returned to the pit, and saw that Joseph wasn’t in the pit; and he tore his clothes.

motu: tadina dekedia e lou lao, eto, Mero na lasihia; lau na ede baina kara toma?
english: He returned to his brothers, and said, “The child is no more; and I, where will I go?”

motu: Bena idia ese Iosef ena hahedoki e abia, nani natuna ta e alaia, rarana amo hahedoki e hamiroa.
english: They took Joseph’s tunic, and killed a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.

motu: Bena hari hahedoki na tamadia dekena e laohaia, eto, Ina na ai ese a davaria; a itaia, ina na natumu ena hahedoki eiava?
english: They took the tunic of many colors, and they brought it to their father, and said, “We have found this. Examine it, now, and see if it is your son’s tunic or not.”

motu: E itaia, bena eto, Ina na natugu ena hahedoki; uda boromana ta ese vada e alaia mase; momokani, Iosef vada e mase.
english: He recognized it, and said, “It is my son’s tunic. An evil animal has devoured him. Joseph is without doubt torn in pieces.”

motu: Bena Iakob ese ena dabua e darea, guma dabuana e rioa, natuna itailaina e tai boi tai rani ela dina hoho.
english: Jacob tore his clothes, and put sackcloth on his waist, and mourned for his son many days.

motu: Bena natuna mamaruanedia bona hahinedia iboudiai na ihamarumaruna totona e lao henia, a ia na tauhalo se ura. Ia na e tai lolololo, eto, Natugu baina lao henia mase gabuna ai mai taigu ida. Tamana ese unu e tailaia toma.
english: All his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. He said, “For I will go down to Sheol + 37:35 Sheol is the place of the dead. * to my son, mourning.” His father wept for him.

motu: A Midian taudia ese Iosef e hoia Aigupto ai, Potifara, Farao ena tuari oreana biaguna ta, enai.
english: The Midianites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard.

motu: Nega ta Iuda ese tadikakana e rakatanidia, ela, Adulama tauna ta, ladana Hira, dekenai e nohova.
english: At that time, Judah went down from his brothers, and visited a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

motu: Unuseni ai ia ese Kanaan tauna ta, ladana Sua, natuna ulatona e itaia; bena e adavaia.
english: There, Judah saw the daughter of a certain Canaanite man named Shua. He took her, and went in to her.

motu: Una hahine e mara, mero ta e abia, ladana e hatoa Ere;
english: She conceived, and bore a son; and he named him Er.

motu: ma ta e abia, ladana e hatoa Onan;
english: She conceived again, and bore a son; and she named him Onan.

motu: ma ihatatoina e abia, ladana e hatoa Sela. Una mero e vara negana ai, hahine na Kesib ai e nohova.
english: She yet again bore a son, and named him Shelah. He was at Chezib when she bore him.

motu: Iuda ese hane-ulato ta davana e heni, natuna roboana Ere adavanaai bainela; ia ladana na Tamara.
english: Judah took a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

motu: A hari Ere, Iuda natuna roboana, na Iehova vairanai e kara havara, bena Iehova ese e alaia mase.
english: Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in Yahweh’s sight. So Yahweh killed him.

motu: Bena Iuda ese Onan e haduaia, eto, Vabu enai ba raka vareai, bavadavaia, natuna ba havaraia, kakamu ena.
english: Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.”

motu: Bena Onan dibana mero na basie gwauraia ia natuna dainai ia na hahine enai e raka vareai, a gau be tano ai e hahebubua, natuna ta basine vara helaoreana.
english: Onan knew that the offspring wouldn’t be his; and when he went in to his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground, lest he should give offspring to his brother.

motu: Una kara dikana dainai Iehova ese e badu henia, e alaia mase, kakana bamona.
english: The thing which he did was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and he killed him also.

motu: Bena Iuda ese ravana Tamara e hamaoroa, eto, Do ba lou lao, tamamu ena ruma ai ba noho vado, ela bona natugu Sela baine bada. Ena lalo-hadai korikori be Sela danu baine mase, kakana heḡereḡeredia. Taunabunai, Tamara na e lou lao. tamana ena ruma ai e nohova.
english: Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father’s house, until Shelah, my son, is grown up;” for he said, “Lest he also die, like his brothers.” Tamar went and lived in her father’s house.

motu: Nega taina vada ela, bena Sua natuna, hari Iuda e adavaia hahinena, na e mase. Bena Iuda ena lalo-hisihisi e ore ai, ia na e tore isi, Timuna ela; ena mamoe huidia e utu gabuna bunai. Ia turana Hira, tau Adulama, ese e bamoa.
english: After many days, Shua’s daughter, the wife of Judah, died. Judah was comforted, and went up to his sheep shearers to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah, the Adullamite.

motu: Tamara ese ravana harina e kamonai, ia na mamoe huidia iutudia totona Timuna e laova;
english: Tamar was told, “Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

motu: bena ia ese ena vabu dabuadia e doki oho, vairana na dabua amo e ḡovaia, ela, Timuna dalana isena ai e helai dala katakata ai. Badina be ia vada e diba hari Sela vada e tauhau, a tamana na se haheadavadia.
english: She took off the garments of her widowhood, and covered herself with her veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the gate of Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown up, and she wasn’t given to him as a wife.

motu: Bena Iuda ese e itaia, banava ia na ariara hahinena eto, badina be vairana vada e ḡovaia.
english: When Judah saw her, he thought that she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

motu: Bena ia ese e hereva henia, eto, Mani aita eno bou. Ia na asi dibana hahine na ia ravana. Bena hahine na eto, Davagu be dahaka ba henigu?
english: He turned to her by the way, and said, “Please come, let me come in to you,” for he didn’t know that she was his daughter-in-law. She|strong="H1931" * said, “ What|strong="H4100" * will|strong="H5414" * you|strong="H3588" * give|strong="H5414" * me|strong="H5414" *, that|strong="H3588" * you|strong="H3588" * may|strong="H4994" * come|strong="H3051" * in|strong="H1870" * to|strong="H5414" * me|strong="H5414" *?”

motu: Ia eto, Nani natuna ta baina henimu. Hahine na eto, Toana be dahaka ba henigu ela bona ba siaia?
english: He said, “I will send you a young goat from the flock.” She|strong="H5704" * said, “ Will|strong="H5414" * you|strong="H5414" * give|strong="H5414" * me|strong="H5414" * a|strong="H3068" * pledge|strong="H6162" *, until|strong="H5704" * you|strong="H5414" * send|strong="H7971" * it|strong="H5414" *?”

motu: Ia ma eto, Dahaka bavabia o tomu? Hahine na eto, Imamu kwakikwakina vaḡivaḡina bona emu gana bona emu itotohi. E henia, bena raruosi e eno bou; gabeai hahine na e rogorogo.
english: He said, “What pledge will I give you?” She|strong="H4100" * said, “ Your|strong="H5414" * signet|strong="H2368" * and|strong="H3027" * your|strong="H5414" * cord|strong="H6616" *, and|strong="H3027" * your|strong="H5414" * staff|strong="H4294" * that|strong="H5414" * is|strong="H4100" * in|strong="H3027" * your|strong="H5414" * hand|strong="H3027" *.” He|strong="H5414" * gave|strong="H5414" * them|strong="H5414" * to|strong="H5414" * her|strong="H5414" *, and|strong="H3027" * came in|strong="H3027" * to|strong="H5414" * her|strong="H5414" *, and|strong="H3027" * she|strong="H4100" * conceived|strong="H2029" * by|strong="H3027" * him|strong="H5414" *.

motu: Hahine na e tore isi, ela, vairana e ḡovalaia dabuana e negea, ena vabu dabuadia e doki lou.
english: She arose, and went away, and put off her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.

motu: Iuda ese turana Hira e siaia, nani natuna baine laohaia, bona toa gaudia hahine vada e henia ma baine abi lou. To ia na lasihia.
english: Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend, the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman’s hand, but he didn’t find her.

motu: Bena ia ese una gabu taudia e nanadaidia, eto, Hari ariara hahinena dala katakata ai e helaiva be edeseni ai? Idia eto, Ariara hahinena ta lasi iniseni ai.
english: Then he asked the men of her place, saying, “Where is the prostitute, that was at Enaim by the road?” They|strong="H3808" * said, “ There|strong="H1961" * has|strong="H1961" * been|strong="H1961" * no|strong="H3808" * prostitute here|strong="H2088" *.”

motu: Taunabunai, ia na Iuda dekena e lou lao, eto, Asina davaria, bona una gabu taudia e tomu ariara hahinena ta lasi unuseni ai.
english: He returned to Judah, and said, “I haven’t found her; and also the men of the place said, ‘There has been no prostitute here.’”

motu: Bena Iuda eto, Egu ḡau ia dekenai bae mia, baita hemarai garina; nani natuna na siaia, to hahinena na so davaria.
english: Judah said, “Let her keep it, lest we be shamed. Behold, I sent this young goat, and you haven’t found her.”

motu: Hua toi vada ela, bena Iuda ese harina e kamonai ia ravana Tamara na mai bogana. Bena ia eto, A hakaua lasi, lahi ai do baine mase.
english: About three months later, Judah was told, “Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has played the prostitute. Moreover, behold, she is with child by prostitution.” Judah|strong="H3063" * said|strong="H3318" *, “ Bring|strong="H3318" * her|strong="H5046" * out|strong="H3318" *, and|strong="H3063" * let|strong="H5046" * her|strong="H5046" * be|strong="H1961" * burned|strong="H8313" *.”

motu: E hakaua lasi, bena ia ese hereva e siaia ravana enai, eto, Ini ḡau biagudia ese e harogorogogu; mani a hereva, ina ima-kwakikwaki vaḡivaḡina, ina gana, ina itotohi be daika ena?
english: When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “I am with child by the man who owns these.” She also said, “Please discern whose these are—the signet, and the cords, and the staff.”

motu: Bena Iuda ese e gwauraia hedinarai, eto, Iena kara maoromaoro ese lauegu e hereaiamu, badina be natugu Sela ida asina haheadavadia. Bena ia ida se eno bou lou.
english: Judah acknowledged them, and said, “She is more righteous than I, because I didn’t give her to Shelah, my son.” He|strong="H3588" * knew|strong="H3045" * her|strong="H5414" * again|strong="H5750" * no|strong="H3808" * more|strong="H3254" *.

motu: Ena mara negana vada e kahira-kahira, vada e diba hekapa na bogana ai.
english: In the time of her travail, behold, twins were in her womb.

motu: Bena e mara negana ai, mero ta imana e toia lasi, bena hegwaroto hahinena ese varo kakakakana ta imana ai e kwatua, eto, Roboana binai.
english: When she travailed, one put out a hand, and the midwife took and tied a scarlet thread on his hand, saying, “This came out first.”

motu: A mero na imana ma e veria vareai, bena tadina e vara guna. Hegwaroto hahinena na eto, Oi na dala vada o lailaia. Bena ladana e hatoa Perese. + 38:29 “Perese” anina be “dala ilailaina”. *
english: As he drew back his hand, behold, his brother came out, and she said, “Why have you made a breach for yourself?” Therefore his name was called Perez. + 38:29 Perez means “breaking out”. *

motu: Bena kakana e vara; ia ladana e hatoa Sera.
english: Afterward his brother came out, who had the scarlet thread on his hand, and his name was called Zerah. + 38:30 Zerah means “scarlet” or “brightness”. *

motu: Iosef na Aigupto e laohaia, unuseni ai Aigupto tauna ta, lohia ta Farao ena ruma ai, ladana Potifara, ese e hoia, hari Ismael taudia, e hakaua lao taudia, edia amo.
english: Joseph was brought down to Egypt. Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites that had brought him down there.

motu: A Iehova ese Iosef e haḡerea, bena vada e namo: ia ese biaguna, Aigupto tauna, ena ruma ai e nohova.
english: Yahweh was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man. He was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

motu: Bena biaguna ese e itaia, Iehova ese e bamoava bona ena kara iboudiai anidia e havara;
english: His master saw that Yahweh was with him, and that Yahweh made all that he did prosper in his hand.

motu: ena hesiai ḡaukaradia danu vada e ita, vada e namo herea. Bena ia ese ena ruma ita-taona tauna ai e halaoa, ena kohu idoinai baine reḡua.
english: Joseph found favor in his sight. He ministered to him, and Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

motu: Bena ena ruma ita-taona bona ena kohu ireḡuna tauna ai e halaoa dinana amo Iehova ese Aigupto tauna e hanamoa, Iosef dainai: Iehova ena hahenamo na ena ruma latanai bona ena uma latadiai e miava.
english: From the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, Yahweh blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake. Yahweh’s blessing was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.

motu: Ena ḡau idoidiai Iosef imana ai e ato: ḡau ta se laloa, ana aniani vairanai e dabaraia mo, vadaeni. Hari Iosef na raho-namo merona.
english: He left all that he had in Joseph’s hand. He didn’t concern himself with anything, except for the food which he ate. Joseph|strong="H3130" * was|strong="H1961" * well-built and|strong="H3027" * handsome|strong="H3303" *.

motu: Bena nega ta ia biaguna adavana ese e ḡahusia, bena e hamaoroa, eto, Aita eno bou.
english: After these things, his master’s wife set her eyes on Joseph; and she said, “Lie with me.”

motu: A Iosef na se ura; e haere henia, eto, Vada o itaia, biagugu na egu ḡaukara ruma ai se itaia taomu, ena kohu idoinai danu lau imagu ai vada e atoa.
english: But he refused, and said to his master’s wife, “Behold, my master doesn’t know what is with me in the house, and he has put all that he has into my hand.

motu: Tau ta se hereagumu ina ruma ai; egu ai ḡau ta se ruamu, oi mo e rumumu, badina be oi na ia adavana. Ina kerere badana baina karaia, Dirava vairanai baina kara havara, be edeheto?
english: No one is greater in this house than I am, and he has not kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”

motu: A hahine ese dina ta ta amo Iosef lalona e ania, raruosi bae eno bou eto; to ia ese se kamonai heniava.
english: As she spoke to Joseph day by day, he didn’t listen to her, to lie by her, or to be with her.

motu: Nega ta, ia na ruma lalonai e raka vareai; ruma na asi tauna.
english: About this time, he went into the house to do his work, and there were none of the men of the house inside.

motu: Bena hahine ese ena dabua e dogoa tao, e veria, eto, Aoma, aita eno bou. A ia ese ena dabua na hahine imana ai e rakatania, ruma amo e heau lasi.
english: She caught him by his garment, saying, “Lie with me!” He|strong="H3027" * left|strong="H5800" * his|strong="H3027" * garment in|strong="H7901" * her|strong="H3318" * hand|strong="H3027" *, and|strong="H3027" * ran|strong="H5127" * outside|strong="H2351" *.

motu: Hahine na e itaia, ena dabua na ia imana ai vada e rakatania, vada e heau lasi:
english: When she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and had run outside,

motu: bena ia ese ruma taudia e boiridia, e hamaorodia, eto, O itaia, ia ese ina Heberu tauna vada e abia dae, ita ihakavakavada. Ia na lau dekegu ai e raka vareai, baia eno bou eto: na lolo,
english: she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying, “Behold, he has brought a Hebrew in to us to mock us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.

motu: bena gadogu e kamonai negana ai ena dabua na imagu ai e rakatania, e heau lasi.
english: When he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”

motu: Bena hahine na hari dabua e dogoa tao ela bona Iosef biaguna ema.
english: She laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.

motu: Bena ma e hamaoroa, eto, Ina Heberu tauna eda ruma ai o abia dae, eda hesiai ilao-henina, na egu ai e raka vareai, baine hakavakavagu eto;
english: She spoke to him according to these words, saying, “The Hebrew servant, whom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me,

motu: bena na lolo negana ai ia ese ena dabua e rakatania, e heau lasi.
english: and as I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”

motu: Ruma tauna ese adavana ena hereva e kamonai, ena hesiai tauna unu vada e kara toma eto, bena e badu dikadika.
english: When his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what your servant did to me,” his wrath was kindled.

motu: Bena Iosef biaguna ese Iosef e dabaia tao, dibura rumana ai e koua, hanua pavapavana ena iḡui taudia e koudia gabuna ai. Bena dibura rumana ai e nohova.
english: Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.

motu: A Iehova ese Iosef e haḡerea, e bogaia hisi, dibura rumana igimana tauna lalona e hanamoa ia enai.
english: But Yahweh was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

motu: Bena dibura rumana igimana tauna ese dibura taudia iboudiai na Iosef henunai e atodia, edia ḡaukara iboudiai Iosef ese e reḡudia.
