english: The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.

motu: Dibura rumana igimana tauna ese ḡau ta se laloa ena hereḡu ai; badina be Iehova ese Iosef e hagerea, bona ena ḡaukara iboudiai anidia e havara.
english: The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because Yahweh was with him; and that which he did, Yahweh made it prosper.

motu: Ini ḡau muridiai, vine ranuna iseina memerodia ireḡudia tauna bona flaoa igabuna memerodia ireḡudia tauna Farao ena ruma ai na raruosi ese Farao e habadua.
english: After these things, the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

motu: Bena Farao ese ena hesiai taudia raruosi, hari vine ranuna iseina memerodia bona flaoa igabuna memerodia ireḡudia taudia, na e badu henidia,
english: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cup bearer and the chief baker.

motu: dibura rumana ai e koudia, hegima taudia biagudia imana ai, Iosef e nohova gabuna ai.
english: He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.

motu: Bena hegima taudia biagudia ese Iosef e hamaoroa, baine naridia; bena ia ese raruosi e naridia. Idia na nega taina daudau dibura rumana ai e nohova.
english: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.

motu: Unu tatau raruosi na hanuaboi tamona ai e nihi: Farao ena vine ranuna iseina memerodia iregudia tauna bona ena flaoa igabuna memerodia ireḡudia tauna na ta ta ena nihi ena nihi e nihirai, dibura rumana ai.
english: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.

motu: Daba ai, Iosef na e raka vareai, idia raruosi dekediai, bena toadia e ita, lalodia e hisihisiva.
english: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.

motu: Bena ia ese hari Farao ena hesiai taudia, ia ida e dibura hebouva taudia, e nanadaidia, eto, Badina be dahaka vairamui o huamu?
english: He asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”

motu: Idia eto, Ai na vada a nihi, bona asi tauna ta ese emai nihi anidia baine hahedinarai. Bena Iosef eto, Nihi anidia ihahedinaraidia na Dirava mo sibona: emui nihi mani a gwaurai hedinarai.
english: They said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it.” Joseph|strong="H3130" * said to|strong="H3808" * them|strong="H4994" *, “Don’t interpretations|strong="H6623" * belong to|strong="H3808" * God|strong="H3808" *? Please|strong="H4994" * tell|strong="H5608" * it|strong="H3808" * to|strong="H3808" * me|strong="H4994" *.”

motu: Bena vine ranuna iseina memerodia ireḡudia tauna ese ena nihi Iosef e hahedinarai henia, eto, Egu nihi ai vine auna ta na itaia;
english: The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,

motu: rigina na toi. Bena e gara kau, burena e vara, huahuana e dobi.
english: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.

motu: Farao ena kehere na imagu ai, bena vine huahuadia na abi, bena na gigi, ranuna na Farao ena kehere ai e diho. Bena kehere na Farao imana ai na atoa.
english: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”

motu: Bena Iosef eto, Emu nihi anina binai: vine rigi toiosi be dina toi.
english: Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.

motu: Dina toi baela, bena Farao ese baine abimu dae, dagimu baine henimu lou; bena Farao ena kehere na imana ai do bavatoa, gunaguna ena vine ranuna iseina memerodia o reḡudiava negana ai heḡereḡerena.
english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cup bearer.

motu: A oiemu dala baine namo negana ai ba lalogu, ani? Ba bogagu hisi, Farao ba hereva henia daigu ai, ina dibura rumana amo ba hakaugu lasi.
english: But remember me when it is well with you. Please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.

motu: Badina be momokani lau na Heberu taudia edia tano ai e abigu mauri; iniseni ai danu kerere ta asina karaia, a dibura rumana ai e kougu kava.
english: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”

motu: Flaoa igabuna memerodia ireḡudia tauna vada e diba hari nihi anina be namo, bena ia ese Iosef e hamaoroa, eto, Lau danu na nihi; egu nihi lalonai flaoa boseadia toi kwaragu ai na ato, na oradia loaloa;
english: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.

motu: bena atai boseana lalonai na flaoa e gabu ḡaudia idau-idau mimia, Farao ana, a manu haida e roho ema, e ani.
english: In the uppermost basket there were all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”

motu: Bena Iosef eto, Emu nihi anina binai: bosea toiosi be dina toi.
english: Joseph answered, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.

motu: Dina toi baela, bena Farao ese dibura rumana amo baine abimu, au ta ai baine taumu dae, bena manu bae roho mai, tau-animu bae ania.
english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.”

motu: Dina ihatoina be Farao ena vara dinana, bena ia ese aria ta e karaia, ena hesiai taudia iboudiai e vavedia; hari vine ranuna iseina memerodia ireḡudia tauna bona flaoa igabuna memerodia ireḡudia tauna danu e vavedia.
english: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

motu: Bena vine ranuna iseina memerodia ireḡudia tauna ena dagi e henia lou; ia ese kehere Farao imana ai ma e atoa.
english: He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;

motu: A flaoa igabuna memerodia ireḡudia tauna na e taua dae ela bona e mase, Iosef ena hereva heḡereḡerena.
english: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.

motu: A hari vine ranuna iseina memerodia ireḡudia tauna ese Iosef se laloa tao; e laloa boio.
english: Yet the chief cup bearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.

motu: Laḡani rua vada e lao bubuni, bena Farao e nihi. Ena nihi ai ia na sinavai badana isena ai e gini.
english: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.

motu: Bena boromakau hitu sinavai badana amo e dae, taudia nanamo bona mai digaradia, sinavai isena ai e anianiva.
english: Behold, seven cattle came up out of the river. They were sleek and fat, and they fed in the marsh grass.

motu: Idia muridiai boromakau idaudia hitu sinavai badana amo ma e dae, taudia didika bona vavaroda-vavaroda, hari mai digaradia ḡaudia badibadidiai e gini.
english: Behold, seven other cattle came up after them out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.

motu: Bena hari boromakau varoda-varodadia hituosi ese boromakau mai digaradia hituosi e anidia ore. Bena Farao na e noga.
english: The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.

motu: Ma e mahuta lou, e nihi. Ena nihi iharuana ai ia ese uit tuhutuhuna tamona amo anidia hitu e tubu e itadia, unu uit anidia be nanamo bona babada.
english: He slept and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, healthy and good.

motu: Idia muridiai uit tuhutuhuna ta amo anidia hitu ma e tubu, unu uit anidia be didika bona mamaraḡi, lai mairiveina ese e hamarai ḡaudia.
english: Behold, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

motu: Bena hari uit anidia dikadia ese uit anidia namodia e anidia ore. Bena Farao na e noga, vada e diba nihi mo.
english: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

motu: Daba ai kudouna e hetaha; bena ia na e hesiai, Aigupto ai babalau taudia iboudiai bona aonega taudia iboudiai e boiridia. Bena Farao ese ena nihi e hamaorolaidia, to idia iboudiai na anidia igwauraidia asi dibadia.
english: In the morning, his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt’s magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.

motu: Bena vine ranuna iseina memerodia ireḡudia tauna ese Farao e hamaoroa, eto, Lau ese egu kerere hari name laloa.
english: Then the chief cup bearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my faults today.

motu: Farao ese ena hesiai taudia e badu henidia negana ai na lau bona flaoa igabuna memerodia ireḡudia tauna raruosi dibura rumana igimana tauna imana ai o atomai.
english: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, with the chief baker.

motu: Bena hanuaboi ai raruosi a nihi, ta ta ena nihi ena nihi na mai anidia.
english: We dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each man dreamed according to the interpretation of his dream.

motu: Tau eregabe ta be dekemai ai, ia na tau Heberu, dibura rumana igimana tauna ena hesiai merona. Bena ai raruosi emai nihi a hamaorolaia; bena anidia ia ese e hadibamai, ta ta ena nihi ena nihi anidia.
english: There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. He interpreted to each man according to his dream.

motu: Taunabunai, nihi anidia ia ese e gwaurai vada e momokani: lau be o halougu egu dagi ai, a bamogu be e taua dae ela bona e mase.
english: As he interpreted to us, so it was. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”

motu: Bena Farao e hesiai, Iosef eha boiria. Bena idia ese dibura rumana amo e hakaua lasi haraḡa-haraḡa; ia ese aukina huina e abia bona ena dabuae boloa, bena Farao dekenai e raka vareai.
english: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.

motu: Bena Farao ese Iosef e hereva henia, eto, Vada na nihi, to nihi anina ihahedinaraina be asi tauna; a harimu vada na kamonai, nihi anidia ihahedinaraidia na mai dibamu.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”

motu: Iosef ese Farao e haere henia, eto, Dia lau, a Dirava ese Farao baine haere henia, maino herevana ai.
english: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It isn’t in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”

motu: Bena Farao ese Iosef e hamaoroa, eto, Egu nihi ai sinavai badana badibadinai na gini;
english: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river;

motu: bena boromakau hitu na sinavai amo e dae, taudia nanamo bona mai digaradia, bena sinavai isena ai e anianiva.
english: and behold, seven fat and sleek cattle came up out of the river. They fed in the marsh grass;

motu: Gabeamo boromakau idaudia hitu ma e dae, taudia didika bona vavaroda-vavaroda, Aigupto tanona idoinai boromakau dikadia unuhetomadia na hata asina itadia.
english: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

motu: Bena boromakau dikadia mai varoda-varodadia ese boromakau mai digaradia hituosi e dae guna ḡaudia na e anidia ore;
english: The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle;

motu: ḡau tamona, e anidia ore murinai tau ta basinema diba idia ese vada e anidia, badina be idia na dounu varoda-varoda. Bena na noga.
english: and when they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

motu: Bena egu nihi ta ai, uit tuhutuhuna tamona na itaia, e tubu mai anina hitu, babada bona nanamo;
english: I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good;

motu: gabeai ta ma e tubu anina hitu, didika bona mamaraḡi, lai mairiveina ese e hamarai ḡaudia.
english: and behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

motu: Bena uit dikadia ese uit namodia e anidia ore. Lau ese babalau taudia vada na hamaorolaidia, to anina ihahedinaraina na ta asi dibana.
english: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”

motu: Bena Iosef ese Farao e hamaoroa, eto, Farao ena nihi be tamona mo; Dirava ese ena kara ta baine karaia e tomu be Farao vada e hamaorolaia guna.
english: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.

motu: Boromakau namodia hituosi be l=agani hitu, bona uit anidia namodia hituosi be laḡani hitu: nihi na tamona mo.
english: The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.

motu: Boromakau hituosi dikadia mai varoda-varodadia gabeai e dae ḡaudia be laḡani hitu, bona uit anidiadikadia hituosi, lai mairiveina ese e hamarai ḡaudia, idia danu laḡani hitu, doe laḡanidia.
english: The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; they will be seven years of famine.

motu: Farao hari na hamaoroa heḡereḡerena, Dirava ese ena kara ta baine karaia e tomu be Farao vada e hamaorolaia guna.
english: That is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.

motu: Laḡani hitu be gini daemu, Aigupto tanona idoinai baine madinamo;
english: Behold, seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt are coming.

motu: gabeamo doe laḡanidia hitu do bae gini dae, madinamo idoinai Aigupto tanona ai do bae laloa boio, badina be doe baine bada herea.
english: Seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,

motu: Taunimanima ese madinamo negana na basie laloa une, doe bada lalonai bae dabu vaitani dainai.
english: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.

motu: Farao na harua e nihi, badina be Dirava ese ina ḡau vada e gwauraia, bona asi vanahana ia ese baine havaraia.
english: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.

motu: Namona binai: Farao ese lalo-parara bona aonega tauna ta baine tahua, Aigupto tanona biaguna ai baine halaoa.
english: “Now therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.

motu: Farao na unu baine kara toma, bona tano ita-taona taudia baine gwauraidia danu: unu madinamo laḡanidia ai aniani ḡaudia iboudiai ina Aigupto tanona ai bae karoadia, karoa ima, bena karoa ta roge ai bae haboua.
english: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.

motu: Madi-namo laḡanidia anianidia iboudiai bae habou, Farao imana ai, bae mia, hanua hanua lalodiai.
english: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and store grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.

motu: Una aniani na roge ai baine mia ela bona doe laḡanidia hituosi na Aigupto ai bae gini dae; bena ina tano taunimanimadia na basie hitolo mase.
english: The food will be to supply the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; so that the land will not perish through the famine.”

motu: Farao mai ena hesiai taudia ida ese una hereva e abia dae.
english: The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.

motu: Bena Farao ese ena hesiai taudia e hereva henidia, eto, Edeseni ai tau ta baita davaria ina tau heḡereḡerena: Dirava ena Lauma be ia lalonai ani?
english: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”

motu: Bena Farao ese Iosef e hereva henia, eto, Dirava ese ina idoinai vada e hahedinarai henimu, bona asi tauna ta mai ena lalo-parara bona mai ena aonega oi heḡereḡeremu.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Because God has shown you all of this, there is no one so discreet and wise as you.

motu: Una dainai, oi ese egu ruma ba halohiaia, egu basileia idoinai oi eremu bae kamonai; lau hanua pavapavana taugu mo ese oi baina hereamu.
english: You shall be over my house. All my people will be ruled according to your word. Only in the throne I will be greater than you.”

motu: Farao ese Iosef ma e hereva henia, eto, A kamonai lau ese Aigupto tanona idoinai lohiana ai name halaomu.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”

motu: Bena Farao ese ia imana kwakikwakina vaḡivaḡina imana amo e abia, Iosef imana kwakikwakina ai e toia vareai; dabua namo-hereadia danu e hahedokilai, bona gold * agevana na aiona ai e atoa kau.
english: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

motu: E haduaia danu, kariota iharuana, iena kariota murinai e heauva ḡauna, latanai baine gui. Haida danu ia vairanai e heau, e boiboi, eto, Dala a lailaia. Unuhetomana ia ese Aigupto tanona idoinai lohiana ai e halaoa.
english: He made him ride in the second chariot which he had. They cried before him, “Bow the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.

motu: Bena Farao ese Iosef e hamaoroa, eto, Lau binai Farao; oi basio hereva negana ai tau ta ese kara ta basine karaia ina Aigupto tanona idoinai.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh. Without you, no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”

motu: Bena Farao ese Iosef ladana e hatoa Safenat-panea; Asenat danu e henia, baine adavaia; una Asenat na Ono ena hahelaḡa tauna, ladana Potifera, natuna. Bena Iosef na Aigupto tanona idoinai e rakaia hanai. Iosef Aigupto lohiana
english: Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

motu: Iosef ena mauri laḡanidia na toi-ahui, ia Farao, Aigupto pavapavana, vairanai e gini negana ai. Bena Iosef na Farao vairana amo e raka lasi, Aigupto tanona idoinai e rakaia hanai.
english: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.

motu: Bena madinamo laḡanidia hituosi lalodiai uma anidia vada e bada herea.
english: In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.

motu: Unu laḡani hitu lalodiai Iosef ese aniani idoinai e haboua, hanua hanua rogedia ai. Hanua ta ta umadia anianidia na unu hanua ta ta rogedia ai e habou.
english: He gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities. He stored food in each city from the fields around that city.

motu: Taunabunai, Iosef ese uit e habou, kone mirina na heto, ela bona iduahina e hadokoa, badina be asi iduahina dalana.
english: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.

motu: Doe negana na do se gini dae ai, Iosef natuna mamaruanedia rarua e vara, Asenat, Ono ena hahelaḡa tauna Potifera natuna, bogana amo.
english: To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.

motu: Roboana na Iosef ese ladana e hatoa Manase; + 41:51 “Manase” anina be “Helalo-boio”. * eto, Dirava ese egu hekwarahi bona tamagu ena ruma ilalolaidia na egu amo vada e abi oho.
english: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, + 41:51 “Manasseh” sounds like the Hebrew for “forget”. * “For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”

motu: A tau muritai ladana e hatoa Efraim; + 41:52 “Efraim” anina be “Anina na momo”. * eto, Hisi na ani tanona ai Dirava ese besegu vada e henigu.
english: The name of the second, he called Ephraim: + 41:52 “Ephraim” sounds like the Hebrew for “twice fruitful”. * “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”

motu: Madinamo laḡanidia hituosi vada e ore Aigupto ai,
english: The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, came to an end.

motu: bena doe laḡanidia gini-gunana vada e gini dae, Iosef ena hereva heḡereḡerena. Bena tano idau-idau iboudiai lalodiai taunimanima e hitolodiava; a Aigupto ai aniani na mia.
english: The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

motu: Bena Aigupto tanona idoinai taunimanima e hitolodiava ai idia ese Farao e tai henia, aniani baine henidia. Bena Farao ese e hamaorodia, eto, Iosef dekena aola, ia ede baine hamaoromui toma vada ba karaia.
english: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”

motu: Tanobada idoinai doe vada e bada. Bena Iosef ese ena roge iboudiai e keho, Aigupto taudia ese aniani e hoia, moni davana; badina be doe na bada herea Aigupto tanona ai.
english: The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.

motu: Bena tano idau-idau iboudiai amo e hesiai ela, Aigupto ai aniani e hoi, Iosef dekenai; badina be doe na bada herea, tanobada idoinai.
english: All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.

motu: Iakob ese harina e kamonai Aigupto be mai uitina, bena ia ese natuna e gwau henidia, eto, Badina be dahaka o herarai hehenimu?
english: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”

motu: Ma eto, Vada na kamonaimu Aigupto be mai uitina; baola, unuseni ai ita ada ba hoia, baita mauri helaoreana; bena basita mase.
english: He said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”

motu: Bena Iosef kakana gwauta-osi Aigupto ela, uit ihoina;
english: Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

motu: a Beniamina, Iosef tadina, na Iakob ese e rua, kakana ida basinela; badina be ia eto, Dika ese bema butua tao na garina.
english: But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he said, “Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”

motu: Taunabunai, Israel natuna na taunimanima loḡora ida uit ihoina ela; badina be doe na bada Kanaan tanona ai.
english: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

motu: Iosef na tano idoinai lohiana, taunabunai taunimanima iboudiai ia dekena ela, uit e hoia. Iosef kakana danu ia dekena ela, ia vairanai e goru diho.
english: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.

motu: Iosef ese kakana e itadia negana ai, ia lalona vada e parara idia be daidia, to e hereva henidia idau tauna na heto, e gwau henidia, eto, Umui be ede amo oma? Idia eto, Kanaan tanona amo ama, aniani ihoina totona.
english: Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?” They|strong="H3667" * said|strong="H1696" *, “ From|strong="H7200" * the|strong="H7200" * land of|strong="H1696" * Canaan|strong="H3667" *, to|strong="H1696" * buy|strong="H7666" * food.”

motu: Iosef be kakana dibana, to idia asi dibadia ia.
english: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.

motu: Bena Iosef ese ena nihi ai idia e nihiraidia e helalolai une. Bena e gwau henidia, eto, Umui na hasinadoa taumui; ina tano ena manoka itana oma.
english: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”

motu: Idia ese e haere henia, eto, Ḡaubada e, lasi, dia unuheto; ai na oi isiaimu ilao-henina taumai, aniani ihoina totona ama.
english: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.

motu: Ai na tau tamona natuna, hereva momokani taumai; asia hasinadoamu.
english: We are all one man’s sons; we are honest men. Your servants are not spies.”

motu: A ia ese ma e gwau henidia, eto, Lasi, tano ena manoka itana totona oma.
english: He said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”

motu: Idia ma eto, Ai na oi isiaimu ilao-henina taumai, tadikaka gwauta-rarua, tau tamona natuna Kanaan ai; a tau-muritai be harihari tamamai dekenai, bona ta be vada e mase.
english: They said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is today with our father, and one is no more.”

motu: A Iosef eto, Vada na hereva, ani, umui be hasinadoa taumui.
english: Joseph said to them, “It is like I told you, saying, ‘You are spies!’

motu: A baina dibamui: Farao maurina ai na herevamu, ini amo basio raka oho ela bona tadimui bainema.
english: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.

motu: Umui emui amo ta ba siaia, tadimui baine hakaua mai; a orena be dibura rumana ai ba noho. Unu amo baina dibamui, emui hereva be momokani eiava lasi. Bema lasi, umui na momokani hasinadoa taumui.
english: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.”

motu: Taunabunai, ia ese dibura rumana ai e koudia, dina toi.
english: He put them all together into custody for three days.

motu: Dina ihatoina ai, Iosef ese e hereva henidia, eto, Ini ba kara toma, bena ba mauri; badina be lau danu Dirava garina na garimu.
english: Joseph said to them the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.

motu: Bema umui na hereva momokani taumui, umui ta ese dibura rumana ai baine noho, a orena be vada baola, uit ba laohaia, varavaramui adia.
english: If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.

motu: Bena ba lou mai, tadimui ba hakaua mai dekegu ai; unu amo baina diba emui hereva na momokani, bena basio mase. Unu ba kara toma.
english: Bring your youngest brother to me; so will your words be verified, and you won’t die.” They|strong="H3651" * did|strong="H6213" * so|strong="H3651" *.

motu: Bena idia na e hereva heheni, eto, Momokani, ita na vada ta kerere tadida dainai; badina be ena taitai ta kamonai, to ena noinoi asita abia dae; una dainai ina hekwarahi na ita edai vada e kau.
english: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”

motu: Bena Ruben eto, Lau na hamaoromui, ani, nato “Mero na basio hadikaia”, to umui na asio kamonai, harihari ia rarana na ita latadai.
english: Reuben answered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘Don’t sin against the child,’ and you wouldn’t listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.”

motu: Idia na asi dibadia Iosef na edia hereva anidia dibana, badina be ia na gado-hanai tauna uduna amo mo vada e hereva henidia.
english: They didn’t know that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.

motu: Bena ia na e raka siri, e tai; gabeamo e lou henidia, e hereva henidia. Bena ia ese Simeon e abia, gadea amo e ḡuia idia vairadiai.
english: He turned himself away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.

motu: Bena Iosef e hahedua, edia puse na uit amo bae hahonu, bona ta ta edia moni edia puse ai bae uda lou, bona dala lakwana danu bae henidia. Bena unu e kara toma.
english: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.

motu: Bena edia puse na edia doniki dorudia ai e ato kau, e raka lao.
english: They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.

motu: Adorahi ai e taruha, bena ta ese ena puse e kehoa, ena doniki baine ubua eto; bena ena moni e itaia, puse uduna ai.
english: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

motu: Bena ia ese tadikakana e hamaorodia, eto, Egu moni vada e haloua, ḡauna na egu puse ai. Bena kudoudia e hetaha, gari ese e butudia tao, e hereva heheni, eto, Dirava na ede vada e karada toma?
english: He said to his brothers, “My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!” Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”

motu: Kanaan tanona ai e kau, tamadia Iakob dekenai. Bena edia laolao sivaraina e hamaorolaia, eto,
english: They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,

motu: Una tano lohiana ese e daḡedaḡe henimai, dibura rumana ai e koumai, eto ai na hasinadoa taumai.
english: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.

motu: A ia ese a hamaoroa, ato “Ai na hereva momokani taumai, dia hasinadoa;
english: We said to him, ‘We are honest men. We are no spies.

motu: ai na tadikaka gwauta-rarua, tau tamona natuna, a ta vada e mase, bona taumuritai be tamamai dekenai, Kanaan tanona ai.”
english: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Canaan.’

motu: Bena una tano lohiana eto “Ini amo baina diba umui na hereva momokani taumui eiava lasi: umui ta baina dogoa tao iniseni ai, a orena be uit ba laohaia, varavaramui adia;
english: The man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way.

motu: bena tadimui tau-muritai tauna ba hakaua mai dekegu ai, bena bainadiba umui be hereva momokani taumui; bena tadikakamui na baina henimui lou, bona ina tano ai ba hoihoi danu”.
english: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”

motu: Bena uit na edia puse amo e bubua negana ai, ta ta edia moni e davari edia puse ai; bena idia bona tamadia moni e itaia ai e gari dikadika.
english: As they emptied their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.

motu: Bena tamadia Iakob ese e gwau henidia, eto, Natugu na egu amo vada o abidia oho: Iosef vada e boio; Simeon vada e boio; harihari Beniamina danu bavabia oho o tomu; ini hisihisi iboudiai na lau mo latagu ai.
english: Jacob, their father, said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.”

motu: Bena Ruben ese tamana e hamaoroa, eto, Beniamina basina hakaua lou dekemu ai, lau natugu raruosi bavaladia mase. Lau imagu ai ba siaia, bena lau ese ma baina mailaia mai maurina ida.
english: Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “Kill my two sons, if I don’t bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him to you again.”

motu: A Iakob eto, Natugu basina kahua nege, basio laohaia; badina be kakana korikori vada e mase, ia mo sibona dekegu ai e nohomu. Dala ai dika ta ienai bema kau, lau buruka taugu na umui daimui ai mase gabuna bama lao henia mai lalo-hisihisigu ida.
english: He said, “My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.” + 42:38 Sheol is the place of the dead. *

motu: Tano idoinai hitolo na bada herea.
english: The famine was severe in the land.

motu: Aigupto amo e mailaia uitina vada e ania ore, bena tamadia ese e hamaorodia, eto, Ma baola, aniani taina ba ha hoia ada.
english: When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”

motu: Bena Iuda ese e haere henia, eto, Una tau ena hereva na auka, eto “Tadimui basio hakaua mai, lau vairagu basio itaia”.
english: Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’

motu: Taunabunai, tadimai ba siaia, ai ida baiala, aniani baia ha hoia amu;
english: If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food;

motu: a basio siaia, ai na basiala, badina be una tau eto “Tadimui basio hakaua mai, lau vairagu basio itaia”.
english: but if you don’t send him, we won’t go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’”

motu: Bena Israel eto, Edeheto umui ese lau o hadikagu, tadimui herevana o hahedinaraia?
english: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”

motu: Idia eto, Una tau ese e nanadaimai malakamalaka, eda iduhu herevadia e nanadailai, eto, “Tamamui dounu e mauri nohomu?” bona “Tadimui ta noho?” Bena ai ese a haere henia. Ede baiama diba toma ia baineto “Tadimui ba hakaua mai” a?
english: They said, “The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”

motu: Bena Iuda ese tamana Israel e noia, eto, Mero na ba siaia, baia tore isi, baiala; unu amo baita mauri, basita mase, oi bona natumai maraḡidia danu.
english: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.

motu: Lau ese do baina naria; lau dekegu ai ba tahua. Basinama loulaia dekemu ai, vairamu ai basinama hakaua, kerere na lau latagu ai bema mia hanaihanai.
english: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;

motu: Basiama halahe, ina laolao iharuana harihari baiama haḡuḡurua.
english: for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now.”

motu: Bena tamadia Israel ese e haere henidia, eto, Bema dala idauna ta lasi, ini ba kara toma: eda tano anidia namo-hereadia bavabi kau, emui maduna ai, muramura mai bonadia, bada ranuna, aniani ihanamodia muramuradia, au-huahuadia aukadia, una tau ena.
english: Their father, Israel, said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;

motu: Moni ikumidia rua rua danu bavabi kau; emui puse ai e uda lou monidia danu ba loulai, badina be e uda taudia na e kerere readia.
english: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.

motu: Tadimui danu ba hakaua lao, una tau do ba lou henia.
english: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.

motu: Siahu-idoinai Diravana ese baine bogamui hisi una tau vairanai baine durumui, bena ia ese tadikakamui ta baine ruhaia nege, bona Beniamina danu baine haloua. A natugu na egu ai bae boio, vadaeni, vada bae boio.
english: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”

motu: Taunabunai, idia ese herahia e abi kau, tamadia ena hereva heḡereḡerena, bona moni ikumidia rua rua amo, bona Beniamina danu e hakaua. Bena e tore isi, Aigupto tanona ela, Iosef vairanai e gini.
english: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

motu: Iosef ese Beniamina e itaia, bena ena hesiai tauna e haduaia, eto, Ini tatau na ba hakaudia lao egu ruma lalonai; aniani danu ba dabaraia, badina be dina tubua ai idia na lau ida baia aniani hebou.
english: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”

motu: Bena hesiai tauna na Iosef ena hereva heḡereḡerena e hakaudia lao, Iosef ena ruma ai e hakaudia vareai.
english: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.

motu: Bena hari tatau e gari dikadika, Iosef ena ruma ai e hakaudia vareai dainai. Idia na e hereva heheni, eto, Nega gini-gunana ai moni euda lou eda puse ai dainai; ia na ihabadelaida dalana e tahuamu, bena baine ḡuida, ena hesiai ai baine halaoda, eda doniki danu baine abidia iena.
english: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”

motu: Taunabunai idia na Iosef ena hesiai tauna dekena ela, ruma iduarana ai;
english: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,

motu: e hamaoroa, eto, Ḡauka e, nega gini-gunana ama, aniani ihoina moama;
english: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.

motu: to emai taruha gabuna ai a kau, emai puse a keho, bena emai moni a ita, ta ta ena puse ena puse ai e heuda, emai moni idoinai; harihari vada a mailai, baia heni lou a tomu.
english: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.

motu: Bona moni haida danu vada a mailai, aniani ihoilaina. A asi dibamai daika ese emai moni na e uda lou emai puse ai.
english: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”

motu: Bena hari hesiai tauna eto, Maino avabia, basio gari; emui Dirava, tamamui danu ena Dirava, ia ese emui puse e hatagadia; emui moni na lau ese na abi. Bena ia ese Simeon e hakaua lasi dekediai.
english: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.

motu: Bena una hesiai tauna ese ena ruma lalonai e hakaudia vareai, aedia ihurilaidia ranuna e henidia, bona edia doniki danu e ubudia.
english: The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.

motu: Bena edia herahia e heḡaeḡaelai, Iosef dina tubua ai bainema bae henia eto, badina be vada e diba idia na unuseni ai bae aniani.
english: They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.

motu: Iosef e raka vareai, bena e haḡaeḡaelai ḡaudia vada e henia, bona e goru goru diho tano ai, ia vairanai.
english: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to the earth before him.

motu: Bena ia ese e nanadaidia, eto, Umui be edeheto? Tamamui danu namo a, hari tau buruka vanegai sivaraina o gwauraia; ia dounu mauri eiava?
english: He asked them of their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”

motu: Idia na e haere, eto, Emu hesiai tauna ai tamamai be namo, dounu e mauri nohomu. Bena idia na e igo diho, e hanamoa.
english: They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.

motu: Bena ia matana e roha isi, tadina Beniamina e itaia, ia sinana natuna; bena eto, Tadimu tau-muritai benai a, vanegai sivaraina o gwauraia merona? Ma eto, Natugu e, Dirava ese baine bogamu hisi.
english: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”

motu: Bena Iosef lalona e manoka: tadina e bogaia hisi bada dainai ia na e raka vareai ena daiutu lalonai, unuseni ai e tai.
english: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.

motu: Bena vairana e huria, e raka lasi, e haheauka, eto, Aniani a dabaraia.
english: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”

motu: Bena aniani e dabaraia, pata ta ai Iosef ana, pata ta ai idia adia, bona ma pata ta ai Aigupto taudia adia. Badina be Aigupto taudia na Heberu taudia ida basie aniani hebou, mai edia taravatu dainai.
english: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.

motu: Bena edia helai gabudia vada e henidia ia vairanai; edia vara heḡereḡeredia, tau-roboana ela bona tau-muritai. Taunabunai e heita heheni, bona e hoa.
english: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled with one another.

motu: Bena Iosef ese aniani iena pata amo e abia, e siaia dekediai, a Beniamina ana ha-ima e siaia. Vine ranuna danu ia ida e inu hebou.
english: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.

motu: Bena Iosef ese ena ruma ireḡuna tauna e haduaia, eto, Ini tatau edia puse aniani ai ba hahonu, bae honu namonamo, bona edia moni danu edia puse ududia ai ba uda.
english: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.

motu: Bona egu kehere, hari silver * ḡauna, taumuritai ena puse uduna ai ba udaia, bona ena uit ihoilaina monina danu. Bena ia ese Iosef ena hereva heḡereḡerena e karaia.
english: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

motu: Daba ai, hari tatau mai edia doniki e siaidia lao.
english: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.

motu: Hanua e rakatania, a do asie raka daudau ai, Iosef ese ena ruma ireḡuna tauna e haduaia, eto, A tore isi, a ḡavadia; ba lasidia tao negana ai ba gwau henidia, baoto “Badina be dahaka umui ese namo dika vada o davalaia a?
english: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?

motu: Biagugu ena kehere, ena inuinu bona ena baguhaoro ḡauna, vada o henaoa. Umui vada o kerere dikadika”.
english: Isn’t this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”

motu: Taunabunai, ia ese e lasidia tao, bena unu e gwau henidia toma.
english: He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.

motu: Idia ese e haere henia, eto, Dahaka dainai ḡaubada na unu e gwau tomamu? Emu hesiai taudia na unu asia kara toma.
english: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!

motu: O itaia, emai puse ududia ai a davari monidia na a henimu lou, Kanaan amo a lou mai negana ai: benaini, dahaka dainai biagumu ena ruma ai silver * eiava gold * baiama henao?
english: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?

motu: A boma davaria oi isiaimu ilao-henina taumai ta unu vada e kara toma, ia na baine mase, bona ai be biagumui ena hesiai taudia ai baiala.
english: With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”

motu: Bena ia eto, Benaini, ini baita kara toma: ena puse ai baina davaria tauna be egu hesiai tauna ai bainela, a orena be baina kahumui nege.
english: He said, “Now also let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found will be my slave; and you will be blameless.”

motu: Bena ta ta ena puse ena puse e abi dobi haraḡa, e ruha.
english: Then they hurried, and each man took his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.

motu: Bena hari tau ese e hetahu, tau guna enai itahuna e matamaia, ela bona tau-muritai enai e hadokoa. Kehere na Beniamina ena puse ai e davaria.
english: He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

motu: Bena edia dabua e dare, edia doniki madunadia dorudia ai ma e ato kau, hanua e lou lao.
english: Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.

motu: Iuda mai tadikakana ida Iosef ena ruma ai e gini dae negana ai, Iosef na do ruma ai, bena idia ese ia vairanai e goru goru diho.
english: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.

motu: Bena Iosef ese e gwau henidia, eto, Ede vada o kara toma? Umui asio laloa lau na bagu-haoro taugu a?
english: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”

motu: Bena Iuda eto, Egu lohia e, ede baia hereva henimu toma? Ede baia maoro toma oi vairamu ai? Dirava ese emu hesiai taudia emai kerere vada e hahedinaraia; harihari ai na oi imamu ai, ai bona ena puse ai emu kehere e davaria tauna danu.
english: Judah said, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? How will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup is found.”

motu: A Iosef eto, Lasi, unu basina karamui toma; egu kehere e abia tauna hari egu hesiai tauna ai bainela, a umui be tamamui dekena ba lou lao mai mainomui ida.
english: He said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”

motu: Bena Iuda na e raka henia kahi, eto, Mani emu kara lau binai emu hesiai tauna na biagugu baina hereva henimu; mani emu kara emu badu do baine keruma emu hesiai tauna egu ai: badina be oi na Farao heḡereḡerena.
english: Then Judah came near to him, and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.

motu: Egu lohia e, emu hesiai taudia o nanadaimai, oto, “Tamamui eiava tadimui nonoho a?”
english: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’

motu: Bena a haere henimu, ato “Tamamai burukana e nohomu, bona mero ta, tau-badana ai e abia; una mero kakana vada emase, sinana natuna tamona mo na ia, una dainai tamamai ese e lalokau henia badamu”.
english: We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’

motu: Bena oi ese o haḡanimai, oto “Ba hakaua mai, lau baina itaia”.
english: You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’

motu: Bena ai ese a haere henimu, ato “Tamana na basine kahua nege; badina be ia bema raka oho, tamana bema mase”.
english: We said to my lord, ‘The boy can’t leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’

motu: Bena oi ese o hamaoromai, oto “Tadimui tau-muritai basio hakaua mai, lau vairagu basio itaia lou”.
english: You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.’

motu: Bena emu hesiai tauna, ai tamamai, dekena a lou lao, lohia taumu emu hereva a hamaorolaia.
english: When we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

motu: Bena tamamai eto “A lou lao, ada aniani taina ma bavabia”.
english: Our father said, ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’

motu: Bena ai ato “Tadimai tau-muritai na ai ida baiala be vada baiala; badina be tadimai na ai ida basiala, una tau vairana basia itaia lou”.
english: We said, ‘We can’t go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down: for we may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is with us.’

motu: Bena tamamai eto “Umui dibamui adavagu ese memero rarua e abidia;
english: Your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.

motu: ta e rakatanigu, bena nato ‘Ḡau ta ese vada e darea patapata’, bena asina itaia lou ema bona harihari.
english: One went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn in pieces;” and I haven’t seen him since.

motu: A harihari ina ta danu egu ai bavabia oho, bena dika ta ienai baine kau, lau buruka taugu na umui daimui ai mase gabuna bainala mai lalo-hisihisigu ida”.
english: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’ + 44:29 Sheol is the place of the dead. *

motu: Taunabunai, emu hesiai tauna lau tamagu dekena bama lou lao, a mero basinama hakaua lao, bena ia bona hari mero na e kara mauri tamona na heto dainai
english: Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;

motu: ia baine itamai mero na lasihia negana ai ia na baine mase; oibe tamamai tau-buruka na mase gabuna bainela mai lalo-hisihisina ida.
english: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol. + 44:31 Sheol is the place of the dead. *

motu: Badina belau ese tamagu na gwau henia hamata, ina mero bagunai, nato “Basina hakaua lou dekemu ai mai maurina ida, kerere na lau latagu ai baine mia ela bona hanaihanai”.
english: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’

motu: Taunabunai na noimumu, lau ese emu hesiai tauna ai bainala, ina mero ibolona, a ia ese kakana ida bae lou lao.
english: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.

motu: Badina be ede baina haheauka toma, tamagu dekena baina lou lao a mero basina hakaua lao, bena dika tamagu enai baine vara be baina itaia?
english: For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t with me?—lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”

motu: Iosef na badibadinai e gini taudia vairadiai lalona iha-aukana asi dibana; bena e lolo, eto, Taunimanima iboudiai na vairagu ai bae raka lasi. Bena asi tauna ta dekediai Iosef ese tadikakana e hahedinarai henidia, ia be daika.
english: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

motu: Ḡau tamona, e tai lolololo dainai Aigupto taudia bona Farao ena ruma taudia iboudiai na ena tai e kamonai.
english: He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.

motu: Bena Iosef ese tadikakana e hereva henidia, eto, Lau binai Iosef, Tamagu na dounu e mauri nohomu eiava? A tadikakana na ihaere-henina asi dibadia, badina be kudoudia e hetaha.
english: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Does my father still live?” His|strong="H6440" * brothers couldn’t answer|strong="H6030" * him|strong="H6440" *; for|strong="H3588" * they|strong="H3588" * were|strong="H3130" * terrified at|strong="H6440" * his|strong="H6440" * presence|strong="H6440" *.

motu: Bena Iosef ese tadikakana ma e hamaorodia, eto, Mani a raka kahi mai. Bena idia na e raka henia kahi. Ia ma eto, Lau binai tadimu Iosef, vada o hoigu, bena Aigupto nama.
english: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came|strong="H5066" * near|strong="H5066" *. He|strong="H3130" * said, “ I|strong="H4714" * am Joseph|strong="H3130" *, your|strong="H4994" * brother, whom you|strong="H4994" * sold|strong="H4376" * into|strong="H4714" * Egypt|strong="H4714" *.

motu: Lalomui basie hisihisi, bona basio hebadu heheni, o hoigu bona ini nama dainai; badina be Dirava ese e siaigu baina gunalaimui, ihamaurimui totona.
english: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.

motu: Badina be ini laḡani rua be doe laḡanidia, a doe laḡanidia ima do mimia, unu laḡani lalodiai tano basie ruaia bona uit basie utua.
english: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.

motu: Dirava ese e siaigu, baina gunalaimui, umui baina hamaurimui bona besemui baina hamauridia helaoreana, bena bese badana ai baola.
english: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.

motu: Taunabunai dia umui, a Dirava ese e siaigu iniseni ai. Ia ese vada e karagu lau be Farao tamana na heto, ena ruma idoinai biaguna ai bona Aigupto tanona idoinai lohiana ai vada e halaogu.
english: So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

motu: Benaini, vada aola haraḡa-haraḡa tamagu dekenai, ba hamaoroa, baota “Natumu Iosef e tomu: Dirava ese Aigupto tanona idoinai lohiana ai vada e halaogu; lau dekegu baoma, basio halahe.
english: Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t wait.

motu: Gosen tanona ai do ba noho, lau badibadigu ai: oi bona natumu bona tubumu bona emu mamoe seridia bona emu boromakau seridia bona emu ḡau idoidiai.
english: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.

motu: Lau ese baina narimui, bena oi bona emu orea taudia iboudiai basio hitolo. Badina be doe laḡanidia ima na do mimia”.
english: There I will provide for you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.”’

motu: O itaia: umui matamui ese vada e itaia, bona tadigu Beniamina danu matana vada e itaia, ini hereva na lau udugu amo vada e lasi.
english: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.

motu: Taunabunai, hairaigu idoinai Aigupto ai, bona o ita ḡaudia iboudiai danu, tamagu ba hamaorolaia; bena tamagu ba hakaua mai haraḡa.
english: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”

motu: Bena ia na tadina Beniamina aiona ai e hegagiu dae mai taina ida; Beniamina danu ia aiona ai e hegagiu dae, vada e hetai heheni.
english: He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

motu: Bena Iosef ese kakana iboudiai e harahudia, bona e rosidia mai taina ida. Gabeamo tadikakana ia ida vada e hereva-hereva, asi edia gari.
english: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.

motu: Ini ḡau haridia na Farao ena ruma ai e piua, ena ruma taudia iboudiai na e kamonai Iosef tadikakana vada ema. Bena Farao mai ena hesiai taudia iboudiai vada e moale.
english: The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.

motu: Bena Farao ese Iosef e hamaoroa, eto, Tadikakamu ba hamaorodia, baoto “Emui kohu be emui doniki dorudia ai bavato kau, Kanaan tanona ba lou lao,
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.

motu: tamamui bona varavaramui bavabidia, ba hakaudia mai dekegu ai; lau ese Aigupto tanona ena ḡau namodia baina henimui, bona ina tano digarana do bavania”.
english: Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’

motu: Ma ba hamaorodia, baoto “Ini ba kara toma: ina Aigupto tanona ai rerue bavabi, ba laohai, natumui bona adavamui ba udadia, ba mailaidia, bona tamamui danu.
english: Now you are commanded to do this: Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.

motu: A emui kohu basio laloa, badina be ina Aigupto tanona ena kohu namodia na bavabi emui”.
english: Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”

motu: Bena Israel natuna ese iena hereva e badina; bona Iosef ese rerue bona dala lakwana e henidia, Farao ena hahedua heḡereḡerena.
english: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.

motu: Ta ta edia hahedoki toi toi danu e henidia, a Beniamina na silver * monidia sinahu-toi e henia bona hahedoki ima.
english: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.

motu: Herahia ḡaudia danu e siai, tamana ena: doniki gwauta Aigupto kohudia namodia e hua, bona doniki hahinedia gwauta uit bona flaoa bona aniani haida danu e hua, tamana ena dala lakwana.
english: He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.

motu: Bena ia ese tadikakana e siaidia lao, eto, Dala ai basio heiri-heiri.
english: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”

motu: Taunabunai idia na Aigupto e toretania, Kanaan tanona ela, tamadia Iakob dekenai.
english: They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.

motu: E hamaoroa, eto, Iosef e maurimu, Aigupto tanona idoinai e lohiaiamu. Bena Iakob laumana e daure, edia hereva se abia dae.
english: They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.

motu: A idia ese Iosef ena hereva iboudiai e hamaorolaia; bena Iakob ese Iosef e siai reruedia e itadia ai, ia laumana ma e mauri lou.
english: They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.

motu: Bena Israel eto, Vadaeni, natugu Iosef dounu e maurimu; lau na do basina mase ai baina ha itaia.
english: Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

motu: Israel na eha laolao, ena kohu idoinai e abi kau, Bere-sieba ai e kau, unuseni ai tamana Isaak ena Dirava e boua.
english: Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.

motu: Bena hanuaboi ai Dirava ese nihi ai Israel e hereva henia, eto, Iakob e, Iakob e! Ia eto, Lau o ina.
english: God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “Jacob, Jacob!” He|strong="H3478" * said, “ Here|strong="H2009" * I|strong="H2009" * am.”

motu: Ma eto, Lau be Dirava, tamamu ena Dirava: Aigupto baola, basio gari, badina be unuseni ai bese badana ai baina halaomu.
english: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation.

motu: Lau ese baina bamomu ela bona Aigupto, ma baina hakaumu lou; bona ba mase negana ai Iosef ese matamu baine hakapua.
english: I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”

motu: Bena Iakob ese Bere-sieba e toretania. Israel natudia ese tamadia Iakob bona natudia maraḡidia bona adavadia e abidia, Farao ese e henidia reruedia ai e udadia, e laohaidia.
english: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

motu: Edia boromakau danu, bona edia kohu idoinai, Kanaan tanona ai e abi, vada e laohai, ela Aigupto ai e lasi. Iakob mai ena iduhu idoinai ela:
english: They took their livestock, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt—Jacob, and all his offspring with him,

motu: natuna mamaruanedia bona tubuna mamaruanedia, natuna hahinedia bona tubuna hahinedia, bona varavarana ibouboudiai. Iboudiai Aigupto e laohaidia. Iakob garana
english: his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he brought all his offspring with him into Egypt.

motu: Israel garana, Aigupto ela taudia, ladadia bini, Iakob mai natuna iboudiai ida.
english: These are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.

motu: Ruben be Iakob natuna roboana. Ruben natuna be Hanok bona Palu bona Hesron bona Karami.
english: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

motu: Simeon natuna be Iemuel bona Iamin bona Ohad bona Iakin bona Sohara bona Saul. Saul be hane Kanaan natuna.
english: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.

motu: Levi natuna be Gereson bona Kohat bona Merari.
english: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

motu: Iuda natuna be Ere bona Onan bona Sela bona Perese bona Sera; a Ere bona Onan be Kanaan tanona ai e mase. Perese natuna be Hesron bona Hamulu.
english: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

motu: Isakara natuna be Tola bona Puva bona Iobo bona Simron.
english: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.

motu: Sebulun natuna be Sered bona Elon bona Ialeel.
english: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

motu: Ini iboudiai bona natuna hahinena Daina be Lea natuna bona tubuna, Iakob ese iena amo e abidia Padan-aram ai. Iboudiai be toi-ahui toi.
english: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.

motu: Gad natuna be Sifion bona Hagi bona Suni bona Esbon bona Eri bona Arodi bona Areli.
english: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.

motu: Asere natuna be Imna bona Isva bona Isvi bona Beria, taihudia Sera ida. Beria natuna be Hebere bona Malkiel.
english: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.

motu: Ini na hesiai hahinena Silpa natuna; Laban ese natuna Lea e henia hahinena bunai. Iakob ese natuna bona tubuna gwauta-tauratoi iena amo e abidia.
english: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.

motu: Iakob adavana Rahela natuna bini: Iosef bona Beniamina.
english: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

motu: Iosef ese natuna rarua, Manase bona Efraim, na Aigupto tanona ai e abidia, Ono ena hahelaḡa tauna Potifera natuna Asenat bogana amo.
english: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.

motu: Beniamina natuna bini: Bela bona Bekere bona Asbel bona Gera bona Naaman bona Ehi bona Ros bona Mupim bona Hupim bona Arad.
english: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.

motu: Ini iboudiai be Rahela natuna bona tubuna, Iakob ese iena amo e abidia. Iboudiai be gwauta-hani.
english: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.

motu: Dan natuna be Husim.
english: The son of Dan: Hushim.

motu: Napatali natuna be Iaseel bona Guni bona Iesere bona Silem.
english: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

motu: Ini be hesiai hahinena Bilha natuna; Laban ese natuna Rahela e henia hahinena bunai. Iboudiai be hahitu.
english: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.

motu: Iakob ida Aigupto ela taunimanimadia iboudiai, ia ese e havaradia taudia, be tauratoi-ahui tauratoi; a ravana be se duahidia.
english: All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct offspring, in addition to Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were sixty-six.

motu: Bona Iosef ese Aigupto ai e abidia memerodia be rarua. Iakob ena iduhu taudia Aigupto ela iboudiai be hitu-ahui. Iakob Aigupto ai
english: The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy.

motu: Iakob ese Iuda e siaia guna, Gosen bainela, Iosef baine hadibaia. Bena Gosen ai e lasi.
english: Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.

motu: Bena Iosef ese ena kariota e heḡaeḡaelaia, Gosen ela, tamana ida bae hedavari; enai e kau, bena aiona ai e hegagiu dae, e tai.
english: Joseph prepared his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

motu: Bena Israel ese Iosef e hereva henia, eto, Harihari aina mase be namo, badina be mai maurimu ida vada na davarimu lou.
english: Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”

motu: Bena Iosef ese tadikakana bona tamana ena orea taudia e hamaorodia, eto, Lau bainala, Farao baina hamaorolaia, bainato “Tadikakagu bona tamagu ena orea taudia na Kanaan tanona amo vada ema, lau dekegu ai.
english: Joseph said to his brothers, and to his father’s house, “I will go up, and speak with Pharaoh, and will tell him, ‘My brothers, and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.

motu: Idia be mamoe bona boromakau ireḡudia taudia, edia mamoe seridia bona edia boromakau seridia bona edia kohu idoinai vada e mailai”.
english: These men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.’

motu: Bena Farao ese baine boirimui bona baine nanadaimui, baineto “Emui ḡaukara be dahaka?”
english: It will happen, when Pharaoh summons you, and will say, ‘What is your occupation?’

motu: Una negana ai umui ba haere, baoto “Ai oi isiaimu ilao-henina taumai na meromai negana amo boromakau vada e reḡudia, senemai bamodia”. Unu amo Gosen bavabia diba, emui tano ai ba halaoa; badina be Aigupto taudia ese seri ireḡudia taudia e dadaraidiamu.
english: that you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

motu: Bena Iosef na Farao dekena ela, eto, Tamagu bona tadikakagu na Kanaan tanona amo vada ema, mai edia mamoe seridia bona edia boromakau seridia bona edia kohu idoinai. Idia na harihari Gosen tanona ai.
english: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, “My father and my brothers, with their flocks, their herds, and all that they own, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”

motu: Bena kakana laima e hakaudia vareai, Farao vairanai.
english: From among his brothers he took five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.

motu: Bena Farao ese e nanadaidia, eto, Emui ḡaukara be dahaka? Idia eto, Ai oi isiaimu ilao-henina taumai be mamoe ireḡudia taumai, senemai bamodia.
english: Pharaoh said to his brothers, “What is your occupation?” They|strong="H4100" * said to|strong="H5650" * Pharaoh|strong="H6547" *, “ Your|strong="H1571" * servants|strong="H5650" * are|strong="H4100" * shepherds|strong="H7462" *, both|strong="H1571" * we|strong="H3068" *, and|strong="H5650" * our|strong="H5650" * fathers.”

motu: Bena idia ese Farao e noia, eto, Ai na vada ama, ina tano ai baia noho a tomamu, badina be Kanaan tanona na asi reina emai seri bae ania. Mani emu kara a hereva, emu hesiai taudia na Gosen tanona ai baia noho.
english: They also said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as foreigners in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks. For the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.”

motu: Bena Farao ese Iosef e hamaoroa, eto, Tamamu bona tadikakamu na dekemu vada ema.
english: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.

motu: Aigupto tanona idoinai be vairamu ai; gabu namo-hereana ta ba henidia, bae noholaia. Gosen tanona ai do bae noho, bona bema goada taudia haida idia bogaragidiai, egu boromakau ireḡudia taudia ai ba halaodia.
english: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land. Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. If you know any able men among them, then put them in charge of my livestock.”

motu: Iosef ese tamana Iakob e hakaua vareai Farao vairanai; bena Iakob ese Farao e hanamoa.
english: Joseph brought in Jacob, his father, and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

motu: Farao ese e nanadaia, eto, Emu mauri laḡanidia be hida?
english: Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How old are you?”

motu: Iakob e haere, eto, Egu laolao laḡanidia ina tanobada ai na sinahuta toi-ahui; egu mauri laḡanidia na dia hoho bona mai hisihisidia, dia tamagu bona tubugu heḡereḡeredia, idia edia laolao laḡanidia tanobada ai na hoho.
english: Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. The days of the years of my life have been few and evil. They have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”

motu: Bena Iakob ese Farao e hanamoa, bena e rakatania.
english: Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.

motu: Bena Iosef ese tamana bona tadikakana edia gabu e lailaia bona edia tano e henidia, Aigupto tanona namo-hereana ta ai, ladana Ramese, Farao ena hahedua heḡereḡerena.
english: Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

motu: Bena Iosef ese tamana bona tadikakana bona tamana ena orea taudia iboudiai e ubudia, ruma ta ta taudia adia e henidia. Aigupto taudia e ogogamiva
english: Joseph provided his father, his brothers, and all of his father’s household with bread, according to the sizes of their families.

motu: Tano idoinai doe na bada herea; taunabunai Aigupto idoinai bona Kanaan idoinai aniani na lasi vaitani.
english: There was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.

motu: Moni idoinai Aigupto ai bona Kanaan ai na uit ihoilaina ai e ore, idoinai Iosef mo imana ai. Bena ia ese Farao ena ruma ai e haboua.
english: Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.

motu: Bena Aigupto ai bona Kanaan ai moni e ore vaitani murinai Aigupto taudia na Iosef dekena ela, eto, Aniani a henimai; oi o uramu ai na oi vairamu ai baia mase a? Ai na asi emai moni.
english: When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, “Give us bread, for why should we die in your presence? For our money fails.”

motu: Iosef eto, Emui boromakau a henigu; lau na uit baina henimui, emui boromakau davadia, asi emui moni dainai.
english: Joseph said, “Give me your livestock; and I will give you food for your livestock, if your money is gone.”

motu: Taunabunai edia boromakau e laohai Iosef dekenai; bena ia ese aniani e henidia, edia hosi bona edia mamoe bona edia boromakau bona edia doniki davadia.
english: They brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he fed them with bread in exchange for all their livestock for that year.

motu: Una l=agani e ore, bena laḡani iharuana ma e lou mai ia dekenai, eto, Lohia taumu e, ai na asia koimumu: emai moni vada e ore, emai boromakau iboudiai vada o abi; ḡau ta dia mia baia henimu, tau-animai bona emai tanomo vadaeni.
english: When that year was ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, “We will not hide from my lord how our money is all spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord’s. There is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.

motu: Ai na oi vairamu ai baia mase bona emai uma bae vahu a? Ai bavabimai, emai tano danu bavabi, aniani ba henimai. Bena ai bona emai tano ese Farao isiaina baia lao heni. Uhe danu ba henimai, bena emai tano na basine vahu.
english: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land won’t be desolate.”

motu: Taunabunai, Iosef ese Aigupto tanodia iboudiai e abi, Farao ena; badina be Aigupto taudia iboudiai ta ta ena tano ena tano e hoi, aniani davana, edia hitolo na bada dainai. Unuhetomana tano idoinai na Farao ena tano ai ela.
english: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for every man of the Egyptians sold his field, because the famine was severe on them, and the land became Pharaoh’s.

motu: Taunimanima danu e abidia, Aigupto hanuadia iboudiai, atai ela bona henu, hesiai taudia ai e halaodia.
english: As for the people, he moved them to the cities from one end of the border of Egypt even to the other end of it.

motu: Ḡau tamona hahelaḡa taudia edia tano ia ese se abi, badina be hahelaḡa taudia na Farao ese e ubudiava; taunabunai Farao ena heubu ḡaudia dekediai mimia dainai idia be edia tano bae hoi na asi badina.
english: Only he didn’t buy the land of the priests, for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and ate their portion which Pharaoh gave them. That is why they didn’t sell their land.

motu: Bena Iosef ese taunimanima e hamaorodia, eto, Hari dina ai umui vada na hoimui bona emui tano vada na hoi. Uhe bini, vada ba hado.
english: Then Joseph said to the people, “Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Behold, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.

motu: Bena uit ba utua negana ai, ba karoa, karoa ima; karoa ta Farao ba henia, a karoa hani be emui hadohado bona amui aniani ḡaudia, emui ruma taudia bona natumui maraḡidia iubulaidia.
english: It will happen at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts will be your own, for seed of the field, for your food, for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.”

motu: Bena idia ese e haere henia, eto, Momokani, oi ese vada o hamaurimai; oi baia imodaimu bona Farao isiaina baia lao heni.
english: They said, “You have saved our lives! Let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.”

motu: Unuhetomana Iosef ese taravadia e atua, hari taravatu na doini mia ema bona harihari: karoa ima lalodiai karoa ta be Farao ena. Ḡau tamona, hahelaḡa taudia edia tano ia ese se abi.
english: Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth. Only the land of the priests alone didn’t become Pharaoh’s.

motu: Israel be Aigupto taudia bogaragidiai e nohova, Gosen ai. Unuseni ai idia na kohu momo e habouva; e hutuma e laova, bona edia taḡa e bada e laova.
english: Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they got themselves possessions therein, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.

motu: Iakob na laḡeni gwauta-hitu Aigupto ai e nohova: ena mauri laḡanidia na sinahu-ta hari-ahui hitu.
english: Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. So the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred forty-seven years.

motu: Ena mase vada e kahira-kahira ai, ia ese natuna Iosef e boiria, e hereva henia, eto, Boma lalokau henigu, imamu na mamugu ai boma atoa kau, boma gwau hamata, Aigupto ai basio gurigu,
english: The time came near that Israel must die, and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, “If now I have found favor in your sight, please put your hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me. Please don’t bury me in Egypt,

motu: a tubu tama dekedia bainala negana ai, Aigupto amo ba laohaigu, idia edia gara ai ba gurigu. Bena Iosef eto, Unu baina kara toma.
english: but when I sleep with my fathers, you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying place.” Joseph said|strong="H1697" *, “ I|strong="H1697" * will|strong="H4714" * do|strong="H6213" * as|strong="H1697" * you|strong="H6213" * have|strong="H1697" * said|strong="H1697" *.”

motu: Bena Iakob eto, A gwau hamata. Bena Iosef ese e gwau henia hamata. Bena Israel na ena mahuta patana duna badina ai e ḡuriḡuri.
english: Israel said, “Swear to me,” and he swore to him. Then Israel bowed himself on the bed’s head.

motu: Ini ḡau muridiai, Iosef na harina e kamonai tamana vada e gorere; bena ia ese natuna raruosi, Manase bona Efraim, e hakaudia lao.
english: After these things, someone said to Joseph, “Behold, your father is sick.” He took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

motu: Bena haida ese Iakob e hamaoroa, eto, Natumu Iosef na oi i'itamu e maimu. Bena Israel na e haheauka, ena mahuta patana ai e helai tore.
english: Someone told Jacob, and said, “Behold, your son Joseph comes to you,” and Israel strengthened himself, and sat on the bed.

motu: Bena Iakob ese Iosef e hereva henia, eto, Siahu-idoinai Diravana ese Lusu ai, Kanaan tanona ai, e hahedinarai henigu bona e hanamogu,
english: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,

motu: eto “Momokani lau ese besemu baina havaraia, baina hahohomu, bese bada-hereana ai bainahalaomu; ina tano danu oi garamu baina henidia, edia tano ai bainela, ela bona hanaihanai”.
english: and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I will make of you a company of peoples, and will give this land to your offspring after you for an everlasting possession.’
