english: The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho came near to Elisha, and said to him, “Do you know that Yahweh will take away your master from over you today?” He|strong="H3588" * answered, “ Yes|strong="H3588" *, I|strong="H3588" * know|strong="H3045" * it|strong="H5921" *. Hold your|strong="H3068" * peace|strong="H2814" *.”

motu: Elia ese ma e hereva henia, eto, Mani emu kara iniseni ai do ba noho, badina be Iehova ese vada e siaigu, Ioridane sinavaina bainala. A ia na eto, Iehova e maurimu bona oi o maurimu heḡereḡerena, lau basina rakatanimu. Taunabunai, raruosi na e raka lao.
english: Elijah said to him, “Please wait here, for Yahweh has sent me to the Jordan.” He|strong="H3588" * said, “ As|strong="H5315" * Yahweh|strong="H3068" * lives|strong="H5315" *, and|strong="H3068" * as|strong="H5315" * your|strong="H3068" * soul|strong="H5315" * lives|strong="H5315" *, I|strong="H3588" * will|strong="H3068" * not|strong="H3588" * leave|strong="H5800" * you|strong="H3588" *.” Then|strong="H7971" * they|strong="H3588" * both|strong="H8147" * went|strong="H3212" * on|strong="H3427" *.

motu: Tatau imahui peroveta oreana amo danu ela, dauhai e giniva, idia raruosi Ioridane sinavaina isena ai e giniva negana ai.
english: Fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance; and they both stood by the Jordan.

motu: Bena Elia ese ena hahedoki badana e abia, e lokua, bena ranu e botalaia; bena ranu na e parara, kahana ela kahana ela, ela bona raruosi na tano kaukauna ai e raka hanai.
english: Elijah took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck the waters; and they were divided here and there, so that they both went over on dry ground.

motu: E raka hanai, bena Elia ese Elisaia e hamaoroa, eto, Emu amo do asina heabi oho ai, ba noigu ede baina karamu toma. Elisaia eto, Na noimumu, lalomu siahuna lauegu ai ba habadaia harua.
english: When they had gone over, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I shall do for you, before I am taken from you.” Elisha said|strong="H6310" *, “ Please|strong="H4994" * let|strong="H4994" * a|strong="H3068" * double|strong="H8147" * portion|strong="H6310" * of|strong="H7307" * your|strong="H3947" * spirit|strong="H7307" * be|strong="H1961" * on|strong="H5674" * me|strong="H4994" *.”

motu: Elia eto, Ḡau aukana ta o noinoilaiamu; ḡau tamona, emu amo baina heabi oho negana ai ba itagu, emu ai unu baine heto, a basio itagu be unu basine heto.
english: He said, “You have asked a hard thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be so.”

motu: Idia na dounu e rakava bona e hereva-herevava ai, lahi kariotana ta bona lahi hosidia ese raruosi e hapararadia. Bena Elia na koehirihiri amo e dae guba ai.
english: As they continued on and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

motu: Elisaia e itaia, bena e boi lolo, eto, Tamagu e, tamagu e, Israel ena kariota bona ena hosi-gui taudia. Bena se itaia lou. Bena ia sibona ena dabua e abidia, e daredia parara. Elisaia ese Elia e boloa
english: Elisha saw it, and he cried, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” He|strong="H1931" * saw|strong="H7200" * him|strong="H7200" * no|strong="H3808" * more|strong="H5750" *. Then|strong="H7200" * he|strong="H1931" * took|strong="H2388" * hold|strong="H2388" * of|strong="H7393" * his|strong="H7200" * own|strong="H2388" * clothes and|strong="H3478" * tore|strong="H7167" * them|strong="H7200" * in|strong="H3478" * two|strong="H8147" * pieces|strong="H7168" *.

motu: Hahedoki badana, Elia ena amo e moru ḡauna, na Elisaia ese e abia, e lou lao, Ioridane sinavaina isena ai e gini.
english: He also took up Elijah’s mantle that fell from him, and went back and stood by the bank of the Jordan.

motu: Bena hari hahedoki badana Elia ena amo e moru ḡauna na e abia, ranu e botalaia, eto, Iehova, Elia ena Dirava, be edeseni ai? Ranu e botaia negana ai, ranu na e parara, kahana ela kahana ela; bena Elisaia e raka hanai.
english: He took Elijah’s mantle that fell from him, and struck the waters, and said, “Where is Yahweh, the God of Elijah?” When he also had struck the waters, they were divided apart, and Elisha went over.

motu: Ieriko peroveta oreana taudia ese e itaia, ia na idia vairadiai, bena idia na eto, Elia lalona siahuna ese Elisaia e roheamu. Bena ia dekena ela, tano ai e igo diho ia vairanai.
english: When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho facing him saw him, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.” They came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.

motu: Bena idia ese e hamaoroa, eto, A itaia, emu hesiai taudia dekemai ai na goada taudia imahui; mani emu kara idia na baela, biagumu bae tahua; reana Iehova ena Lauma ese vada e abia isi, ororo ta ai eiava koura ta lalonai vada e tahoa dobi. Bena ia e haere, eto, Basio siaidia.
english: They said to him, “See now, there are with your servants fifty strong men. Please let them go and seek your master. Perhaps Yahweh’s Spirit has taken him up, and put him on some mountain or into some valley.” He|strong="H3068" * said, “Don’t send|strong="H7971" * them|strong="H7971" *.”

motu: To idia ese e ha-uraia ela bona e hemarai, bena eto, A siaidia. Taunabunai, idia ese tatau imahui e siaidia, idia na dina toi e tahua, to asie davaria.
english: When they urged him until he was ashamed, he said, “Send them.” Therefore|strong="H7971" * they|strong="H3117" * sent|strong="H7971" * fifty|strong="H2572" * men; and|strong="H7971" * they|strong="H3117" * searched|strong="H1245" * for|strong="H5704" * three|strong="H7969" * days|strong="H3117" *, but|strong="H3808" * didn’t find|strong="H4672" * him|strong="H7971" *.

motu: Bena e lou lao, Elisaia dekenai, ia na dounu Ieriko ai nohona ai. Bena ia ese e hamaorodia, eto, Na hamaoromui nato “Basiola” ani?
english: They came back to him while he stayed at Jericho; and he said to them, “Didn’t I tell you, ‘Don’t go’?”

motu: Bena hanua taudia ese Elisaia e hamaoroa, eto, A itaia, ina hanua e ginimu gabuna na gabu namona, egu lohia o itaiamu heḡereḡerena. A ranu na dika, bona tano anina e ruru negemu.
english: The men of the city said to Elisha, “Behold, please, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord sees; but the water is bad, and the land is barren.”

motu: Ia eto, Nau matamatana ta a mailaia, lalonai damena ba uda. Taunabunai idia ese e mailaia ia dekenai.
english: He said, “Bring me a new jar, and put salt in it.” Then they brought it to him.

motu: Bena ia na ranu gurina ela, damena na ranu lalonai e tahoa dobi, eto, Iehova na ini e gwau tomamu: Ina ranu vada na haḡoevaia; ina negana amo ia ese mase eiava ruru-nege basine havaraia.
english: He went out to the spring of the waters, and threw salt into it, and said, “Yahweh says, ‘I have healed these waters. There shall not be from there any more death or barren wasteland.’”

motu: Taunabunai, una ranu vada e namo ema bona hari dina, Elisaia ese e gwauraia herevana heḡereḡerena.
english: So the waters were healed to this day, according to Elisha’s word which he spoke.

motu: Unu amo ia na e dae lao Betele ai. Dala ai e laova ai na memero maraḡidia haida na hanua amo e raka lasi, e kirikirilaia, eto, Kwara boha e, a dae lao, kwara boha e, a dae lao.
english: He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up by the way, some youths came out of the city and mocked him, and said to him, “Go up, you baldy! Go up, you baldy!”

motu: Ia na e gini kerehai, e itadia; bena Iehova ladana ai e uduguiraidia. Bena bea hahinedia rua na uda amo e raka lasi, memero hari-ahui rua e aladia mase.
english: He looked behind him and saw them, and cursed them in Yahweh’s name. Then two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of those youths.

motu: Unu amo ia na ena dala ai e raka, ela bona Karamele ororona; bena unu amo Samaria ma e lou lao.
english: He went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

motu: Iehosafat, Iuda pavapavana, ena lohia laḡanina ihagwauta-taurahanina ai, Iehroam, Ahaba natuna, na Israel pavapavana ai ela, Samaria ai. Ena lohia laḡanina na gwauta-rua.
english: Now Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned twelve years.

motu: Iehova vairanai e kara havara, a dia tamana sinana heḡereḡeredia; badina be Baal ena au-tubua, tamana ese e karaia ḡauna, na ia ese e abia oho.
english: He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, but not like his father and like his mother, for he put away the pillar of Baal that his father had made.

motu: Ḡau tamona, Ieroboam Nebata ena kara dika, Israel e hakaralaia dika ḡauna, na ia ese e dogoa tao, se rakatania. Elisaia ese kwalimu e gwauraia guna
english: Nevertheless he held to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin. He didn’t depart from them.

motu: Mesa, Moab pavapavana, na mamoe e haperedia rohoroho tauna; laḡani ta ta amo ia ese mamoe natudia domaga ta bona mamoe mamaruanedia domaga ta + 3:4 Domaga ta = 100,000. * huidia na Israel pavapavana dekena e siaidia lao.
english: Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder; and he supplied the king of Israel with one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.

motu: A Ahaba e mase murinai Moab pavapavana ese Israel pavapavana e daḡedaḡe henia.
english: But when Ahab was dead, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

motu: Taunabunai, una negana ai King Iehoram na Samaria amo e raka lasi, Israel taudia iboudiai e haboudia.
english: King Jehoram went out of Samaria at that time, and mustered all Israel.

motu: Bena ela, hereva na Iehosafat, Iuda pavapavana, dekena e siaia, eto, Moab pavapavana ese e daḡedaḡe henigumu; oi na lau ida aitala, Moab baita tuari henia ani? Ia eto, Baina vasi; lau oi na tamona, lauegu orea bona oiemu orea danu tamona; lauegu hosi bona oiemu hosi danu tamona.
english: He went and sent to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab to battle?” He|strong="H7971" * said, “ I|strong="H3644" * will|strong="H4428" * go|strong="H3212" * up|strong="H5927" *. I|strong="H3644" * am as|strong="H3644" * you|strong="H7971" * are|strong="H5971" *, my|strong="H7971" * people|strong="H5971" * as|strong="H3644" * your|strong="H7971" * people|strong="H5971" *, my|strong="H7971" * horses|strong="H5483" * as|strong="H3644" * your|strong="H7971" * horses|strong="H5483" *.”

motu: Ma eto, Edena dala amo baitala? Iehoram e haere, eto, Edom tano-ḡaḡaena dalana amo.
english: Then he said, “Which way shall we go up?” Jehoram answered, “ The|strong="H5927" * way|strong="H1870" * of|strong="H1870" * the|strong="H5927" * wilderness|strong="H4057" * of|strong="H1870" * Edom.”

motu: Taunabunai Israel pavapavana na Iuda pavapavana bona Edom pavapavana ida ela. Dina hitu lalodiai idia na dala magevana amo e raka heḡeḡe; bena tuari taudia bona edia ubu-ubu ḡaudia, idia muridiai e rakava gaudia, na asi adia ranu.
english: So the king of Israel went with the king of Judah and the king of Edom, and they marched for seven days along a circuitous route. There was no water for the army or for the animals that followed them.

motu: Bena Israel pavapavana eto, Madi ihabaida, Iehova ese ita pavapava tatoiosi vada e boirida, Moab pavapavana imana ai baine atoda totona.
english: The king of Israel said, “Alas! For Yahweh has called these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”

motu: Iehosafat eto, Iehova ena peroveta tauna ta dia iniseni ai a? Iena amo Iehova baitama nanadaia. Bena Israel pavapavana ena hesiai tauna ta e haere, eto, Elisaia Safata na iniseni ai, ia be Elia imana ranu amo e dairidia tauna.
english: But Jehoshaphat said, “Isn’t there a prophet of Yahweh here, that we may inquire of Yahweh by him?” One|strong="H1121" * of|strong="H1121" * the|strong="H5921" * king|strong="H4428" * of|strong="H1121" * Israel|strong="H3478" *’s servants|strong="H5650" * answered|strong="H6030" *, “Elisha the|strong="H5921" * son|strong="H1121" * of|strong="H1121" * Shaphat|strong="H8202" *, who|strong="H3068" * poured|strong="H3332" * water|strong="H4325" * on|strong="H5921" * the|strong="H5921" * hands|strong="H3027" * of|strong="H1121" * Elijah, is|strong="H3068" * here|strong="H6311" *.”

motu: Iehosafat eto, Iehova ena hereva na ia enai. Taunabunai Israel pavapavana bona Iehosafat bona Edom pavapavana na ia dekena ela.
english: Jehoshaphat said, “Yahweh’s word is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

motu: Elisaia ese Israel pavapavana e hamaoroa, eto, Dahaka baina kara henimu? Tamamu bona sinamu edia peroveta taudia dekedia aola. A Israel pavapavana ese e hamaoroa, eto, Lasi, Iehova ese pavapava taumai tatoiosi vada e boirimai, Moab taudia imadia ai baine atomai totona.
english: Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father, and to the prophets of your mother.” The|strong="H3588" * king|strong="H4428" * of|strong="H4428" * Israel|strong="H3478" * said|strong="H7121" * to|strong="H3478" * him|strong="H5414" *, “ No|strong="H5414" *, for|strong="H3588" * Yahweh|strong="H3068" * has|strong="H3068" * called|strong="H7121" * these|strong="H7121" * three|strong="H7969" * kings|strong="H4428" * together|strong="H7121" * to|strong="H3478" * deliver|strong="H5414" * them|strong="H5414" * into|strong="H3212" * the|strong="H3588" * hand|strong="H3027" * of|strong="H4428" * Moab|strong="H4124" *.”

motu: Elisaia eto, Iehova Sabaota, isiaina na lao heniamu Diravana, e maurimu heḡereḡerena, Iehosafat, Iuda pavapavana, basinama matauraia, lau ese oi basinarna haḡeremu bona basinama itamu.
english: Elisha said, “As Yahweh of Armies lives, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I respect the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward you, nor see you.

motu: Benaini, hatai-hatai ḡaudia e hataimu tauna ta ba hakaua mai dekegu ai. Bena hatai-hatai ḡaudia e hatai tauna ta ese ena ḡau e hataia negana ai, Iehova ena siahu ese Elisaia e rohea.
english: But now bring me a musician.” When the musician played, Yahweh’s hand came on him.

motu: Bena ia eto, Iehova na ini e gwau tomamu: Ina koupa kaukauna lalonai lau ese ranu gohogohudia baina karadia.
english: He said, “Yahweh says, ‘Make this valley full of trenches.’

motu: Badina be Iehova na ini e gwau tomamu: Lai eiava medu basio itadia, to una koupa na ranu ai baine honu, ba inu helaoreana, umui bona emui boromakau bona emui ubu-ubu ḡaudia iboudiai.
english: For Yahweh says, ‘You will not see wind, neither will you see rain, yet that valley will be filled with water, and you will drink, both you and your livestock and your other animals.

motu: Iehova vairanai una na ḡau pipikina; ia ese Moab taudia danu umui imamui ai baine atodia;
english: This is an easy thing in Yahweh’s sight. He will also deliver the Moabites into your hand.

motu: bena hanua mai maḡudia iboudiai bona abi-hidi hanuadia iboudiai na ba hadareredia, au namodia iboudiai na ba hagaridia, ranu guridia iboudiai na ba tahunidia, bona tano namodia iboudiai na nadi amo ba hadikadia.
english: You shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and shall fell every good tree, and stop all springs of water, and mar every good piece of land with stones.’”

motu: Daba-rerena ai, boubou ḡaudia e hahelaḡadiava horana sisivana ai, ranu na Edom kahana amo e aru ema, ela bona una tano idoinai na ranu ese e utua dae.
english: In the morning, about the time of offering the sacrifice, behold, water came by the way of Edom, and the country was filled with water.

motu: Moab taudia iboudiai na e kamonai, hari pavapava na idia ituari-henidia totona vada ema; bena tuari dabuadia bae doki diba taudia, maragina amo ela bona badana, e boiridia, tano hetoana ai e haginidia heḡaeḡae.
english: Now when all the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, they gathered themselves together, all who were able to put on armor, young and old, and stood on the border.

motu: Daba matana ai e tore tore isi, bena dina e tara ranu latanai; bena Moab taudia ese ranu idia vairadiai e itaia na vada e kakakaka, rara na heto.
english: They rose up early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and the Moabites saw the water opposite them as red as blood.

motu: Bena idia na eto, Ina na rara; momokani hari pavapava na sibodia e tuari bona vada e heala-ala heheni. Moab e, aitala, edia ḡau aita ha-abi.
english: They said, “This is blood. The kings are surely destroyed, and they have struck each other. Now therefore, Moab, to the plunder!”

motu: A Israel edia taruha ai e kau negana ai, Israel taudia na e tore isi, Moab taudia e guru henidia, ela bona Moab taudia na idia vairadia amo e heau. Bena idia ese e lao henidia, Moab taudia e aladia laova.
english: When they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck the Moabites, so that they fled before them; and they went forward into the land attacking the Moabites.

motu: Hanua na e ḡiḡidia dobi, bona tano namodia iboudiai latadiai idia ta ta ese nadi ta ta e taho kau, ela bona tano e bubuni. Ranu guridia iboudiai danu e tahunidia, bona au namodia iboudiai e hagaridia; ela bona Kiri-haresete nadina mo mimia. Bena vilipopo taudia ese e koua heḡeḡe bona e hadarerea.
english: They beat down the cities; and on every good piece of land each man cast his stone, and filled it. They also stopped all the springs of water and cut down all the good trees, until in Kir Hareseth all they left was its stones; however the men armed with slings went around it and attacked it.

motu: Moab pavapavana e diba, ia vada e darere; bena ia ese dare taudia sinahu hitu e abidia, Edom pavapavana vairanai bae raka uru eto, to asie heḡereḡere.
english: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too severe for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew a sword, to break through to the king of Edom; but they could not.

motu: Bena ia ese natuna roboana, ena gabu ai bema lohia merona, na e abia, e hahelaḡaia, ḡole-oho boubouna ḡauna ai e halaoa, hanua maguna latanai. Bena badu ḡaraḡara na Israel taudia latadiai e kau; bena idia na iena amo e raka oho, edia tano korikori e lou lao.
english: Then he took his oldest son who would have reigned in his place, and offered him for a burnt offering on the wall. There was great wrath against Israel; and they departed from him, and returned to their own land.

motu: Peroveta oreana tauna ta vabuna ese Elisaia e tai henia, eto, Emu hesiai tauna, lau adavagu, na vada e mase. Oi dibamu emu hesiai tauna na Iehova garina e gariva, to enai e abi torehai tauna na vada ema, natugu raruosi baine abidia oho, ena hesiai memerodia ai baine halaodia e tomamu.
english: Now a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead. You know that your servant feared Yahweh. Now the creditor has come to take for himself my two children to be slaves.”

motu: Elisaia ese e hamaoroa, eto, Ede baina karamu toma? A hamaorogu, emu ruma ai na dahaka ḡau mia? Hahine na eto, Emu hesiai hahinena na asi ena ḡau ta ruma ai mia, dehoro kavabu tamona mo.
english: Elisha said to her, “What should I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She|strong="H3588" * said, “ Your|strong="H3605" * servant|strong="H8198" * has|strong="H4100" * nothing|strong="H3605" * in|strong="H6213" * the|strong="H3605" * house|strong="H1004" *, except|strong="H3588" * a|strong="H3068" * pot of|strong="H1004" * oil|strong="H8081" *.”

motu: Bena Elisaia eto, A raka lasi, bamomu dekediai kavabu haida do a ha-abi, kavabu asi anidia taina momo.
english: Then he said, “Go, borrow empty containers from all your neighbors. Don’t borrow just a few containers.

motu: Bena ba raka vareai, iduara ba koua, natumu raruosi danu oi ida ruma lalonai ba hekou ahu. Bena dehoro na kavabu iboudiai lalodiai ba vedadia; ta baine honu, bavatoa siri.
english: Go in and shut the door on you and on your sons, and pour oil into all those containers; and set aside those which are full.”

motu: Taunabunai, hahine ese ia e rakatania, mai natuna raruosi ida e raka vareai, iduara e koua; bena dehoro e seia negana ai, idia ese kavabu na ia dekena e mailaidia.
english: So she went from him, and shut the door on herself and on her sons. They brought the containers to her, and she poured oil.

motu: Kavabu iboudiai e honu, bena ia ese natuna ta e hamaoroa, eto, Kavabu ta ma a mailaia. Hari mero ese e hamaoroa, eto, Ta dia mia. Bena dehoro ena aru e doko.
english: When the containers were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another container.” He|strong="H1121" * said to|strong="H1961" * her|strong="H4390" *, “ There|strong="H1961" * isn’t another|strong="H5750" * container|strong="H3627" *.” Then|strong="H1961" * the|strong="H4390" * oil|strong="H8081" * stopped|strong="H5975" * flowing|strong="H3627" *.

motu: Hahine na ela, Dirava ena tau e hamaoroa; bena ia eto, Aola, dehoro ba hoia, emu abi-torehai davadia ba heni; orena na oi bona natumu raruosi emui mauri ḡauna. Suneme hahinena sivaraina
english: Then she came and told the man of God. He said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt; and you and your sons live on the rest.”

motu: Dina ta Elisaia na Suneme ela. Taḡa hahinena ta unuseni ai e nohova, bena ia ese Elisaia e ura henia bada, baine aniani. Taunabunai, una dala amo e laova negadia iboudiai ia na unuseni ai e dae kau, baine aniani totona.
english: One day Elisha went to Shunem, where there was a prominent woman; and she persuaded him to eat bread. So it was, that as often as he passed by, he turned in there to eat bread.

motu: Bena una hahine ese adavana e hamaoroa, eto, A itaia, lau vada name diba ina eda gabu e rakaia hanai louloumu tauna na Dirava ena tau helaḡana ta.
english: She said to her husband, “See now, I perceive that this is a holy man of God who passes by us continually.

motu: Mani emu kara, atai ai daiutu maraḡina ta baita karaia, unuseni ai mahuta ḡauna bona pata bona helai ḡauna bona lamepa baita atodia iena; bena dekedai bainema negadia ai ia na unuseni ai baine dae kau.
english: Please, let’s make a little room on the roof. Let’s set a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp stand for him there. When he comes to us, he can stay there.”

motu: Dina ta ia na unuseni ai e kau, bena una daiutu ai e dae kau,
english: One day he came there, and he went to the room and lay there.

motu: laḡana e ania. Bena ia ese ena hesiai tauna Gehasi e hamaoroa, eto, Hari hane Suneme a boiria. E boiria, bena ia vairanai e gini.
english: He said to Gehazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite.” When he had called her, she stood before him.

motu: Bena ia ese Gehasi e hamaoroa, eto, A hereva henia, aogwa “O itaiamu, ina idoinai vada o hekwarahilaia ai daimai ai; dahaka baia kara henimu? Oi daimu ai hanua pavapavana eiava tuari oreana biaguna baia hereva henia a?” Hahine e haere, eto, Lau na varavaragu bogaragidiai na nohomu.
english: He said to him, “Say now to her, ‘Behold, you have cared for us with all this care. What is to be done for you? Would you like to be spoken for to the king, or to the captain of the army?’” She|strong="H2063" * answered|strong="H1696" *, “ I|strong="H2009" * dwell|strong="H3427" * among|strong="H8432" * my|strong="H3605" * own|strong="H5971" * people|strong="H5971" *.”

motu: Elisaia ma eto, Vada dahaka baita kara henia? Gehasi na e haere, eto, O, ia na asi natuna merona ta, bona adavana na vada e buruka.
english: He said, “What then is to be done for her?” Gehazi|strong="H1522" * answered, “Most certainly|strong="H6213" * she|strong="H4100" * has|strong="H4100" * no|strong="H6213" * son|strong="H1121" *, and|strong="H1121" * her|strong="H6213" * husband is|strong="H4100" * old|strong="H1121" *.”

motu: Elisaia eto, A boiria. E boiria; bena hahine na iduara ai e gini.
english: He said, “Call her.” When he had called her, she stood in the door.

motu: Elisaia eto, Laḡani vairai, nega inihetomana ai, natumu merona ta ba rosia. Hahine eto, Egu lohia, Dirava ena tau e, lasi; emu hesiai hahinena basio koia.
english: He said, “At this season next year, you will embrace a son.” She|strong="H6256" * said, “No, my|strong="H2088" * lord, you|strong="H6256" * man|strong="H1121" * of|strong="H1121" * God, do|strong="H2088" * not|strong="H2088" * lie|strong="H3576" * to|strong="H6256" * your|strong="H2088" * servant|strong="H8198" *.”

motu: A hahine na e rogorogo, bena tubu-kau negana sisivana ai mero ta e abia, Elisaia ese e hamaoroa negana heḡereḡerena ai.
english: The woman conceived, and bore a son at that season when the time came around, as Elisha had said to her.

motu: Mero na e bada oho bada oho, bena dina ta ia na e raka lasi, tamana dekena ela, uit iutuna taudia bogaragidiai.
english: When the child was grown, one day he went out to his father to the reapers.

motu: Bena ia ese tamana e tai henia, eto, Kwaragu o, kwaragu o. Bena tamana ese ena hesiai tauna e hamaoroa, eto, A rosia, sinana dekena a laohaia.
english: He said to his father, “My head! My head!” He said to|strong="H5375" * his|strong="H5375" * servant|strong="H5288" *, “ Carry|strong="H5375" * him|strong="H5375" * to|strong="H5375" * his|strong="H5375" * mother.”

motu: E abia isi, sinana dekena e laohaia; bena mero na sinana mamuna ai e helai ela bona dina tubua, bena e mase.
english: When he had taken him and brought him to his mother, he sat on her knees until noon, and then died.

motu: Bena hahine ese e daelaia, Dirava ena tau ena mahuta ḡauna ai e kurea kau, bena iduara e koua. Bena e diho.
english: She went up and laid him on the man of God’s bed, and shut the door on him, and went out.

motu: Bena ia ese adavana e boi henia, eto, Hesiai tauna ta dekegu a siaia, bona doniki ta danu; lau na Dirava ena tau dekena baina lao haraḡa, bena ma baina lou mai.
english: She called to her husband and said, “Please send me one of the servants, and one of the donkeys, that I may run to the man of God and come again.”

motu: Adavana eto, Dahaka dainai hari dina ai ba lao henia? Ina na dia hua matamata dinana eiava dia dina helaḡana. Hahine eto, Vada baine namo.
english: He said, “Why would you want to go to him today? It is not a new moon or a Sabbath.” She|strong="H2320" * said, “ It|strong="H1980" *’s all|strong="H3117" * right.”

motu: Bena ia ese doniki e haheḡaeḡaea, bona ena hesiai tauna e hamaoroa, eto, Ba haḡavaia, ena raka basio hametaua ela bona lau ese baina hamaoromu dahaka.
english: Then she saddled a donkey, and said to her servant, “Drive, and go forward! Don’t slow down for me, unless I ask you to.”

motu: Taunabunai ia na ela, bona Dirava ena tau enai e kau, Karamele ororona ai. Dirava ena tau ese maina ai e itaia negana ai, ia ese ena hesiai tauna Gehasi e hamaoroa, eto, A itaia, Suneme hahinena bunai;
english: So she went, and came to the man of God to Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her afar off, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Behold, there is the Shunammite.

motu: a heau lao haraḡa, ia ida ba hedavari, baoto “Oi namo a? Adavamu bona natumu danu nanamo a?” Hahine na e haere, eto, Nanamo.
english: Please run now to meet her, and ask her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with your child?’” She answered, “ It|strong="H7965" * is|strong="H3206" * well|strong="H7965" *.”

motu: Ororo ai e kau, Dirava ena tau dekenai, bena ia ese aena e abi tao. Gehasi ema, baine doria oho eto; a Dirava ena tau eto, Aine noho, badina be darana e dokomu. Iehova ese e hunia egu ai; se hamaorogu.
english: When she came to the man of God to the hill, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to thrust her away; but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her soul is troubled within her; and Yahweh has hidden it from me, and has not told me.”

motu: Bena hahine eto, Lau ese egu lohia emu ai natugu na noia a? Lau nato “Basio koigu” ani?
english: Then she said, “Did I ask you for a son, my lord? Didn’t I say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”

motu: Elisaia ese Gehasi e hamaoroa, eto, Emu rami ba hekasilaia, egu itotohi na imamu ai bavabia, baola. Ta ida boma hedavari, Basio hahenamo henia; bona ta ese bema hahenamo henimu, basio haere henia. Bena egu itotohi na mero vairana latanai ba dagaia diho.
english: Then he said to Gehazi, “Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my staff in your hand, and go your way. If you meet any man, don’t greet him; and if anyone greets you, don’t answer him again. Then lay my staff on the child’s face.”

motu: Bena mero sinana eto, Iehova e maurimu bona oi o maurimu heḡereḡerena, lau na oi basina rakatanimu. Taunabunai, ia na e tore isi, hahine murina amo e raka.
english: The child’s mother said, “As Yahweh lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” So|strong="H6965" * he|strong="H3068" * arose|strong="H6965" *, and|strong="H6965" * followed|strong="H3212" * her|strong="H5800" *.

motu: Gehasi na e raka guna, itotohi na mero vairana latanai e dagaia diho, a mauri reḡena ta eiava toana ta enai se hedinarai. Taunabunai ia na e lou ela, Elisaia ida e hedavari; bena e hamaoroa, eto, Mero na do se noga.
english: Gehazi went ahead of them, and laid the staff on the child’s face; but there was no voice and no hearing. Therefore he returned to meet him, and told him, “The child has not awakened.”

motu: Elisaia na ruma ai e dae kau, bena iena mahuta ḡauna latanai mero hekurena ai e itaia, mase.
english: When Elisha had come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and lying on his bed.

motu: Taunabunai, ia na e raka vareai, e hekou ahu, idia raruosi mo nonoho. Bena ia ese Iehova e ḡuria.
english: He went in therefore, and shut the door on them both, and prayed to Yahweh.

motu: Bena ia na ela, mero latanai e goru kau, ia uduna mero uduna latanai, ia matana mero matana latadiai, ia imana mero imana latadiai; bena latanai e goru parapara negana ai hari mero tau-anina e siahu-siahu.
english: He went up and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He stretched himself on him; and the child’s flesh grew warm.

motu: Bena ia na e tore isi lou, ruma lalonai e raka lao e raka lou; bena ma e dae kau, ma latanai e goru parapara. Bena mero na nega hitu e asimana; bena matana e papa.
english: Then he returned, and walked in the house once back and forth, then went up and stretched himself out on him. Then the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.

motu: Bena Elisaia ese Gehasi e boiria, eto, Hari Suneme hahinena a boiria. Bena e boiria. Hahine na ema, bena Elisaia eto, Natumu avabia isi.
english: He called Gehazi, and said, “Call this Shunammite!” So he called her. When|strong="H1121" * she|strong="H7121" * had|strong="H1121" * come in|strong="H1121" * to|strong="H1121" * him|strong="H7121" *, he|strong="H7121" * said|strong="H7121" *, “ Take|strong="H5375" * up|strong="H5375" * your|strong="H5375" * son|strong="H1121" *.”

motu: Hahine na ema, ia aena badidiai e igo diho, tano ai e goru diho; bena ia ese natuna e abia isi, e raka lasi. Elisaia Gilgal ai
english: Then she went in, fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground; then she picked up her son, and went out.

motu: Elisaia na e lou lao, Gilgal ela. Una negana ai doe vada e vara una tano ai. Peroveta oreana taudia na ia vairanai hehelai; bena ia ese ena hesiai tauna e hamaoroa, eto, Uro badana na lahi ai ba laia kau, vasiahu ba nadua, peroveta oreana taudia adia.
english: Elisha came again to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land; and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him; and he said to his servant, “Get the large pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.”

motu: Idia ta e raka lasi, tano paka ai aniani avadia baine gogo eto; bena uda varovarona ta e davaria, bena huahuana e gogo, vairana ramina e hahonua, bena ela, e reredia, vasiahu urona lalonai e udadia. Asi dibana unu be dahaka ḡau.
english: One went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered a lap full of wild gourds from it, and came and cut them up into the pot of stew; for they didn’t recognize them.

motu: Bena e seia, tatau bae inua totona. A vasiahu inuna ai idia na e lolo, eto, Dirava ena tau e, mase na uro lalonai. Idia na asie inua diba.
english: So they poured out for the men to eat. As they were eating some of the stew, they cried out and said, “Man of God, there is death in the pot!” And they could not eat it.

motu: Elisaia eto, Flaoa taina a mailaia. Bena uro ai e udaia. Ma eto, Ma a seia, tatau adia, bae inua. Dika ta dia mia uro lalonai.
english: But he said, “Then bring meal.” He threw it into the pot; and he said, “Serve it to the people, that they may eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.

motu: Tau ta Baal-salisa amo ema, Dirava ena tau ana e mailai, uma anidia roboadia flaoana, bali igabudia ruahui, bona uit anidia matamatadia, na ena puse ai. Bena Elisaia eto, Tatau a henidia, bae ani.
english: A man from Baal Shalishah came, and brought the man of God some bread of the first fruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha said, “Give to the people, that they may eat.”

motu: A ena hesiai tauna eto, Tatau sinahu ta vairadiai ede baina dabarai toma? Ma e hamaoroa, eto, Tatau a henidia, bae aniani, badina be Iehova na ini e gwau tomamu: Bae aniani, bona bahudia na bae mia.
english: His servant said, “What, should I set this before a hundred men?” But|strong="H3588" * he|strong="H3588" * said, “ Give|strong="H5414" * it|strong="H5414" * to|strong="H3068" * the|strong="H6440" * people|strong="H5971" *, that|strong="H3588" * they|strong="H3588" * may|strong="H3068" * eat; for|strong="H3588" * Yahweh|strong="H3068" * says|strong="H3541" *, ‘ They|strong="H3588" * will|strong="H3068" * eat, and|strong="H3967" * will|strong="H3068" * have|strong="H3068" * some|strong="H3498" * left|strong="H3498" * over|strong="H5414" *.’”

motu: Bena e dabaraia idia vairadiai. Bena idia na e aniani, bona bahudia na e mia, Iehova ena hereva heḡereḡerena.
english: So he set it before them and they ate and had some left over, according to Yahweh’s word.

motu: Naaman, Suria pavapavana ena tuari oreana lohiana, na biaguna ena tau badana ta, bona e lalo namo heniava; badina be iena amo Iehova ese kwalimu na Suria e henia. Ia na goada dikadika bona boga-auka tauna; to ia na lepra tauna.
english: Now Naaman, captain of the army of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honorable, because by him Yahweh had given victory to Syria; he was also a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.

motu: Edia tuari ta ai, Suria taudia ese kekeni ta e abia mauri, Israel tanona ai; bena una kekeni ese Naaman adavana isiaina e lao heniva.
english: The Syrians had gone out in bands, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little girl, and she waited on Naaman’s wife.

motu: Bena ia ese biaguna hahinena e hereva henia, eto, Una egu lohia na bema Samaria peroveta tauna dekenai, ia ese ena lepra bema hanamoa.
english: She said to her mistress, “I wish that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.”

motu: Taunabunai, Naaman e raka vareai, ena lohia e hamaoroa, eto, Israel kekenina na unu ini e gwau tomamu.
english: Someone went in and told his lord, saying, “The girl who is from the land of Israel said this.”

motu: Bena Suria pavapavana eto, Vada aola, revareva ta baina siaia, Israel pavapavana ena. Taunabunai, ia na ela, silver talent * gwauta + 5:5 Talent gwauta = 500 kilograms sisivana. Sekele daha tauratoi = 98 kilograms sisivana. * bona gold * sekele daha tauratoi bona dabua ḡoeva-daedia gwauta e abi kau, e laohai.
english: The king of Syria said, “Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” He|strong="H3027" * departed|strong="H3212" *, and|strong="H3478" * took|strong="H3947" * with|strong="H3212" * him|strong="H7971" * ten|strong="H6235" * talents|strong="H3603" * + 5:5 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds * of|strong="H4428" * silver|strong="H3701" *, six|strong="H8337" * thousand pieces of|strong="H4428" * gold|strong="H2091" *, and|strong="H3478" * ten|strong="H6235" * changes|strong="H2487" * of|strong="H4428" * clothing.

motu: Israel pavapavana dekena e laohaia revarevana ai ini e torea toma: Ina revareva ba davaria negana ai ba diba, lau ese egu hesiai tauna Naaman vada na siaia vasi, ena lepra ba hanamoa totona.
english: He brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, “Now when this letter has come to you, behold, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, that you may heal him of his leprosy.”

motu: Israel pavapavana ese revareva e duahia, bena ena dabua e dare, eto, Lau na Dirava, bona taunimanima baina hamasedia bona baina hamauridia, a? Una dainai ina tau ese lepra tauna ta ihanamona herevana egu ai e siaia mai a? Mani a haeroa, a itaia, iheai-henigu dalana e tahuamu.
english: When the king of Israel had read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to heal a man of his leprosy? But please consider and see how he seeks a quarrel against me.”

motu: Elisaia, Dirava ena tau, e kamonai Israel pavapavana ese ena dabua vada e dare; bena ia ese hereva e siaia lao, hanua pavapavana enai, eto, Dahaka dainai emu dabua vada o dare? Ia na dekegu ainema, baine diba, peroveta tauna ta na Israel ai e nohomu.
english: It was so, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.”

motu: Taunabunai, Naaman na mai hosina bona mai kariotana ida ela, Elisaia ena ruma iduarana vairanai e gini.
english: So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariots, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.

motu: Bena Elisaia ese gwaukau tauna ta ia dekena e siaia lao, eto, Aola, Ioridane sinavaina ai ba digu nega hahitu, bena taumu baine namo lou, bona vada ba ḡoeva.
english: Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall come again to you, and you shall be clean.”

motu: A Naaman na e badu, e raka oho, eto, Lau banava nato ia korikorina ese baine mai henigu, bena baine gini, Iehova, ena Dirava, ladana baine hahanea bona hisi gabuna baine daroa, unu amo lepragu baine hanamoa nato.
english: But Naaman was angry, and went away and said, “Behold, I thought, ‘He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of Yahweh his God, and wave his hand over the place, and heal the leper.’

motu: Damasko sinavaina Abana bona Farapara, ese Israel sinavaidia iboudiai na asie hereadiamu a? Idia lalodiai basinama digu basinama ḡoeva diba a? Bena e raka muri, mai lalo-ḡaraḡarana ida e raka oho.
english: Aren’t Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Couldn’t I wash in them and be clean?” So he turned and went away in a rage.

motu: A iena hesiai taudia na e raka kahira, e hereva henia, eto, Tamagu e, peroveta tauna ese kara aukana ta bema haḡanilaimu, boma karaia ani? Matogana, ia e gwaumu “Ba digu bena ba ḡoeva” be edeheto?
english: His servants came near and spoke to him, and said, “My father, if the prophet had asked you do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much rather then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?”

motu: Taunabunai, ia na e diho ela, nega hitu Ioridane sinavaina ai e heuru utu, Dirava ena tau ena hereva heḡereḡerena. Bena tauna vada e namo lou, mero karukaruna heḡereḡerena ai ela; bena vada e ḡoeva.
english: Then went he down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

motu: Bena e lou lao, Dirava ena tau dekenai, ia bona ena orea idoinai. E kau, bena vairanai e gini, eto, Harihari lau dibagu tanobada idoinai latanai na asi Dirava ta, a Israel ai mo; taunabunai emu hesiai tauna ena amo herahia ḡauna mani avabia.
english: He returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him; and he said, “See now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel. Now therefore, please take a gift from your servant.”

motu: A Elisaia eto, Iehova, isiaina na lao henimu Diravana, e maurimu heḡereḡerena, ḡau ta basina abia. Bena e ha-uraia, baine abia, to se ura.
english: But he said, “As Yahweh lives, before whom I stand, I will receive none.” He|strong="H3068" * urged|strong="H6484" * him|strong="H6440" * to|strong="H3068" * take|strong="H3947" * it|strong="H6440" *; but|strong="H3947" * he|strong="H3068" * refused|strong="H3985" *.

motu: Bena Naaman eto, Bema lasi be lau na noimumu, emu hesiai tauna na tano taina ba henigu, doniki rua edia huahua heḡeregeredia; badina be harihari bainela emu hesiai tauna na ḡole-oho boubouna ḡauna eiava boubou ḡauna ta basina hahelaḡaia dirava ta ena, a Iehova mo ena.
english: Naaman said, “If not, then, please let two mules’ load of earth be given to your servant; for your servant will from now on offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods, but to Yahweh.

motu: Ina kara tamona ai Iehova ese emu hesiai tauna bema bogagu hisi: biagugu na toma-diho totona Rimon + 5:18 “Rimon” na Suria taudia edia dirava ta ladana. * ena dubu ai baine dae kau, bona lau imagu ai baine hetao kau, bena una negana ai lau ese Rirnon ena dubu ai baina igo diho, Iehova ese una kara ai baine bogagu hisi.
english: In this thing may Yahweh pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon. When I bow myself in the house of Rimmon, may Yahweh pardon your servant in this thing.”

motu: Elisaia ese e hamaoroa, eto, Mai mainomu ida aola. A Naaman na do se raka daudau ai,
english: He said to him, “Go in peace.” So he|strong="H3212" * departed|strong="H3212" * from|strong="H3212" * him a|strong="H3068" * little|strong="H3530" * way|strong="H3212" *.

motu: Gehasi, Dirava ena tau Elisaia ena hesiai tauna, eto, Ia, lau biagugu ese Naaman tau Suria, vada e bogaia hisi, e mailai gaudia na ia imana amo se abidia. Iehova e maurimu heḡereḡerena, lau na ia murina amo baina heau, ḡau ta iena amo baina abia.
english: But Gehazi the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, “Behold, my master has spared this Naaman the Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought. As Yahweh lives, I will run after him, and take something from him.”

motu: Taunabunai, Gehasi na Naaman murina amo ela. Naaman ese tau ta e itaia, murina amo e maimu, bena ena kariota amo e diho, ia ihedavari-henina totona; eto, Edeheto, namo eiava?
english: So Gehazi followed after Naaman. When Naaman saw one running after him, he came down from the chariot to meet him, and said, “Is all well?”

motu: Ia eto, Namo. Biagugu ese vada e siaigu, e tomu, Peroveta oreana tau-eregabedia rarua na ina harihari Efraim ororodia amo vada ema; bena e noimumu, silver talent * ta + 5:22 Silver talent ta = 50 kilograms sisivana. * bona dabua herea-daedia rua ba henidia.
english: He said, “All is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Behold, even now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent + 5:22 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds * of silver and two changes of clothing.’”

motu: Naaman eto, Mani emu kara talent * rua bavabi. Bena ia ese e ha-uraia, bena silver talent * rua na puse rua ai e uda, bona dabua herea-daedia rua danu; bena puse na ena hesiai taudia rarua e hahualaidia; bena raruosi ese e hua, Gehasi vairanai.
english: Naaman said, “Be pleased to take two talents.” He urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and laid them on two of his servants; and they carried them before him.

motu: Ororo ai e kau, bena ia ese idia imadia amo e abidia, ruma ai e atodia; e siaidia, bena e raka oho.
english: When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand, and stored them in the house. Then he let the men go, and they departed.

motu: Ia na e raka vareai, biaguna vairanai e gini. Bena Elisaia ese e nanadaia, eto, Gehasi e, ede ola? Ia eto, Emu hesiai tauna na gabu ta asinala.
english: But he went in, and stood before his master. Elisha said to him, “Where did you come from, Gehazi?” He|strong="H1931" * said, “ Your|strong="H3808" * servant|strong="H5650" * went|strong="H1980" * nowhere|strong="H3808" *.”

motu: A ia ese e gwau henia, eto, Lauma ai oi ida asita lao hebou, una tau na ena kariota amo e hegiro oi ihedavari-henimu totona negana ai a? Una na moni bona dabua, eiava olive bona vine imeadia, eiava mamoe bona boromakau, eiava hesiai taudia bona hahinedia, iabidia negana buna a?
english: He said to him, “Didn’t my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and olive groves and vineyards, and sheep and cattle, and male servants and female servants?

motu: Taunabunai, Naaman ena lepra na oiemu ai baine kau, bona oi garamu ediai danu, ela bona hanaihanai. Taunabunai, ia na ia vairana amo e raka lasi mai leprana; kopina e kuroka-kuroka danu, snow * na heto.
english: Therefore the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and to your offspring + 5:27 or, seed * forever.” He|strong="H6440" * went|strong="H3318" * out|strong="H3318" * from|strong="H3318" * his|strong="H6440" * presence|strong="H6440" * a|strong="H3068" * leper|strong="H6879" *, as|strong="H3318" * white as|strong="H3318" * snow|strong="H7950" *.

motu: Peroveta oreana taudia ese Elisaia e hamaoroa, eto, A itaia, emu hereḡu henunai a nohomu gabuna na maraḡi herea.
english: The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “See now, the place where we live and meet with you is too small for us.

motu: Mani Ioridane sinavaina aiala, ta ta au ta ta baia abi, bena emai noho gabuna ta baia karaia unuseni ai. Ia na e haere, eto, Aola.
english: Please let us go to the Jordan, and each man take a beam from there, and let’s make us a place there, where we may live.” He|strong="H5704" * answered, “ Go|strong="H3212" *!”

motu: Bena idia ta eto, Mani emu kara oi danu emu hesiai taudia ida baitala. Ia na e haere, eto, Baitala.
english: One said, “Please be pleased to go with your servants.” He|strong="H3212" * answered, “ I|strong="H5650" * will|strong="H5650" * go|strong="H3212" *.”

motu: Taunabunai ia na idia ida ela. Ioridane ai e kau, bena idia ese au haida e hagaridia.
english: So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they cut down wood.

motu: Bena tau ta ese au ta e hagaria negana ai na ena ira kwarana na ranu ai e moru. Bena e boi lolo, eto, Biagugu e, ihabaigu, na abia torehai.
english: But as one was cutting down a tree, the ax head fell into the water. Then he cried out and said, “Alas, my master! For it was borrowed.”

motu: Dirava ena tau eto, Edeseni ai e moru? Ia ese gabu na e haheitalaia; bena Elisaia ese auau ta e utua, una gabu ai e tahoa dobi, bena auri na e hakenia dae.
english: The man of God asked, “Where did it fall?” He showed him the place. He cut down a stick, threw it in there, and made the iron float.

motu: Ia eto, Avabia isi, Taunabunai, ia na e dau lao, e abia. Elisaia ese Suria taudia imadia amo e roho mauri
english: He said, “Take it.” So he put out his hand and took it.

motu: Nega ta, Suria pavapavana ese Israel e tuari heniava negana ai, ia na ena hesiai taudia ida e henega bou, gabu ta ladana e hatoa, eto, Una gabu ai baina taruha.
english: Now the king of Syria was at war against Israel; and he took counsel with his servants, saying, “My camp will be in such and such a place.”

motu: A Dirava ena tau ese hereva na Israel pavapavana dekena e siaia lao, eto, Una gabu na basio rakaia hanai, badina be Suria taudia na unu a be laomu.
english: The man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, “Beware that you not pass this place, for the Syrians are coming down there.”

motu: Bena Israel pavapavana ese haida e siaidia lao, Dirava ena tau ese e hamaorolaia gabuna baela. Unuhetomana ia ese vaevae e sisiba heniava, bena e roho mauri, dia nega tamona eiava nega rua hona.
english: The king of Israel sent to the place which the man of God told him and warned him of; and he saved himself there, not once or twice.

motu: Suria pavapavana lalona e hekwarahiva ina ḡau dainai, bena ia ese ena hesiai taudia e boiridia, e gwau henidia, eto, Basio hamaorogu ita bogaragidai daika ese Israel pavapavana e duruamu a?
english: The king of Syria’s heart was very troubled about this. He called his servants, and said to them, “Won’t you show me which of us is for the king of Israel?”

motu: Bena ena hesiai taudia ta eto, Egu lohia bona egu pavapava e, ta lasi; to Elisaia, peroveta tauna Israel ai e nohomu, ia ese emu mahuta daiutuna lalonai o gwauraimu herevadia na Israel pavapavana e hamaorolaiamu.
english: One of his servants said, “No, my lord, O king; but Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom.”

motu: Ia eto, Aola, ba itaia ia be edeseni ai; bena haida na ia idabai-taona baina siaidia lao. Haida ese e hamaoroa, eto, A kamonai, tauna na Dotan ai.
english: He said, “Go and see where he is, that I may send and get him.” He|strong="H1931" * was|strong="H1931" * told|strong="H5046" *, “ Behold|strong="H2009" *, he|strong="H1931" * is|strong="H1931" * in|strong="H3212" * Dothan|strong="H1886" *.”

motu: Taunabunai, ia ese hosi bona kariota bona tuari oreana badana ta e siaidia. Idia na hanuaboi ai ela, hanua e koua heḡeḡe.
english: Therefore he sent horses, chariots, and a great army there. They came by night and surrounded the city.

motu: Dirava ena tau ena hesiai tauna na daba matana ai e tore isi, e raka lasi, e itaia, tuari oreana ta mai hosidia bona mai kariotadia ida, ese hanua vada e koua heḡeḡe. Hesiai tauna eto, Biagugu e, madi ihabaida! Ede baita kara toma?
english: When the servant of the man of God had risen early and gone out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was around the city. His servant said to him, “Alas, my master! What shall we do?”

motu: Elisaia eto, Basio gari; badina be ita e bamodamu taudia na hutuma, a idia e bamodiamu taudia na dia hoho.
english: He answered, “Don’t be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”

motu: Bena Elisaia e ḡuriḡuri, eto, Iehova e, na noimumu, ia matana a hapapa, baine itaia helaoreana. Taunabunai, Iehova ese una eregabe tauna matana e hapapadia, bena e itaia, ororo na lahi hosidia bona kariotadia ai e honu, idia ese Elisaia e ḡeḡea ahu.
english: Elisha prayed, and said, “Yahweh, please open his eyes, that he may see.” Yahweh opened the young man’s eyes, and he saw; and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.

motu: Bena Suria taudia na ia iabina totona e hekei diho negana ai, Elisaia ese Iehova e ḡuria, eto, Na noimumu, ina orea na matadia a huari kepulu. Taunabunai ia ese matadia e huari kepulu, Elisaia ena ḡuriḡuri heḡereḡerena.
english: When they came down to him, Elisha prayed to Yahweh, and said, “Please strike this people with blindness.” He|strong="H3068" * struck|strong="H5221" * them|strong="H5221" * with|strong="H3068" * blindness|strong="H5575" * according to|strong="H3381" * Elisha’s word|strong="H1697" *.

motu: Bena Elisaia ese e hereva henidia, eto, Dalana na dia inai, bona hanuana na dia inai; murigu amo a raka, bena baina hakaumui lao, o tahuamu tauna dekenai. Bena ia ese e hakaudia lao, ela bona Samaria.
english: Elisha said to them, “This is not the way, neither is this the city. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom you seek.” He led them to Samaria.

motu: Samaria ai e raka vareai, bena maoromaoro Elisaia eto, Iehova e, ini taunimanima matadia ba hapapadia, do bae ita. Taunabunai Iehova ese idia matadia e hapapadia, bena e itaia, idia na Samaria bogaraginai.
english: When they had come into Samaria, Elisha said, “Yahweh, open these men’s eyes, that they may see.” Yahweh|strong="H3068" * opened|strong="H6491" * their|strong="H3068" * eyes|strong="H5869" *, and|strong="H3068" * they|strong="H3068" * saw|strong="H7200" *; and|strong="H3068" * behold|strong="H2009" *, they|strong="H3068" * were|strong="H1961" * in|strong="H3068" * the|strong="H7200" * middle|strong="H8432" * of|strong="H3068" * Samaria|strong="H8111" *.

motu: Israel pavapavana ese e itadia, bena ia ese Elisaia e hamaoroa, eto, Tamagu e, aina aladia mase eiava?
english: The king of Israel said to Elisha, when he saw them, “My father, shall I strike them? Shall I strike them?”

motu: Ia na e haere, eto, Basio aladia mase. Emu dare bona emu peva amo boma abidia mauri taudia na boma aladia mase a? Aniani bona ranu na vairadiai ba dabara, bae aniani bona ranu bae inu, bena biagudia dekena baela.
english: He answered, “You shall not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, then go to their master.”

motu: Taunabunai, ia ese aria badana e dabaraia adia; bena e aniani bona e inuinu vaitani murinai ia ese e siaidia, bena biagudia dekena ela. Suria taudia ese Israel tanona asie daea lou. Samaria e koua heḡeḡe
english: He prepared a great feast for them. After they ate and drank, he sent them away and they went to their master. So the bands of Syria stopped raiding the land of Israel.

motu: Una murinai Ben-hadad, Suna pavapavana, ese ena tuari oreana idoinai e haboua, e dae ela, Samaria e koua heḡeḡe.
english: After this, Benhadad king of Syria gathered all his army, and went up and besieged Samaria.

motu: Bena doe bada e vara Samaria ai, vada e koua heḡeḡe dainai; ela bona doniki kwarana ta e hoia, davana na silver * sekeledia taurahani-ahui, + 6:25 “Sekele taurahani-ahui”. Readia K20 heḡereḡerena, ita eda moni ai. “Sekele ima”. Readia K1.25 heḡereḡerena, ita eda moni ai. * bona pune taḡena kebere ta davana na silver * sekeledia ima.
english: There was a great famine in Samaria. Behold, they besieged it until a donkey’s head was sold for eighty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a kab + 6:25 A kab was about 2 liters, so a fourth of a kab would be about 500 milliliters or about a pint * of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.

motu: Nega ta Israel pavapavana na magu latana amo e raka hanaiva ai, hahine ta ese e boi henia, eto, Egu lohia bona egu pavapava, a durugu.
english: As the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried to him, saying, “Help, my lord, O king!”

motu: Ia eto, Bema Iehova ese basine durumu, lau na ede amo baina durumu? Uit ikwadilaina gabuna amo eiava vine itaolaina gabuna amo a?
english: He said, “If Yahweh doesn’t help you, where could I get help for you? From the threshing floor, or from the wine press?”

motu: Bena hanua pavapavana ese hahine na e nanadaia, eto, Emu hekwakwanai be dahaka? Hahine na e haere, eto, Ina hahine ese e hamaorogu, eto “Natumu a heni, hari dina ai baita ania, bena kerukeru lau natugu baita ania”.
english: Then the king asked her, “What is your problem?” She|strong="H2063" * answered, “ This|strong="H2063" * woman said to|strong="H5414" * me|strong="H5414" *, ‘ Give|strong="H5414" * your|strong="H5414" * son|strong="H1121" *, that|strong="H3117" * we|strong="H3068" * may|strong="H4428" * eat him|strong="H5414" * today|strong="H3117" *, and|strong="H1121" * we|strong="H3068" * will|strong="H4428" * eat my|strong="H5414" * son|strong="H1121" * tomorrow|strong="H4279" *.’

motu: Taunabunai, lau natugu a nadua, bena a ania. Daba-rerena ai lau ese na hamaoroa, nato “Natumu a heni, baita ania”; a ia ese natuna e hunia.
english: So we boiled my son and ate him; and I said to her on the next day, ‘Give up your son, that we may eat him;’ and she has hidden her son.”

motu: Hanua pavapavana ese hahine ena hereva e kamonai; bena maḡu latana amo rakana ai ia ese ena dabua e dare; bena taunimanima ese e itaia, ena dabua henunai na puse dabuana vada e hahedokilai.
english: When the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes. Now he was passing by on the wall, and the people looked, and behold, he had sackcloth underneath on his body.

motu: Bena ia eto, Hari dina ai Elisaia Safata kwarana na pagana ai bema mia, Dirava ese bema hadikagu, bona ma bema hadikagu bada.
english: Then he said, “God do so to me, and more also, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat stays on him today.”

motu: Elisaia na ena ruma ai e helaiva, bona tau-badadia na ia ida hehelai. Hanua pavapavana ese tau ta ia vairana amo vada e siaia lao; a hari gwaukau tauna do se kau ai, Elisaia ese unu tau-badadia e hamaorodia, eto, O itaiamu, una roroma tauna vada e hesiai, lau kwaragu iabi-ohona totona. Gwaukau tauna bainema negana ai, iduara na ba koua kunuka-kunuka, ia ba laoa ahu. Biaguna aena regedia na ia murina amo se maimu a?
english: But Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. Then the king sent a man from before him; but before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, “Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? Behold, when the messenger comes, shut the door, and hold the door shut against him. Isn’t the sound of his master’s feet behind him?”

motu: Dounu e hereva henidiava ai, hanua pavapavana na ia dekenai e kau, eto, Ina hehvarahi na Iehova ena amo. Iehova ma baina naria anina be dahaka?
english: While he was still talking with them, behold, the messenger came down to him. Then he said, “Behold, this evil is from Yahweh. Why should I wait for Yahweh any longer?”

motu: A Elisaia eto, Iehova ena hereva a kamonaia. Iehova na ini e gwau tomamu: Kerukeru, hari ina hora sisivana, flaoa namo-hereana bosea ta eiava bali bosea rua na Samaria ikoukouna ai bae hoi, davadia na sekele tamona. + 7:1 “Sekele tamona”. Readia 25 toea heḡereḡerena, ita eda moni ai. *
english: Elisha said, “Hear Yahweh’s word. Yahweh says, ‘Tomorrow about this time a seah + 7:1 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks * of fine flour will be sold for a shekel, + 7:1 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces. In this context, it was probably a silver coin weighing that much. * and two seahs of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.’”

motu: Bena tuari biaguna, imana ai hanua pavapavana e hetao kau tauna, ese Dirava ena tau e hamaoroa, eto, Iehova sibona ese gaba-mauru bema kara guba ai, ina kara bema vara diba a? A Elisaia eto, Oi sibomu matamu amo ba itaia, to basio ania.
english: Then the captain on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God, and said, “Behold, if Yahweh made windows in heaven, could this thing be?” He|strong="H8033" * said|strong="H1697" *, “ Behold|strong="H2009" *, you|strong="H5921" * will|strong="H3068" * see|strong="H7200" * it|strong="H5921" * with|strong="H3068" * your|strong="H3068" * eyes|strong="H5869" *, but|strong="H3808" * will|strong="H3068" * not|strong="H3808" * eat of|strong="H4428" * it|strong="H5921" *.”

motu: Lepra taudia hahani na hanua ikoukouna ai nonoho, bena e hereva heheni, eto, Iniseni ai ta helaimu ela bona baita mase anina be dahaka?
english: Now there were four leprous men at the entrance of the gate. They said to one another, “Why do we sit here until we die?

motu: Bema baitato “Hanua lalonai aita raka vareai”, to doe na hanua lalonai, bena unuseni ai baita mase; a iniseni ai baitama helai danu baita mase. Benaini, Suria taudia edia taruha aitala; idia ese bema hamaurida, baita noho; eiava bema alada, baita mase mo.
english: If we say, ‘We will enter into the city,’ then the famine is in the city, and we will die there. If we sit still here, we also die. Now therefore come, and let’s surrender to the army of the Syrians. If they save us alive, we will live; and if they kill us, we will only die.”

motu: Taunabunai, dina kerekerena ai e tore isi, taruha bae lao henia totona; a Suria taudia edia taruha isena ai e kau negana ai, tau ta asie davaria unuseni ai.
english: They rose up in the twilight to go to the camp of the Syrians. When they had come to the outermost part of the camp of the Syrians, behold, no man was there.

motu: Badina be Ḡaubada ese kariota bona hosi bona tuari oreana badana reḡedia e havara Suria taudia taiadia ai; taunabunai idia ese e hereva heheni, eto, A kamonai, Israel pavapavana ese Hiti taudia edia pavapava bona Aigupto pavapavadia vada e vatudia, bae tuari henida totona.
english: For the Lord + 7:6 The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” * had made the army of the Syrians to hear the sound of chariots and the sound of horses, even the noise of a great army; and they said to one another, “Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of the Egyptians to attack us.”

motu: Taunabunai, idia na dina kerekerena ai e heau oho, edia kalaga, edia hosi, edia doniki e rakatanidia, taruha lalona ḡaudia miadia ai e laputani, mauridia e tahu.
english: Therefore they arose and fled in the twilight, and left their tents, their horses, and their donkeys, even the camp as it was, and fled for their life.

motu: Hari lepra taudia na taruha isena ai e kau, bena kalaga ta ai e raka vareai, e aniani, e inuinu, bena silver * bona gold * bona dabua e hua lao, e hunidia. Bena e lou lao, ma kalaga ta ai e raka vareai, ḡau haida ma e hua lao, e hunidia.
english: When these lepers came to the outermost part of the camp, they went into one tent, and ate and drank, then carried away silver, gold, and clothing and went and hid it. Then they came back, and entered into another tent and carried things from there also, and went and hid them.

motu: Bena idia na e hereva heheni, eto, Ita na asita kara maoromu. Ina dina na hari namona dinana; bema basita herevalaia, baita noho hedavauhe ela bona daba, na mata-hakanina ese baine lasida tao. Taunabunai aitala, hanua pavapavana ena ruma taudia baita hamaorodia.
english: Then they said to one another, “We aren’t doing right. Today is a day of good news, and we keep silent. If we wait until the morning light, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore come, let’s go and tell the king’s household.”

motu: Taunabunai, idia na hanua ela, hanua ikoukoudia igimadia taudia e boi henidia, e hamaorodia, eto, Suria taudia edia taruha ala, unuseni ai tau ta asia itaia bona ere ta asia kamonai, a hosi bona doniki mo hehemata, bona kalaga mai ḡaudia ida mo mimia.
english: So they came and called to the city gatekeepers; and they told them, “We came to the camp of the Syrians, and, behold, there was no man there, not even a man’s voice, but the horses tied, and the donkeys tied, and the tents as they were.”

motu: Bena ikoukou igimadia taudia e boi lao, hanua pavapavana ena ruma taudia ediai e hehari piu.
english: Then the gatekeepers called out and told it to the king’s household within.

motu: Bena hanua pavapavana na hanuaboi ai e tore isi, ena hesiai taudia e hamaorodia, eto, Aina hamaoromui, Suria taudia ese ita ihadikada dalana na ede e hegaeḡaelaia toma. Dibadia ita na e hitolodamu; taunabunai idia na taruha vada e rakalania, tano paka ai e komumu, e tomamu “Hanua amo bae raka lasi negana ai baita abidia mauri, bona hanua lalonai baita didi vareai”.
english: The king arose in the night, and said to his servants, “I will now show you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are hungry. Therefore they have gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, ‘When they come out of the city, we shall take them alive, and get into the city.’”

motu: Bena ena hesiai tauna ta eto, Mani emu kara tatau haida a siaidia, doini mimia hosidia ima bae abidia, badina be dibada doini iniseni ai e nohomu taudia na Israel hutuma vada e mase taudia heḡereḡeredia ai baela. Mani aita siaidia, bae itaia.
english: One of his servants answered, “Please let some people take five of the horses that remain, which are left in the city. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are left in it. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are consumed. Let’s send and see.”

motu: Taunabunai, hosi-gui taudia rarua e abidia; bena hanua pavapavana ese e siaidia, Suria taudia edia tuari oreana murina amo baela. Ia na eto, Aola, a ha itadia.
english: Therefore they took two chariots with horses; and the king sent them out to the Syrian army, saying, “Go and see.”

motu: Taunabunai raruosi na idia muridia amo ela, ela bona Ioridane sinavaina; bena e itaia, dala idoinai dabua bona kohu e hepetapetalai, Suria taudia ese heaudia ai e nege ḡaudia. Bena e siaidia taudia na e lou, hanua pavapavana e hamaorolaia.
english: They went after them to the Jordan; and behold, all the path was full of garments and equipment which the Syrians had cast away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.

motu: Bena hanua taudia na e raka lasi, Suria taudia edia taruha ela, edia kohu e abi ore. Taunabunai, flaoa namo-hereana bosea ta e hoia, davana na sekele tamona, bona bali bosea rua danu e hoi, davana na sekele tamona, Iehova ena hereva heḡereḡerena.
english: The people went out and plundered the camp of the Syrians. So a seah + 7:16 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks * of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, + 7:16 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces. In this context, it was probably a silver coin weighing that much. * according to Yahweh’s word.

motu: Hanua pavapavana ese tuari biaguna, imana ai e hetao kau tauna, na vada e siaia, ikoukou baine naria; bena hanua taudia ese e moia taotao, ikoukou raka-lasina ai; bena ia na e mase, Dirava ena tau ena hereva, hanua pavapavana ia dekena ela negana ai e gwauraia herevana, heḡereḡerena.
english: The king had appointed the captain on whose hand he leaned to be in charge of the gate; and the people trampled over him in the gate, and he died as the man of God had said, who spoke when the king came down to him.

motu: Badina be Dirava ena tau ese hanua pavapavana e hamaoroa, eto “Kerukeru, hari ina hora sisivana, bali bosea rua eiava flaoa namo-hereana bosea ta na Samaria ikoukouna ai bae hoi, davadia na sekele tamona” negana ai
english: It happened as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, “Two seahs + 7:18 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks * of barley for a shekel, + 7:18 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces. In this context, it was probably a silver coin weighing that much. * and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, shall be tomorrow about this time in the gate of Samaria;”

motu: hari tuari biaguna ese Dirava ena tau e haere henia, eto “Iehova sibona ese gaba-mauru bema kara guba ai, ina kara bema vara diba a?”. Una negana ai Dirava ena tau eto “Oi sibomu matamu amo ba itaia, to basio ania”.
english: and that captain answered the man of God, and said, “Now, behold, if Yahweh made windows in heaven, might such a thing be?” and he said, “Behold, you will see it with your eyes, but will not eat of it.”

motu: Benaini, unu e vara toma ienai, badina be hanua taudia ese ikoukou raka-lasina ai e moia taotao, bena e
english: It happened like that to him, for the people trampled over him in the gate, and he died.

motu: Elisaia ese natuna e hamauria lou hahinena na vada e hamaoroa, eto, A tore isi, emu ruma taudia ida aola, ba noholaia diba gabuna ta ai vada ba noho; badina be Iehova ese doe vada e gwauraia, bena ina tano na baine doe ela bona laḡani hitu.
english: Now Elisha had spoken to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Arise, and go, you and your household, and stay for a while wherever you can; for Yahweh has called for a famine. It will also come on the land for seven years.”

motu: Taunabunai, una hahine na e tore isi, Dirava ena tau ena hereva heḡereḡerena e karaia; ia na ela, ena ruma taudia ida, Filistia taudia edia tano ai e nohova, laḡani hitu.
english: The woman arose, and did according to the man of God’s word. She went with her household, and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.

motu: Laḡani hitu e ore ai, hahine na Filistia taudia edia tano amo e lou lao, bena ia na hanua pavapavana dekena ela, baine noia totona; ena ruma bona ena tano iabi-loudia herevadia baine gwaurai.
english: At the end of seven years, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines. Then she went out to beg the king for her house and for her land.

motu: Una negana ai hanua pavapavana na Gehasi, Dirava ena tau ena hesiai tauna, ida e hereva-herevava ai, hanua pavapavana na eto, Elisaia ena kara badadia iboudiai sivaraidia ba hamaorolaigu.
english: Now the king was talking with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please tell me all the great things that Elisha has done.”

motu: Hari tau ese hanua pavapavana na Elisaia mase merona e hamauria sivaraina e hamaorolaiava lalonai, hari natuna e hamauria lou hahinena ese hanua pavapavana e noia, ena ruma bona ena tano herevadia e gwaurai. Bena Gehasi eto, Pavapava e, egu lohia, hari hahinena binai, bona natuna danu, Elisaia ese e hamauria lou merona.
english: As he was telling the king how he had restored to life him who was dead, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life begged the king for her house and for her land. Gehazi said, “My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.”

motu: Hanua pavapavana ese hahine na e nanadaia, bena ia ese sivarai ma e gwauraia. Taunabunai, hanua pavapavana ese ena ḡaukara itataona tauna ta e haḡania, eto, Ena ḡau iboudiai ba henia lou, bona uma anidia iboudiai danu, e raka oho dinana amo ema bona hari. Hasaele ese Suria e lohiaia matama
english: When the king asked the woman, she told him. So the king appointed to her a certain officer, saying, “Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.”

motu: Elisaia na Damasko ai e kau. Una negana ai Ben-hadad, Suria pavapavana, na e gorerea. Bena haida ese e hamaoroa, eto, Dirava ena tau vada ema.
english: Elisha came to Damascus; and Benhadad the king of Syria was sick. He was told, “The man of God has come here.”

motu: Bena hanua pavapavana ese Hasaele e hamaoroa, eto, Herahia ḡauna avabia kau, baola, Dirava ena tau ida ba hedavari; bena iena amo Iehova ba nanadaia, ina gorere amo baina mauri lou eiava?
english: The king said to Hazael, “Take a present in your hand, and go meet the man of God, and inquire of Yahweh by him, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”

motu: Taunabunai, Hasaele na ia ihedavari-henina totona ela, herahia e laohai, Damasko kohudia idau-idau, kamelo hari-ahui edia huahua. Ia na ela, vairanai e gini, eto, Natumu Ben-hadad, Suria pavapavana, ese vada e siaigu dekemu ai, e tomu “Ina gorere amo baina mauri lou eiava?”
english: So Hazael went to meet him and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him and said, “Your son Benhadad king of Syria has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”

motu: Elisaia ese e haere henia, eto, Aola, ba hamaoroa, baoto “Momokani, vada ba mauri lou”; ḡau tamona, Iehova ese vada e haheitalaigu, momokani ia na baine mase.
english: Elisha said to him, “Go, tell him, ‘You will surely recover;’ however Yahweh has shown me that he will surely die.”

motu: Bena e raraia tao ela bona e hemarai. Bena Dirava ena tau e tai.
english: He settled his gaze steadfastly on him, until he was ashamed. Then the man of God wept.

motu: Bena Hasaele eto, Egu lohia e, dahaka dainai o taimu? Ia na e haere, eto, Badina be Israel taudia ede ba hadikadia toma na vada dibagu: edia kohoro ba doudia, edia eregabe taudia na dare amo bavaladia mase, natudia maraḡidia ba huaridia, bona edia rogorogo hahinedia ba dapadia.
english: Hazael said, “Why do you weep, my lord?” He|strong="H3588" * answered, “ Because|strong="H3588" * I|strong="H3588" * know|strong="H3045" * the|strong="H3588" * evil|strong="H7451" * that|strong="H3588" * you|strong="H3588" * will|strong="H3478" * do|strong="H6213" * to|strong="H3478" * the|strong="H3588" * children|strong="H1121" * of|strong="H1121" * Israel|strong="H3478" *. You|strong="H3588" * will|strong="H3478" * set|strong="H7971" * their|strong="H3588" * strongholds|strong="H4013" * on|strong="H7971" * fire, and|strong="H1121" * you|strong="H3588" * will|strong="H3478" * kill|strong="H2026" * their|strong="H3588" * young|strong="H1121" * men|strong="H1121" * with|strong="H6213" * the|strong="H3588" * sword|strong="H2719" *, and|strong="H1121" * will|strong="H3478" * dash|strong="H7376" * their|strong="H3588" * little|strong="H5768" * ones|strong="H5768" * in|strong="H3478" * pieces|strong="H7376" *, and|strong="H1121" * rip|strong="H1234" * up|strong="H1234" * their|strong="H3588" * pregnant|strong="H2030" * women|strong="H2030" *.”

motu: Bena Hasaele eto, Emu hesiai tauna be daika, ia na una kara badana baine karaia? Ia na sisia mo. Elisaia na e haere, eto, Iehova ese vada e haheitalaigu, oi na Suria pavapavana ai baola.
english: Hazael said, “But what is your servant, who is but a dog, that he could do this great thing?” Elisha answered|strong="H1697" *, “ Yahweh|strong="H3068" * has|strong="H3068" * shown|strong="H7200" * me|strong="H7200" * that|strong="H3588" * you|strong="H3588" * will|strong="H3068" * be|strong="H1697" * king|strong="H4428" * over|strong="H5921" * Syria.”

motu: Bena una tau ese Elisaia e rakatania, biaguna dekena e lou lao; bena biaguna ese e nanadaia, eto, Elisaia be dahaka eto? Ia na e haere, eto, E hamaorogu, oi na momokani ba mauri lou.
english: Then he departed from Elisha, and came to his master, who said to him, “What did Elisha say to you?” He|strong="H3212" * answered, “ He|strong="H3212" * told me|strong="H2421" * that|strong="H3212" * you|strong="H4100" * would|strong="H2421" * surely|strong="H2421" * recover|strong="H2421" *.”

motu: A daba ai ia ese hetaru ḡauna e abia, ranu ai e urua diho; bena hanua pavapavana vairana e ḡovalaia ela bona e mase. Bena Hasaele na ia gabuna ai e lohia. Iehoram ese Iuda e lohiaia
english: On the next day, he took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it on the king’s face, so that he died. Then Hazael reigned in his place.

motu: Ioram Ahaba, Israel pavapavana, ena lohia laḡanina iha-imana ai, Iehoram, Iuda pavapavana Iehosafat natuna, na e lohia matama.
english: In the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being king of Judah then, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign.

motu: E lohia matama negana ai, ena mauri laḡanidia na toi-ahui rua; ia na Ierusalem ai e lohia, laḡani taurahani.
english: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign. He reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

motu: Ia na Israel pavapavadia edia dala ai e rakava, Ahaba ena iduhu taudia e karava heḡereḡerena, badina be adavana na Ahaba natuna hahinena. Ia na Iehova vairanai e kara dikava.
english: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did Ahab’s house, for he married Ahab’s daughter. He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight.

motu: Ḡau tamona, Iehova ese Iuda na se habuaia tari, ena hesiai tauna David dainai, badina be vada e gwau hamata, lamepa ta ia baine henia bona ia garana baine henidia ela bona hanaihanai.
english: However, Yahweh would not destroy Judah, for David his servant’s sake, as he promised him to give to him a lamp for his children always.

motu: Iena nega ai Edom ese Iuda ena helohia e dadaraia, sibodia edia pavapava ta e haginia.
english: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.

motu: Bena Ioram e hanai, mai ena kariota iboudiai ida, Sairi kahana ela. Bena hanuaboi ai e tore isi; bena ia bona ena kariota biagudia ese Edom oreana, ia e daia heḡeḡe taudia, na e rahudia mase. A ena tuari taudia na e heau, edia hanua ela.
english: Then Joram crossed over to Zair, and all his chariots with him; and he rose up by night and struck the Edomites who surrounded him with the captains of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents.

motu: Taunabunai Edom ese Iuda ena helohia e dadaraiamu ema bona ina dina. Libna ese danu una nega tamona ai e dadaraia.
english: So Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time.

motu: Ioram ena kara orena, e kara karadia iboudiai, na Iuda Pavapavadia Sisigadia Bukana ai vada eme hetore, ani?
english: The rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

motu: Bena Ioram na tubu tama dekediai e mahuta, senena ida e guridia hebou, David ena hanua ai. Bena ia natuna Ahasia ese ia gabuna ai e lohia. Ahasia ese Iuda e lohiaia
english: Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in David’s city; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

motu: loram Ahaba, Israel pavapavana, ena lohia laḡanina ihagwauta-ruana ai, Ahasia, Iuda pavapavana Iehoram natuna, na e lohia matama.
english: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.

motu: E lohia matama negana ai, Ahasia ena mauri laḡanidia na ruahui rua; ia na laḡani tamona Ierusalem ai e lohia. Sinana ladana na Atalia, Omri, Israel pavapavana, tubuna.
english: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri king of Israel.

motu: Ia danu Ahaba ena iduhu edia dala ai e rakava, bona Iehova vairanai e kara dikava, Ahaba ena iduhu taudia e karava heḡereḡerena; badina be ia na Ahaba iduhuna ravadia.
english: He walked in the way of Ahab’s house and did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as did Ahab’s house, for he was the son-in-law of Ahab’s house.

motu: Ia na Ioram Ahaba ida ela, Hasaele, Suria pavapavana, e tuari henia, Ramoto-gilead ai; unuseni ai Suria taudia ese Ioram e haberoa.
english: He went with Joram the son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians wounded Joram.

motu: Bena King Ioram na e lou ela, Iesrele ai ena bero bae namo totona. Unu bero be Suria taudia edia amo e davaridia Rama ai, ia ese Hasaele, Suria pavapavana, e tuari henia negana ai. Bena Ahasia Iehoram, Iuda pavapavana, na Iesrele ela, Ioram Ahaba baine igoa ita totona, badina be ia na e gorereava.
english: King Joram returned to be healed in Jezreel from the wounds which the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. Ahaziah the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.

motu: Bena peroveta tauna Elisaia ese peroveta oreana tauna ta e boiria, e hamaoroa, eto, Emu rami ba hekasilaia, ina dehoro kavabuna na imamu ai bavabia, Ramoto-gilead baola.
english: Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets, and said to him, “Put your belt on your waist, take this vial of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth Gilead.

motu: Ba kau negana ai, Iehu, Iehosafat Nimisi natuna, ba tahua. Ba raka vareai, ba hamaoroa, ia na bamona bogaragidia amo baine tore isi; bena laloma daiutuna lalonai ba hakaua vareai.
english: When you come there, find Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in and make him rise up from among his brothers, and take him to an inner room.

motu: Bena dehoro kavabuna bavabia, dehoro na ia kwarana ai ba bubua, baoto “Iehova na ini e gwau tomamu: lau ese na horomumu, Israel pavapavana”. Bena iduara ba kehoa, ba heau; basio halahe.
